requirements.lead_text: Practical Application. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Practical Application. Do ONE of the following: (a) With your counselor's approval, choose an artificial intelligence project based on your personal interest or a community need. Develop a plan outlining the project's objectives, data requirements, and potential ethical considerations. Implement the project utilizing appropriate artificial intelligence tools, languages, or platforms. Share your project with your counselor. Discuss the steps you followed to create the project and your experience during the process. (b) With your counselor's approval, design a short lesson plan on AI and teach it to your patrol or a group of Scouts. The lesson should include an AI-generated age-appropriate explanation of AI, examples of how AI is used in both everyday life as well as in the workplace, and an interactive demonstration of how Scouts could utilize AI to assist them with a school assignment, Scouting activity, or rank advancement. Share information on the development process and teaching experience with your counselor.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When evaluating how a machine learning model makes predictions in Artificial Intelligence Requirement 1, why can an AI system produce biased or inaccurate outputs even when its software code has no syntax errors?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When evaluating how a machine learning model makes predictions in Artificial Intelligence Requirement 1, why can an AI system produce biased or inaccurate outputs even when its software code has no syntax errors?
options: A. Because machine learning algorithms physically wear out their silicon transistors after processing more than a thousand queries.
B. Because AI models never use training data and instead generate answers using purely random voltage fluctuations.
C. Because computer processors automatically rewrite their own operating systems to ignore human instructions after compilation.

D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
choices: A. Because machine learning algorithms physically wear out their silicon transistors after processing more than a thousand queries.
B. Because AI models never use training data and instead generate answers using purely random voltage fluctuations.
C. Because computer processors automatically rewrite their own operating systems to ignore human instructions after compilation.

D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): AI and machine learning systems infer patterns directly from training data sets; if the training data contains gaps or historical biases, the resulting model outputs will reflect those flaws, requiring human verification.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: During the 'AI or Not?' game with your counselor, which of the following everyday scenarios actually utilizes artificial intelligence?
options: A. A digital kitchen timer beeping when sixty seconds have elapsed
B. A smartphone camera recognizing a user's face under different lighting angles to unlock the screen
C. An automatic sliding grocery store door opening when a motion sensor beam is broken
D. A word processor alphabetizing a list of Scout names from A to Z
choices: A. A digital kitchen timer beeping when sixty seconds have elapsed
B. A smartphone camera recognizing a user's face under different lighting angles to unlock the screen
C. An automatic sliding grocery store door opening when a motion sensor beam is broken
D. A word processor alphabetizing a list of Scout names from A to Z
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. A smartphone camera recognizing a user's face under different lighting angles to unlock the screen
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Facial recognition uses trained machine learning models to identify features across varying lighting and angles, whereas timers, basic motion sensors, and alphabetical sorting use fixed rules (p. 6).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the primary operational benefit of using automation for high-volume, repetitive tasks?
options: A. It performs repetitive steps without human intervention, reducing human error and optimizing resources.
B. It enables the machine to invent brand-new business goals without human oversight.
C. It eliminates the need to maintain or inspect physical equipment.
D. It replaces structured databases with unorganized text files.
choices: A. It performs repetitive steps without human intervention, reducing human error and optimizing resources.
B. It enables the machine to invent brand-new business goals without human oversight.
C. It eliminates the need to maintain or inspect physical equipment.
D. It replaces structured databases with unorganized text files.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It performs repetitive steps without human intervention, reducing human error and optimizing resources.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Automation executes repetitive workflows consistently without continuous human intervention, which minimizes human error and optimizes time, energy, and material resources (p. 6).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: What did mathematician Alan Turing propose the 'Turing test' (originally called the imitation game) to evaluate?
options: A. Whether a computer's power supply can run for twenty-four hours without overheating
B. Whether a database can encrypt ten million passwords in under one second
C. Whether a robot arm can lift heavier loads than a human factory worker
D. Whether a machine can generate text responses in a conversation that a human judge cannot distinguish from another human
choices: A. Whether a computer's power supply can run for twenty-four hours without overheating
B. Whether a database can encrypt ten million passwords in under one second
C. Whether a robot arm can lift heavier loads than a human factory worker
D. Whether a machine can generate text responses in a conversation that a human judge cannot distinguish from another human
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Whether a machine can generate text responses in a conversation that a human judge cannot distinguish from another human
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): The Turing test evaluates whether a machine can communicate in natural language convincingly enough that an evaluator cannot reliably tell the machine apart from a human (p. 6).

pamphlet_excerpts: Shelter and Dry Blankets: Move the victim to a shelter, remove damp clothing, and warm the person with blankets until body temperature returns to normal (p. 11).
Head Coverings and Warm Drinks: Cover the head with a warm hat or other covering, and offer hot drinks (p. 11).
Active Body Warming: If the condition progresses, actively warm the victim's body (p. 11).
Shared Sleeping Bag Warming: Place the victim into a sleeping bag with one or two other people (p. 11).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Actively Warm the Body: If the condition progresses, actively warm the victim's body (p. 11).
Step 2 - Share a Sleeping Bag: Place the victim into a sleeping bag with one or two other people (p. 11).
Step 3 - Use Direct Skin Contact: All should be stripped of most clothing so that skin-to-skin contact can hasten the warming, and perhaps save a life (p. 11).
Step 4 - Seek Emergency Medical Care: Severe hypothermia requires immediate medical attention (p. 11).

options: A. View the Sun directly through binoculars while wearing polarized sunglasses, and use a bright white LED lantern at night to read star charts.

B. Never look at the Sun through any telescope, binoculars, or camera without a certified front-aperture solar filter or indirect pinhole projection, and use a dim red flashlight at night to preserve dark adaptation.
C. Thread a dark glass eyepiece filter onto the back of a large reflector telescope to view sunspots, and shine a green laser pointer into the eyes of observers to line up constellations.
D. Wipe morning dew off telescope objective lenses with a dry paper towel and warm frozen eyepieces over an open camp stove flame.

pamphlet_excerpts: Urban Artificial Sky Glow: Light pollution is, very simply, too much artificial light concentrated in urban areas (areas around cities) (p. 24).
Unshielded Outdoor Lighting Sources: The glare of streetlights, outdoor signs, parking-lot lights, dusk-to-dawn security lights, and outdoor fixtures around private homes creates (p. 24).
Atmospheric Air Turbulence: Turbulent air can ruin views of the Moon, planets, and faint nebulae (p. 24).
Calm Night Observing Conditions: Wind less nights are better for studying the Moon and planets (p. 24).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Assess Upper Air Turbulence: Turbulent air can ruin views of the Moon, planets, and faint nebulae (p. 24).
Step 2 - Choose Calm Windless Nights: Wind less nights are better for studying the Moon and planets (p. 24).
Step 3 - Monitor Humidity and Airborne Dust: Other conditions that can affect observing are clouds, high or low humidity, and air pollution such as dust and chemicals (p. 24).
Step 4 - Wait for Clear Dark Skies: Faint stars may be visible only on clear, dark nights (p. 24).

Specialized Microfiber Lens Cloths: Use a cloth (such as a microfiber cloth) and cleaner made especially for lenses (p. 62).
Sparing Cleaner Application: Apply cleaner very sparingly to the cloth and never directly to the lenses. Keep dust from building up on lenses (p. 62).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Select Proper Optical Cleaners: Use a cloth (such as a microfiber cloth) and cleaner made especially for lenses (p. 62).
Step 2 - Moisten Cloth Instead of Lens: Apply cleaner very sparingly to the cloth and never directly to the lenses. Keep dust from building up on lenses (p. 62).
Step 3 - Brush Away Loose Dust Gently: Aside from normal cleaning, you may use a very soft brush (such as camel's hair), or compressed air if you take some precautions (p. 62).
Step 4 - Prevent Liquid Contact on Optics: You want to avoid any contact with the lenses and any liquid (p. 62).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the main structural difference between a refracting telescope and a Newtonian reflecting telescope?
quiz_item.question: What is the main structural difference between a refracting telescope and a Newtonian reflecting telescope?
options: A. A refractor uses a curved primary mirror at the bottom of the tube, while a reflector uses only glass lenses
B. A refractor can only observe radio waves, while a reflector observes visible starlight
C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
D. A refractor requires an equatorial mount, while a reflector can only use an altazimuth mount
choices: A. A refractor uses a curved primary mirror at the bottom of the tube, while a reflector uses only glass lenses
B. A refractor can only observe radio waves, while a reflector observes visible starlight
C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
D. A refractor requires an equatorial mount, while a reflector can only use an altazimuth mount
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Refracting telescopes bend light through an objective lens at the front of the tube, whereas reflecting telescopes collect and focus light off a curved primary mirror at the rear (p. 56).

requirements.req_text: Do the following (if instruction is done in a planetarium, Scouts must still identify the required stars and constellations outside under the natural night sky): (a) Identify in the sky 10 constellations, at least four of which are in the zodiac. options: A. Hold the chart flat against the ground with north pointing toward your feet
B. Hold the chart overhead and rotate it until the east label is at the bottom
C. Always keep the north label at the bottom regardless of which direction you face
D. Flip the chart face-down and view it through a mirror

pamphlet_excerpts: Twilight Visibility of Venus: Venus also appears only in the early evening or early morning sky, but it is much easier to see than Mercury (p. 35).
Brilliant Morning and Evening Star: Sometimes called the morning or the evening star, diamond white and brilliant Venus is the brightest planet as seen from the Earth (p. 35).
Unmistakable Evening Sky Brilliance: If Venus is in the evening sky, you can't miss (p. 35).
Inner Planetary Phase Cycles: Because different parts of their sunlit areas are visible from Earth at different times, Mercury and Venus have phases similar to the Moon's (p. 35).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Spot Venus After Sunset: If Venus is in the evening sky, you can't miss (p. 35).
Step 2 - Track Inner Planet Phases: Because different parts of their sunlit areas are visible from Earth at different times, Mercury and Venus have phases similar to the Moon's (p. 35).
Step 3 - Identify Crescent and Gibbous Shapes: At different times, they appear full, gibbous (three-quarters full), half-full (like a first-quarter or last quarter moon), as a crescent (p. 35).
Step 4 - Note Inferior Conjunction Alignment: When Mercury or Venus is on the same side of the Sun as Earth, the planet's unlit side faces Earth (p. 35).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why do Mercury and Venus exhibit crescent phases as seen from Earth while Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn do not?
quiz_item.question: Why do Mercury and Venus exhibit crescent phases as seen from Earth while Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn do not?
options: A. Mercury and Venus have thick cloud layers that block half of their sunlight
B. Outer planets spin too rapidly for telescopes to capture their crescent shadows
C. Earth's shadow falls directly across Mercury and Venus every month
D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
choices: A. Mercury and Venus have thick cloud layers that block half of their sunlight
B. Outer planets spin too rapidly for telescopes to capture their crescent shadows
C. Earth's shadow falls directly across Mercury and Venus every month
D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Because Mercury and Venus orbit closer to the Sun than Earth does, we view their sunlit hemispheres from changing angles, including a crescent when they pass nearly between Earth and the Sun (p. 35).

pamphlet_excerpts: Lunar Maria and Crater Contours: Draw the contours of visible features and label seas and prominent craters (p. 43).
Reference Lunar Map Guides: If you have trouble identifying craters, most public libraries have astronomy books with lunar maps (p. 43).
Apparent Daily Westward Motion: Due to the rotation of the Earth, the Moon appears to travel westward since we see it rise in the east and set in the west (p. 43).
Eastward Orbital Shift Against Stars: If you watch the Moon's position against the background stars, you will see that it also moves slowly eastward due to its orbit around the Earth (p. 43).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Daily East-to-West Rising: Due to the rotation of the Earth, the Moon appears to travel westward since we see it rise in the east and set in the west (p. 43).
Step 2 - Track Eastward Shift Against Stars: If you watch the Moon's position against the background stars, you will see that it also moves slowly eastward due to its orbit around the Earth (p. 43).
Step 3 - Account for Fifty-Minute Delay: This eastward motion means that the Moon rises about 50 minutes later each day (p. 43).
Step 4 - Measure Full Orbital Period: The Moon takes an average of 27¼ days to make one trip around Earth (p. 43).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
quiz_item.question: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
options: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
choices: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The Moon stays in orbit because its forward orbital velocity (inertia) balances the inward gravitational attraction between Earth and the Moon (p. 43).

quiz_item.question: What does a star's color (such as blue-white Rigel, yellow Capella, or red Betelgeuse) primarily reveal to astronomers?
options: A. Its exact distance in light-years from Earth
B. The number of rocky planets orbiting in its habitable zone
C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
D. Whether the star is located in the northern or southern celestial hemisphere
choices: A. Its exact distance in light-years from Earth
B. The number of rocky planets orbiting in its habitable zone
C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
D. Whether the star is located in the northern or southern celestial hemisphere
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A star's color is a direct indicator of its surface temperature: blue stars are the hottest, yellow stars like the Sun are intermediate, and red stars are the coolest (p. 51).

requirements.lead_text: With your counselor's approval and guidance, do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: With your counselor's approval and guidance, do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a planetarium or astronomical observatory. Submit a written report, a scrapbook, OR a video presentation afterward to your counselor that includes the following information: activities occurring there, exhibits and displays you saw, telescopes and other instruments being used, and celestial objects you observed. (b) Plan and participate in an observation session that includes using binoculars or a telescope and includes at least 10 celestial objects beyond those observed in requirement 4. These might be lunar features, Messier objects, additional constellations or planets, or artificial satellites including the International Space Station. List the celestial objects you want to observe and find each in a star chart, guidebook or by using an app. Prepare a log or notebook. Discuss with your counselor what you hope to observe prior to your observation session. Review your log or notebook with your counselor afterward. (c) Plan and host a star party for your Scout troop or other group such as your class at school. Use binoculars or a telescope to show and explain celestial objects to the group. (d) Help an astronomy club in your community hold a star party that is open to the public. (e) Personally take a series of photographs or digital images of the movement of the Moon, a planet, an asteroid, meteor, or a comet. In your visual display, label each image and include the date and time it was taken. Show all positions on a star chart or map. Show your display at school or at a troop meeting. Explain the changes you observed. (f) With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, use online observing opportunities such as SkyNet to observe planets, comets, galaxies, and/or the sun. Describe your experience to your counselor.

requirements.description: With your counselor's approval and guidance, do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a planetarium or astronomical observatory. Submit a written report, a scrapbook, OR a video presentation afterward to your counselor that includes the following information: activities occurring there, exhibits and displays you saw, telescopes and other instruments being used, and celestial objects you observed. (b) Plan and participate in an observation session that includes using binoculars or a telescope and includes at least 10 celestial objects beyond those observed in requirement 4. These might be lunar features, Messier objects, additional constellations or planets, or artificial satellites including the International Space Station. List the celestial objects you want to observe and find each in a star chart, guidebook or by using an app. Prepare a log or notebook. Discuss with your counselor what you hope to observe prior to your observation session. Review your log or notebook with your counselor afterward. (c) Plan and host a star party for your Scout troop or other group such as your class at school. Use binoculars or a telescope to show and explain celestial objects to the group. (d) Help an astronomy club in your community hold a star party that is open to the public. (e) Personally take a series of photographs or digital images of the movement of the Moon, a planet, an asteroid, meteor, or a comet. In your visual display, label each image and include the date and time it was taken. Show all positions on a star chart or map. Show your display at school or at a troop meeting. Explain the changes you observed. (f) With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, use online observing opportunities such as SkyNet to observe planets, comets, galaxies, and/or the sun. Describe your experience to your counselor.

options: A. View the Sun directly through binoculars while wearing polarized sunglasses, and use a bright white LED lantern at night to read star charts.

B. Never look at the Sun through any telescope, binoculars, or camera without a certified front-aperture solar filter or indirect pinhole projection, and use a dim red flashlight at night to preserve dark adaptation.
C. Thread a dark glass eyepiece filter onto the back of a large reflector telescope to view sunspots, and shine a green laser pointer into the eyes of observers to line up constellations.
D. Wipe morning dew off telescope objective lenses with a dry paper towel and warm frozen eyepieces over an open camp stove flame.
choices: A. View the Sun directly through binoculars while wearing polarized sunglasses, and use a bright white LED lantern at night to read star charts.

B. Never look at the Sun through any telescope, binoculars, or camera without a certified front-aperture solar filter or indirect pinhole projection, and use a dim red flashlight at night to preserve dark adaptation.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Never look at the Sun through any telescope, binoculars, or camera without a certified front-aperture solar filter or indirect pinhole projection, and use a dim red flashlight at night to preserve dark adaptation.

B. They act as a natural filter that sharpens the edges of bright planets
C. They only block radio waves and have no effect on visible starlight
D. They push turbulent air layers higher into the stratosphere to stop twinkling
choices: A. They scatter artificial light across the sky and reduce transparency for faint objects
B. They act as a natural filter that sharpens the edges of bright planets
C. They only block radio waves and have no effect on visible starlight
D. They push turbulent air layers higher into the stratosphere to stop twinkling
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. They scatter artificial light across the sky and reduce transparency for faint objects
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Airborne particles and moisture scatter artificial light from below to brighten sky glow while absorbing faint starlight from deep-sky objects (p. 24).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the main structural difference between a refracting telescope and a Newtonian reflecting telescope?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the main structural difference between a refracting telescope and a Newtonian reflecting telescope?
options: A. A refractor uses a curved primary mirror at the bottom of the tube, while a reflector uses only glass lenses
B. A refractor can only observe radio waves, while a reflector observes visible starlight
C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
D. A refractor requires an equatorial mount, while a reflector can only use an altazimuth mount
choices: A. A refractor uses a curved primary mirror at the bottom of the tube, while a reflector uses only glass lenses
B. A refractor can only observe radio waves, while a reflector observes visible starlight
C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
D. A refractor requires an equatorial mount, while a reflector can only use an altazimuth mount
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Refracting telescopes bend light through an objective lens at the front of the tube, whereas reflecting telescopes collect and focus light off a curved primary mirror at the rear (p. 56).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How should you orient a printed star chart when you are standing outside facing east to identify constellations?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How should you orient a printed star chart when you are standing outside facing east to identify constellations?
options: A. Hold the chart flat against the ground with north pointing toward your feet
B. Hold the chart overhead and rotate it until the east label is at the bottom
C. Always keep the north label at the bottom regardless of which direction you face
D. Flip the chart face-down and view it through a mirror
choices: A. Hold the chart flat against the ground with north pointing toward your feet
B. Hold the chart overhead and rotate it until the east label is at the bottom
C. Always keep the north label at the bottom regardless of which direction you face
D. Flip the chart face-down and view it through a mirror
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Hold the chart overhead and rotate it until the east label is at the bottom
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): To match a star chart to the real sky, hold it overhead and turn it so the compass direction you are facing is at the bottom of the chart (p. 9).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do Mercury and Venus exhibit crescent phases as seen from Earth while Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn do not?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do Mercury and Venus exhibit crescent phases as seen from Earth while Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn do not?
options: A. Mercury and Venus have thick cloud layers that block half of their sunlight
B. Outer planets spin too rapidly for telescopes to capture their crescent shadows
C. Earth's shadow falls directly across Mercury and Venus every month
D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
choices: A. Mercury and Venus have thick cloud layers that block half of their sunlight
B. Outer planets spin too rapidly for telescopes to capture their crescent shadows
C. Earth's shadow falls directly across Mercury and Venus every month
D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Because Mercury and Venus orbit closer to the Sun than Earth does, we view their sunlit hemispheres from changing angles, including a crescent when they pass nearly between Earth and the Sun (p. 35).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
options: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
choices: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The Moon stays in orbit because its forward orbital velocity (inertia) balances the inward gravitational attraction between Earth and the Moon (p. 43).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What does a star's color (such as blue-white Rigel, yellow Capella, or red Betelgeuse) primarily reveal to astronomers?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What does a star's color (such as blue-white Rigel, yellow Capella, or red Betelgeuse) primarily reveal to astronomers?
options: A. Its exact distance in light-years from Earth
B. The number of rocky planets orbiting in its habitable zone
C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
D. Whether the star is located in the northern or southern celestial hemisphere
choices: A. Its exact distance in light-years from Earth
B. The number of rocky planets orbiting in its habitable zone
C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
D. Whether the star is located in the northern or southern celestial hemisphere
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A star's color is a direct indicator of its surface temperature: blue stars are the hottest, yellow stars like the Sun are intermediate, and red stars are the coolest (p. 51).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does a spectrometer attached to an observatory telescope help astronomers study a distant star or galaxy?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does a spectrometer attached to an observatory telescope help astronomers study a distant star or galaxy?
options: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
B. It amplifies sound waves traveling through space from stellar explosions
C. It shoots a laser beam at the star to measure the bounce-back time
D. It sweeps dust off the primary mirror during long photographic exposures
choices: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
B. It amplifies sound waves traveling through space from stellar explosions
C. It shoots a laser beam at the star to measure the bounce-back time
D. It sweeps dust off the primary mirror during long photographic exposures
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): By dispersing light into a spectrum, a spectrometer reveals unique elemental spectral lines and Doppler shifts that show composition and radial velocity (p. 64).

B. Calculus or precalculus, physics, chemistry, and computer science alongside strong communication skills

choices: A. Only art history and foreign languages
B. Calculus or precalculus, physics, chemistry, and computer science alongside strong communication skills
C. Automotive repair and woodworking

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Calculus or precalculus, physics, chemistry, and computer science alongside strong communication skills
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): High school students preparing for a career in astronomy should take calculus or precalculus, physics, chemistry, and computer science, while also developing reading, writing, and speaking skills (p. 75).

pamphlet_excerpts: Dietary Sources of Calcium: Calcium is found in dairy products such as milk, cheese, and yogurt, and foods such as nuts, beans, broccoli, and canned salmon (p. 7).
Daily Calcium for Bones: Making sure you have at least four servings of calcium daily will help ensure that your bones stay strong throughout your life (p. 7).
Preventing Future Osteoporosis Risks: If you do not get enough calcium in your diet while you are young, you could be at risk for the bone-thinning disease called osteoporosis (p. 7).
Consequences of Poor Fueling: Failing to fuel and refuel your body with good foods can lead to fatigue and injury; you will also be more likely to getsick (p. 7).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Consume Enough Daily Calcium: If you do not get enough calcium in your diet while you are young, you could be at risk for the bone-thinning disease called osteoporosis (p. 7).
Step 2 - Fuel and Refuel Properly: Failing to fuel and refuel your body with good foods can lead to fatigue and injury; you will also be more likely to getsick (p. 7).
Step 3 - Build Lifelong Eating Habits: Develop good eating habits now so that they will become second nature to you throughout your lifetime (p. 7).
Step 4 - Consult Related Fitness Resources: For more information about nutrition and physical fitness, read the Cooking and Personal Fitness merit badge pamphlets (p. 7).

requirements.description: Do the following with your counselor: (a) Discuss the importance of having a physical examination each year. Discuss why overall health, immunizations, medications, allergies, and medical history are covered during an examination. Tell your counselor when you last underwent a physical examination. (b) Explain how you maintain good health habits, especially during training, and how the use of tobacco products, alcohol, and other harmful substances can negatively affect your health and your performance in athletic activities. (c) Describe the elements of a nutritious, balanced diet, and explain what you do to maintain a healthy diet.

pamphlet_excerpts: Selecting Suitable Athletic Activities: Choose an activity that matches your body type and abilities (p. 21).
Cross Training Across Seasons: During the year, you might want to participate in a variety of athletic activities so that you gain overall fitness (p. 21).
Finding Your Favorite Sport: This also can help you determine which athletic endeavor you like the best (p. 21).
Rules and Training Methods: Participating in an athletic activity means taking the time to learn the rules and proper training methods (p. 21).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Identify Preferred Athletic Endeavors: This also can help you determine which athletic endeavor you like the best (p. 21).
Step 2 - Study Rules and Training: Participating in an athletic activity means taking the time to learn the rules and proper training methods (p. 21).
Step 3 - Verify Equipment With Coach: Your coach can help you learn about the official rules and regulations of the activity you choose and can make sure that you have the right equipment (p. 21).
Step 4 - Consult Counselor on Regulations: Ask your merit badge counselor or coach for help in learning the rules and regulations for the athletic activities you pursue (p. 21).

pamphlet_excerpts: Upholding High Athletic Standards: Regardless if they are considered amateur or professional, athletes should uphold high standards (p. 21).
Historic Olympic Amateur Tradition: They The Olympic Games once featured the world's best amateurs (p. 21).
Original 1896 Eligibility Rules: When the modern Games began in 1896, only amateurs were allowed to compete (p. 21).
Modern Professional Olympic Eligibility: However, the rules changed in 1986 and professionals competed for the first time at the 1988 Olympic Games (p. 21).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Understand Amateur Olympic History: When the modern Games began in 1896, only amateurs were allowed to compete (p. 21).
Step 2 - Note 1988 Rule Changes: However, the rules changed in 1986 and professionals competed for the first time at the 1988 Olympic Games (p. 21).
Step 3 - Check Sport Governing Eligibility: Each Olympic sports group now has the authority to determine whether professionals can compete in its particular event (p. 21).
Step 4 - Practice Good Sportsmanship Always: When participating in athletics, you should practice good sportsmanship (p. 21).

requirements.lead_text: Complete the activities in FOUR of the following options and show improvement over a three-month period:
requirements.req_text: Complete the activities in FOUR of the following options and show improvement over a three-month period: (a) Option A, Sprinting. Do ALL of the following: (1) 100-meter dash (2) 200-meter dash (b) Option B, Long-Distance Running. Do ALL of the following: (1) 3k run (2) 5k run (c) Option C, Long Jump OR High Jump. Do ALL of the following: (1) Running long jump OR running high jump (best of three tries) (2) Standing long jump OR standing high jump (best of three tries) (d) Option D, Swimming. Do ALL of the following: (1) 100-meter swim (2) 200-meter swim (e) Option E, Pull-Ups AND Push-Ups. Do ALL of the following: (1) Pull-ups in two minutes (2) Push-ups in two minutes (f) Option F, Baseball Throw. Do ALL of the following: (1) Baseball throw for accuracy, 10 throws at a target (distance to be determined by age): ages 11 to 12, 20 feet; ages 13 to 15, 30 feet; ages 16 to 17, 40 feet (2) Baseball throw for distance, five throws (total distance) (g) Option G, Basketball Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Basketball shot for accuracy, 10 free-throw shots (2) Basketball throw for skill and agility, the following shots: (a) Left-side layup (b) Right-side layup (c) Left side of hoop, along the key line (d) Right side of hoop, along the key line (e) Where key line and free-throw line meet, left side (f) Where key line and free-throw line meet, left side (g) Top of the key (h) Another spot along the three-point line (h) Option H, Football Kick OR Soccer Kick. Do ALL of the following: (1) Goals from the 10-yard line, eight kicks (2) Football kick or soccer kick for distance, five kicks (total distance) (i) Option I, Weight Training. Do ALL of the following: (1) Chest/bench press, two sets of 15 repetitions each (2) Leg curls, two sets of 15 repetitions each

requirements.description: Complete the activities in FOUR of the following options and show improvement over a three-month period: (a) Option A, Sprinting. Do ALL of the following: (1) 100-meter dash (2) 200-meter dash (b) Option B, Long-Distance Running. Do ALL of the following: (1) 3k run (2) 5k run (c) Option C, Long Jump OR High Jump. Do ALL of the following: (1) Running long jump OR running high jump (best of three tries) (2) Standing long jump OR standing high jump (best of three tries) (d) Option D, Swimming. Do ALL of the following: (1) 100-meter swim (2) 200-meter swim (e) Option E, Pull-Ups AND Push-Ups. Do ALL of the following: (1) Pull-ups in two minutes (2) Push-ups in two minutes (f) Option F, Baseball Throw. Do ALL of the following: (1) Baseball throw for accuracy, 10 throws at a target (distance to be determined by age): ages 11 to 12, 20 feet; ages 13 to 15, 30 feet; ages 16 to 17, 40 feet (2) Baseball throw for distance, five throws (total distance) (g) Option G, Basketball Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Basketball shot for accuracy, 10 free-throw shots (2) Basketball throw for skill and agility, the following shots: (a) Left-side layup (b) Right-side layup (c) Left side of hoop, along the key line (d) Right side of hoop, along the key line (e) Where key line and free-throw line meet, left side (f) Where key line and free-throw line meet, left side (g) Top of the key (h) Another spot along the three-point line (h) Option H, Football Kick OR Soccer Kick. Do ALL of the following: (1) Goals from the 10-yard line, eight kicks (2) Football kick or soccer kick for distance, five kicks (total distance) (i) Option I, Weight Training. Do ALL of the following: (1) Chest/bench press, two sets of 15 repetitions each (2) Leg curls, two sets of 15 repetitions each

options: A. Have the Scout jog two slow cool-down laps around the track while sipping a sports drink.

choices: A. Have the Scout jog two slow cool-down laps around the track while sipping a sports drink.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Recognize life-threatening heatstroke: call 911 immediately, move the Scout into shade, remove excess layers, and rapidly cool the body with cold water or ice packs at the neck, armpits, and groin.

intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-12-31). The Auctioneering Badge is a dynamic blend of public speaking and salesmanship that offers Scouts the opportunity to develop essential communication and persuasion skills. Scouts will learn about the history of auctioneering, develop presentation techniques, and build rapport with an audience. They’ll engage in mock auctions to practice creating demand and closing deals while also learning how to handle challenges and uphold ethical standards. This badge fosters confidence and critical thinking skills that are powerful tools for personal growth, leadership roles, and future success.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
quiz_item.question: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
options: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
choices: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Auctioneering ethics and state licensing laws require complete transparency in bid calling; undisclosed shill bidding is fraudulent and destroys buyer trust.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How does price discovery in an ascending-bid auction differ from a traditional fixed-price sale?
quiz_item.question: How does price discovery in an ascending-bid auction differ from a traditional fixed-price sale?
options: A. The seller sets a price ceiling and buyers negotiate downward from that number
B. Government regulators assign a fixed value before any buyer can make an offer
C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
D. Buyers must wait thirty days after the sale to learn what the final price will be
choices: A. The seller sets a price ceiling and buyers negotiate downward from that number
B. Government regulators assign a fixed value before any buyer can make an offer
C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
D. Buyers must wait thirty days after the sale to learn what the final price will be
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Unlike fixed-price listings that cap what a seller can receive, competitive bidding in an auction allows buyers to push the price upward to true market value (p. 17).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What happens near the end of many online auctions that makes watching until the sale concludes essential?
quiz_item.question: What happens near the end of many online auctions that makes watching until the sale concludes essential?
options: A. All prior bids are erased and the auction restarts as a voice auction
B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
C. The website hides the current high bid so buyers must guess the price
D. Online auctions always close early as soon as three bids are placed
choices: A. All prior bids are erased and the auction restarts as a voice auction
B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
C. The website hides the current high bid so buyers must guess the price
D. Online auctions always close early as soon as three bids are placed
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Most online auction platforms use a staggered soft-close feature that extends the countdown clock by a few minutes whenever a last-second bid arrives (p. 25).

options: A. The seller may cancel the sale after the gavel falls if the price feels too low
B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
choices: A. The seller may cancel the sale after the gavel falls if the price feels too low
B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): An absolute auction has no minimum reserve price, meaning the property is sold to the highest bidder regardless of price, which attracts maximum buyer interest (p. 30).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which two pieces of information must always be clearly understood in an auctioneer's chant?
quiz_item.question: Which two pieces of information must always be clearly understood in an auctioneer's chant?
options: A. The original retail price of the item and the seller's home address
B. The total number of people in the room and the time remaining in the hour
C. The commission percentage and the state sales tax rate on each lot
D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
choices: A. The original retail price of the item and the seller's home address
B. The total number of people in the room and the time remaining in the hour
C. The commission percentage and the state sales tax rate on each lot
D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Every effective chant clearly communicates two numbers to the audience: the bid currently held ('have') and the next increment sought ('want') (p. 34).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why should every item in a unit auction be assigned a distinct lot number before the event starts?
quiz_item.question: Why should every item in a unit auction be assigned a distinct lot number before the event starts?
options: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
B. Because state law requires a ten-digit barcode on Scout camping equipment
C. To prevent anyone from inspecting the items during the preview period
D. So the auctioneer never has to describe what the item is while on stage
choices: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
B. Because state law requires a ten-digit barcode on Scout camping equipment
C. To prevent anyone from inspecting the items during the preview period
D. So the auctioneer never has to describe what the item is while on stage
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Numbering each lot before the sale allows the auctioneer, clerk, and cashier to track every transaction accurately from opening bid to final checkout (p. 41).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
options: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
choices: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Auctioneering ethics and state licensing laws require complete transparency in bid calling; undisclosed shill bidding is fraudulent and destroys buyer trust.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the primary responsibility of a ringperson (or bid spotter) during a live auction?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the primary responsibility of a ringperson (or bid spotter) during a live auction?
options: A. Recording the winning bidder number and final price in the official ledger
B. Spotting buyer bids in the crowd and relaying them clearly to the auctioneer
C. Processing credit card payments and issuing paid lot receipts to buyers
D. Signing the legal consignment contract with the property owner before the sale
choices: A. Recording the winning bidder number and final price in the official ledger
B. Spotting buyer bids in the crowd and relaying them clearly to the auctioneer
C. Processing credit card payments and issuing paid lot receipts to buyers
D. Signing the legal consignment contract with the property owner before the sale
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Spotting buyer bids in the crowd and relaying them clearly to the auctioneer
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Ring persons work the floor to spot bids in large crowds, communicate bid increments to buyers, and relay active bids directly to the auctioneer (p. 12).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does price discovery in an ascending-bid auction differ from a traditional fixed-price sale?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does price discovery in an ascending-bid auction differ from a traditional fixed-price sale?
options: A. The seller sets a price ceiling and buyers negotiate downward from that number
B. Government regulators assign a fixed value before any buyer can make an offer
C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
D. Buyers must wait thirty days after the sale to learn what the final price will be
choices: A. The seller sets a price ceiling and buyers negotiate downward from that number
B. Government regulators assign a fixed value before any buyer can make an offer
C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
D. Buyers must wait thirty days after the sale to learn what the final price will be
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Unlike fixed-price listings that cap what a seller can receive, competitive bidding in an auction allows buyers to push the price upward to true market value (p. 17).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens near the end of many online auctions that makes watching until the sale concludes essential?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens near the end of many online auctions that makes watching until the sale concludes essential?
options: A. All prior bids are erased and the auction restarts as a voice auction
B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
C. The website hides the current high bid so buyers must guess the price
D. Online auctions always close early as soon as three bids are placed
choices: A. All prior bids are erased and the auction restarts as a voice auction
B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
C. The website hides the current high bid so buyers must guess the price
D. Online auctions always close early as soon as three bids are placed
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Most online auction platforms use a staggered soft-close feature that extends the countdown clock by a few minutes whenever a last-second bid arrives (p. 25).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What defines an absolute auction compared to a reserve auction?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What defines an absolute auction compared to a reserve auction?
options: A. The seller may cancel the sale after the gavel falls if the price feels too low
B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
choices: A. The seller may cancel the sale after the gavel falls if the price feels too low
B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): An absolute auction has no minimum reserve price, meaning the property is sold to the highest bidder regardless of price, which attracts maximum buyer interest (p. 30).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which two pieces of information must always be clearly understood in an auctioneer's chant?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which two pieces of information must always be clearly understood in an auctioneer's chant?
options: A. The original retail price of the item and the seller's home address
B. The total number of people in the room and the time remaining in the hour
C. The commission percentage and the state sales tax rate on each lot
D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
choices: A. The original retail price of the item and the seller's home address
B. The total number of people in the room and the time remaining in the hour
C. The commission percentage and the state sales tax rate on each lot
D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Every effective chant clearly communicates two numbers to the audience: the bid currently held ('have') and the next increment sought ('want') (p. 34).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why should every item in a unit auction be assigned a distinct lot number before the event starts?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why should every item in a unit auction be assigned a distinct lot number before the event starts?
options: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
B. Because state law requires a ten-digit barcode on Scout camping equipment
C. To prevent anyone from inspecting the items during the preview period
D. So the auctioneer never has to describe what the item is while on stage
choices: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
B. Because state law requires a ten-digit barcode on Scout camping equipment
C. To prevent anyone from inspecting the items during the preview period
D. So the auctioneer never has to describe what the item is while on stage
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Numbering each lot before the sale allows the auctioneer, clerk, and cashier to track every transaction accurately from opening bid to final checkout (p. 41).

options: A. Contract law, professional ethics, sale marketing, and Uniform Commercial Code regulations
B. Heavy diesel engine repair and commercial livestock veterinary surgery

choices: A. Contract law, professional ethics, sale marketing, and Uniform Commercial Code regulations
B. Heavy diesel engine repair and commercial livestock veterinary surgery

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Auction schools prepare professionals for all aspects of the business, covering auction law, ethics, consignment contracts, marketing, and chant technique (p. 47).

requirements.lead_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter during automotive maintenance activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing a motor vehicle. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (c) Explain the different ways motor vehicles are powered. (d) Explain the safety considerations when performing maintenance on a vehicle equipped with a high-voltage electrical system. (e) Review the maintenance chart in the vehicle owner's manual. Explain the requirements and time limits. (f) Explain the purpose, importance, and limitations of safety belts and passive restraints. (g) Find out the requirements for your state's emissions and safety inspections (as applicable), including how often a vehicle needs to be inspected. (h) Explain the importance of registering a vehicle and find out the annual registration fee for renewing your family car's registration.

pamphlet_excerpts: Side-Impact Air bag Protection: Some cars also include side-impact airbags, which open if the car is hit from either side (p. 20).
Automatic Passive Restraint Operation: These are safety features that do not need the driver or passenger to do anything to make them work (p. 20).
Steering and Dashboard Storage: These devices stay in the steering wheel and dashboard until needed (p. 20).
Front-Seat Occupant Protection: They protect the driver and front-seat passenger (p. 20).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Keep Airbags Stowed Safely: These devices stay in the steering wheel and dashboard until needed (p. 20).
Step 2 - Protect Front-Seat Vehicle Occupants: They protect the driver and front-seat passenger (p. 20).
Step 3 - Verify Mandatory Air bag Equipment: Air bags are required on all new passenger vehicles sold in the United States (p. 20).
Step 4 - Detect Rapid Crash Deceleration: If a front-end crash occurs, sensors in the air bags notice that the car has suddenly slowed down or even stopped (a process called deceleration) (p. 20).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
quiz_item.question: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
options: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
choices: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Hydraulic jacks can fail or leak pressure without warning; a vehicle must always be supported on properly rated mechanical jack stands on level ground with wheels chocked before anyone works beneath it.

requirements.description: Safety and Registration. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter during automotive maintenance activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing a motor vehicle. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (c) Explain the different ways motor vehicles are powered. (d) Explain the safety considerations when performing maintenance on a vehicle equipped with a high-voltage electrical system. (e) Review the maintenance chart in the vehicle owner's manual. Explain the requirements and time limits. (f) Explain the purpose, importance, and limitations of safety belts and passive restraints. (g) Find out the requirements for your state's emissions and safety inspections (as applicable), including how often a vehicle needs to be inspected. (h) Explain the importance of registering a vehicle and find out the annual registration fee for renewing your family car's registration.

requirements.lead_text: General Maintenance. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: General Maintenance. Do the following: (a) Demonstrate how to check the following: (1) Brake fluid (2) Engine oil (3) Coolant (4) Power steering fluid (5) Windshield washer fluid (6) Transmission fluid (7) Battery fluid (if possible) and condition of the battery terminals (b) Locate the fuse boxes; determine the type and size of fuses. Demonstrate the proper replacement of burned-out fuses. (c) Demonstrate how to check the condition and tension of belts and hoses. (d) Check the vehicle for proper operation of its lights, including the interior overhead lights, instrument lights, warning lights, and exterior bulbs. (e) Locate and check the air filter(s).

pamphlet_excerpts: Signs of Hose Deterioration: Belts and hoses that need to be replaced might feel brittle or mushy when you pinch them; they also might show cracks (p. 16).
Accurate Belt Tension Measurement: To accurately check the tension of belts, you must use a belt tension gauge (p. 16).
Manual Belt Deflection Test: However, you can get a rough idea of tension by depressing the belt in the middle of its longest straight section (p. 16).
Serpentine Belt Wear Gauges: Modern serpentine belts do not show obvious wear; use amanufacturerapproved wear gauge to determine if replacement is needed (p. 16).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Press Longest Belt Span: However, you can get a rough idea of tension by depressing the belt in the middle of its longest straight section (p. 16).
Step 2 - Measure Grooves With Gauge: Modern serpentine belts do not show obvious wear; use amanufacturerapproved wear gauge to determine if replacement is needed (p. 16).
Step 3 - Maintain Exterior Vehicle Surfaces: While keeping the engine and other internal systems is vital in extending the life of a car, don't forget to maintain the car'soutside (p. 16).
Step 4 - Protect Clear-Coat Body Paint: Most older-model cars were painted with a clear-coat finish that protects the metal or fiberglass car body and provides an attractive shine (p. 16).

quiz_item.question: How should you determine if a modern serpentine belt needs to be replaced when it does not show obvious cracks?
options: A. Pour soapy water on the pulley while the engine is running
B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
C. Pry the belt off with a screwdriver to test its elasticity
D. Wait until the belt snaps or squeals loudly during highway driving
choices: A. Pour soapy water on the pulley while the engine is running

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Because modern serpentine belts rarely show obvious cracking, technicians use a manufacturer-approved belt wear gauge to check whether the ribs are worn down (p. 16).

pamphlet_excerpts: Proper Tire Inflation Benefits: Tires work best and last longest when they are properly inflated (p. 39).
Underinflation Fuel Economy Loss: In addition, fuel efficiency goes down by 1 percent for every 3 pounds per square inch that tires are under inflated (p. 39).
Vehicle Placard Pressure Priority: If the inflation pressure listed on the tire is different from the pressure noted on the vehicle, use the pressure noted on the vehicle (p. 39).
Monthly Spare Tire Checks: You should check the pressure of all tires, including the spare tire, once a month (p. 39).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Follow Vehicle Placard Pressure: If the inflation pressure listed on the tire is different from the pressure noted on the vehicle, use the pressure noted on the vehicle (p. 39).
Step 2 - Check All Tires Monthly: You should check the pressure of all tires, including the spare tire, once a month (p. 39).
Step 3 - Measure With Handheld Gauge: You can use a handheld tire gauge (p. 39).
Step 4 - Align and Balance Wheels: Adjust camber totoe-in to specifications. specifications. balance wheels (p. 39).

pamphlet_excerpts: Electric vs Gasoline Propulsion: An electric vehicle (EV) works differently than a traditional gasoline car (p. 30).
Battery-Powered Electric Motor Drive: Instead of using an internal combustion engine that runs on gasoline, an EV uses an electric motor powered by electricity stored in a large battery (p. 30).
Underfloor Battery Pack Placement: EVs have a big battery pack, usually located under the floor or in the back of the car (p. 30).
Rechargeable Electrical Energy Storage: This battery stores electricity, much like how your phone stores power (p. 30).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Locate High-Capacity Battery Pack: EVs have a big battery pack, usually located under the floor or in the back of the car (p. 30).
Step 2 - Store Electrical Driving Energy: This battery stores electricity, much like how your phone stores power (p. 30).
Step 3 - Connect Vehicle Charging Cable: The battery is charged by plugging it into a charging station or a wall outlet (p. 30).
Step 4 - Power Electric Drive Motor: The electric motor in an EV is like the engine in a regular car, but it runs on electricity (p. 30).

pamphlet_excerpts: Balanced Water-Antifreeze Mixture: Manufacturers generally recommend an equal mixture of water and ethylene-glycol antifreeze (p. 60).
Year-Round Temperature Protection: This coolant mixture offers good cooling during the summer and protects the engine down to about 35 degrees below zero Fahrenheit in the winter (p. 60).
Premixed Coolant Usage Rule: When you use this type of coolant, you should not add water (p. 60).
Scheduled Coolant Replacement Intervals: Coolant should be checked regularly and replaced about every 30,000 miles or two years, or up to five years in some newer vehicles (p. 60).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Use Premixed Coolant Directly: When you use this type of coolant, you should not add water (p. 60).
Step 2 - Replace Coolant On Schedule: Coolant should be checked regularly and replaced about every 30,000 miles or two years, or up to five years in some newer vehicles (p. 60).
Step 3 - Flush Rusty Cooling Passages: The system also might need to be flushed if there is too much dirt and rust in the coolant (p. 60).

Step 4 - Inspect Plastic Coolant Reservoir: To check the car's coolant in most new cars, you need only to check the coolant level on the plastic coolant reservoir and, if necessary, add coolant (p. 60).

common_misconception_pair.fact: Engines use a specific non-sequential firing order designed by the manufacturer to balance crankshaft forces and minimize vibration (p. 71).

pamphlet_excerpts: Voltage Regulator Charging Control: A voltage regulator controls the amount of recharging (p. 69).
Complete Vehicle Lighting Circuits: The lighting system includes the interior overhead lights, instrument lights, headlights, taillights, turn signals, warning lights, hazard lights (p. 69).
Door-Activated Interior Light Switches: When you open a car door, plunger-type switches close a circuit to the interior lights and make them (p. 69).
Pedal-Activated Brake Light Switch: When you apply the brakes, a switch under the pedal closes a circuit to the brake light bulbs so they light (p. 69).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trigger Door Plunger Switch: When you open a car door, plunger-type switches close a circuit to the interior lights and make them (p. 69).
Step 2 - Depress Pedal Brake Switch: When you apply the brakes, a switch under the pedal closes a circuit to the brake light bulbs so they light (p. 69).
Step 3 - Supply Battery Power Accessories: Wires connect the battery to many other accessories, including the sound system, heating and cooling systems, and (if the car has them) power (p. 69).
Step 4 - Turn Ignition Switch: In some cases (such as the sound system and the heating and cooling systems), you must also turn the ignitions witch on to close the circuit (p. 69).

quiz_item.question: What component in the charging system prevents the alternator from overcharging the vehicle's battery?
options: A. The starter solenoid switch
B. The door jamb plunger switch
C. The spark plug electrode gap
D. The voltage regulator
choices: A. The starter solenoid switch
B. The door jamb plunger switch
C. The spark plug electrode gap
D. The voltage regulator
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. The voltage regulator
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A voltage regulator monitors system voltage and controls the amount of recharging current sent from the alternator to the battery (p. 69).

common_misconception_pair.fact: The outside wheel must travel a longer arc than the inside wheel during a turn, so the differential allows the drive wheels to rotate at different speeds (p. 35).

pamphlet_excerpts: Bicycle Gear Ratio Analogy: You may have seen this idea at work on a bicycle (p. 33).
Low-Gear Hill-Climbing Torque: If your chain is on a small chain ring in the front and a large sprocket in the back, it will help you climb a very steep hill (p. 33).
High-Gear Flat-Road Cruising: If it is on a large chain ring and a small sprocket, it will help you pedal along a flat road at high speed (p. 33).
Paired Automotive Transmission Gears: A key difference between a car transmission and a bicycle gear set is that on a bicycle, you can use any chain ring with any sprocket (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Select High-Speed Cruising Ratio: If it is on a large chain ring and a small sprocket, it will help you pedal along a flat road at high speed (p. 33).
Step 2 - Compare Bicycle Sprocket Combinations: A key difference between a car transmission and a bicycle gear set is that on a bicycle, you can use any chain ring with any sprocket (p. 33).
Step 3 - Mesh Input-Output Gear Pairs: On a car, however, the gears on the input shaft (coming from the engine) and the output shaft (going toward the wheels) are always connected in pairs (p. 33).
Step 4 - Shift Active Gear Pair: Each time you shift gears, the transmission tells a different pair of gears to send power to the wheels (p. 33).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How do the gears inside a car transmission differ from the chain rings and sprockets on a bicycle?
quiz_item.question: How do the gears inside a car transmission differ from the chain rings and sprockets on a bicycle?
options: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
B. Any input gear can slide sideways to connect with any output gear at random
C. A rubber belt jumps from sprocket to sprocket each time the driver shifts
D. Car transmissions have only one fixed gear ratio for both hills and highways
choices: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
B. Any input gear can slide sideways to connect with any output gear at random
C. A rubber belt jumps from sprocket to sprocket each time the driver shifts

quiz_item.correct_answer: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Unlike a bicycle where any chain ring can pair with any rear sprocket, the gears on a car transmission's input and output shafts are always connected in matched pairs (p. 33).

pamphlet_excerpts: Owner's Manual Light Controls: Check the owner'smanual to learn how to turn on the lights for your particular vehicle (p. 46).
Burned-Out Bulb Replacement: Light bulbs in a car burn out just like the ones at home, and you must replace them (p. 46).
Routine Exterior Light Inspections: You should check all the lights on your vehicle from time to time to make sure they work properly (p. 46).
Headlight and Taillight Activation: Turn on the headlights, which will simultaneously light the instrument lights and taillights (p. 46).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Inspect All Vehicle Lights: You should check all the lights on your vehicle from time to time to make sure they work properly (p. 46).
Step 2 - Switch On Main Headlights: Turn on the headlights, which will simultaneously light the instrument lights and taillights (p. 46).
Step 3 - Verify Both High Beams: Engage the high beams on the headlights and make sure that both headlights' high beams work (p. 46).
Step 4 - Test Rear Brake Lights: Have a friend step on the brake pedal while you check to see that the brake lights work (p. 46).
