requirements.lead_text: Do TWO of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Determine the value of three different vehicles you are interested in purchasing. One must be new and one must be used; the third vehicle can be new or used. For each vehicle, find out the requirements and cost of automobile insurance to include basic liability and options for collision, comprehensive, towing, and rental car. Using the three vehicles you chose and with your counselor's assistance, complete the operation/maintenance chart provided in the Automotive Maintenance merit badge pamphlet. Use this information to determine the operating cost per mile for each vehicle, and discuss what you learn with your counselor. (b) Choose a car cleaner and wax product for a vehicle you want to clean. Explain clear-coat paint and the precautions necessary for care. Clean the vehicle, both inside and out, and wax the exterior. Use a vinyl and rubber protectant (on vinyl tops, rubber door seals, sidewalls, etc.) and explain the importance of this protectant. (c) Locate the manufacturer's jack. Use the jack to demonstrate how to engage the jack correctly on the vehicle, then change a tire correctly. (d) Perform an oil filter and oil change on a vehicle. Explain how to properly dispose of the used oil and filter.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why are professionals who service modern vehicles called automotive technicians rather than just mechanics?
quiz_item.question: Why are professionals who service modern vehicles called automotive technicians rather than just mechanics?
options: A. They no longer use any wrenches, sockets, or hydraulic lifts in the shop
B. They only wash and wax the exterior of vehicles at dealerships
C. They must diagnose complex electronics like engine control units and onboard diagnostics in addition to mechanical parts
D. They work exclusively from home offices using remote software updates
choices: A. They no longer use any wrenches, sockets, or hydraulic lifts in the shop
B. They only wash and wax the exterior of vehicles at dealerships
C. They must diagnose complex electronics like engine control units and onboard diagnostics in addition to mechanical parts
D. They work exclusively from home offices using remote software updates
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. They must diagnose complex electronics like engine control units and onboard diagnostics in addition to mechanical parts
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Working on today's sophisticated vehicles requires mastering electronic systems like the engine control unit and onboard diagnostics, not just hand tools (p. 94).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
options: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
choices: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Hydraulic jacks can fail or leak pressure without warning; a vehicle must always be supported on properly rated mechanical jack stands on level ground with wheels chocked before anyone works beneath it.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How should you determine if a modern serpentine belt needs to be replaced when it does not show obvious cracks?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How should you determine if a modern serpentine belt needs to be replaced when it does not show obvious cracks?
options: A. Pour soapy water on the pulley while the engine is running
B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
C. Pry the belt off with a screwdriver to test its elasticity
D. Wait until the belt snaps or squeals loudly during highway driving
choices: A. Pour soapy water on the pulley while the engine is running
B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
C. Pry the belt off with a screwdriver to test its elasticity
D. Wait until the belt snaps or squeals loudly during highway driving
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Because modern serpentine belts rarely show obvious cracking, technicians use a manufacturer-approved belt wear gauge to check whether the ribs are worn down (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What does it mean when the malfunction indicator lamp (check engine light) illuminates on the instrument cluster?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What does it mean when the malfunction indicator lamp (check engine light) illuminates on the instrument cluster?
options: A. The windshield washer fluid reservoir is completely empty
B. The vehicle is overdue for an exterior wash and wax treatment
C. One of the engine's emissions control systems may have a problem
D. The high-beam headlights are currently switched on
choices: A. The windshield washer fluid reservoir is completely empty
B. The vehicle is overdue for an exterior wash and wax treatment
C. One of the engine's emissions control systems may have a problem
D. The high-beam headlights are currently switched on
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. One of the engine's emissions control systems may have a problem
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The malfunction indicator lamp, commonly called the check engine light, illuminates when the onboard computer detects a problem in an engine or emissions control system (p. 85).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: If the pressure molded on the tire sidewall differs from the recommended pressure on the vehicle's door jamb placard, which pressure should you use?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: If the pressure molded on the tire sidewall differs from the recommended pressure on the vehicle's door jamb placard, which pressure should you use?
options: A. Always inflate the tire to the maximum pressure stamped on the tire sidewall
B. Average the two numbers together and add 5 psi for highway driving
C. Let air out until the tire sidewall bulges slightly on level pavement
D. Use the recommended inflation pressure noted on the vehicle
choices: A. Always inflate the tire to the maximum pressure stamped on the tire sidewall
B. Average the two numbers together and add 5 psi for highway driving
C. Let air out until the tire sidewall bulges slightly on level pavement
D. Use the recommended inflation pressure noted on the vehicle
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Use the recommended inflation pressure noted on the vehicle
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): The tire sidewall shows the maximum pressure the tire can hold, so you should always use the vehicle manufacturer's recommended pressure listed on the car (p. 39).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does a battery electric vehicle (EV) generate motion compared to a traditional gasoline car?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does a battery electric vehicle (EV) generate motion compared to a traditional gasoline car?
options: A. It uses an electric motor powered by electricity stored in a large battery pack
B. It burns liquid hydrogen inside a four-stroke piston cylinder block
C. It uses a diesel generator in the trunk that runs continuously at idle
D. It relies on compressed air tanks that refill at gas stations
choices: A. It uses an electric motor powered by electricity stored in a large battery pack
B. It burns liquid hydrogen inside a four-stroke piston cylinder block
C. It uses a diesel generator in the trunk that runs continuously at idle
D. It relies on compressed air tanks that refill at gas stations
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It uses an electric motor powered by electricity stored in a large battery pack
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Instead of burning gasoline in an internal combustion engine, an EV uses an electric motor powered by a large rechargeable battery pack (p. 30).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What temperature protection does an equal 50/50 mixture of water and ethylene-glycol antifreeze provide during winter?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What temperature protection does an equal 50/50 mixture of water and ethylene-glycol antifreeze provide during winter?
options: A. It protects the engine only down to 32 degrees Fahrenheit
B. It protects the engine down to about 35 degrees below zero Fahrenheit
C. It prevents freezing only if the engine stays idling overnight
D. It freezes at 10 degrees Fahrenheit unless extra water is added
choices: A. It protects the engine only down to 32 degrees Fahrenheit
B. It protects the engine down to about 35 degrees below zero Fahrenheit
C. It prevents freezing only if the engine stays idling overnight
D. It freezes at 10 degrees Fahrenheit unless extra water is added
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It protects the engine down to about 35 degrees below zero Fahrenheit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Manufacturers generally recommend a 50/50 mixture of water and ethylene-glycol antifreeze, which protects the cooling system down to about -35 degrees Fahrenheit (p. 60).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What air-to-gasoline ratio allows an engine to achieve the most complete combustion and the lowest exhaust emissions?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What air-to-gasoline ratio allows an engine to achieve the most complete combustion and the lowest exhaust emissions?
options: A. 1 part air to 1 part gasoline
B. 5 parts air to 2 parts gasoline
C. 14.7 parts air to 1 part gasoline
D. 50 parts air to 1 part gasoline
choices: A. 1 part air to 1 part gasoline
B. 5 parts air to 2 parts gasoline
C. 14.7 parts air to 1 part gasoline
D. 50 parts air to 1 part gasoline
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. 14.7 parts air to 1 part gasoline
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A gasoline engine achieves the most complete combustion and lowest emissions when mixing 14.7 parts of air with 1 part of gasoline (p. 48).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What component in the charging system prevents the alternator from overcharging the vehicle's battery?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What component in the charging system prevents the alternator from overcharging the vehicle's battery?
options: A. The starter solenoid switch
B. The door jamb plunger switch
C. The spark plug electrode gap
D. The voltage regulator
choices: A. The starter solenoid switch
B. The door jamb plunger switch
C. The spark plug electrode gap
D. The voltage regulator
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. The voltage regulator
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A voltage regulator monitors system voltage and controls the amount of recharging current sent from the alternator to the battery (p. 69).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do the gears inside a car transmission differ from the chain rings and sprockets on a bicycle?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do the gears inside a car transmission differ from the chain rings and sprockets on a bicycle?
options: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
B. Any input gear can slide sideways to connect with any output gear at random
C. A rubber belt jumps from sprocket to sprocket each time the driver shifts
D. Car transmissions have only one fixed gear ratio for both hills and highways
choices: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
B. Any input gear can slide sideways to connect with any output gear at random
C. A rubber belt jumps from sprocket to sprocket each time the driver shifts
D. Car transmissions have only one fixed gear ratio for both hills and highways
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Unlike a bicycle where any chain ring can pair with any rear sprocket, the gears on a car transmission's input and output shafts are always connected in matched pairs (p. 33).

requirements.req_text: Aviation Basics and Mechanics of Flight. Do the following: (a) Define "aircraft." Describe three kinds of aircraft today, and their typical uses. (b) Provide a brief overview of the evolution of flight, and discuss three notable times in history important to aviation. (c) Explain the difference between a fixed wing and a rotary wing aircraft, and the benefits of each. (d) Explain the operation of piston, turbine, and jet engines. (g) Identify and describe the aerodynamic control surfaces on the aircraft of your choice, and explain how they operate to control its attitude and direction of flight. (h) Explain the purposes and functions of the various instruments found in a typical single-engine aircraft: attitude indicator, heading indicator, altimeter, airspeed indicator, turn and bank indicator, vertical speed indicator, compass, navigation, communication, and engine performance indicators.

pamphlet_excerpts: Engine Monitoring Instruments: The last three instruments, tachometer, oil pressure gauge, and oil temperature gauge, tell a pilot how the engine is operating (p. 28).
The Attitude Indicator: The attitude indicator or "artificial horizon" lets the pilot get an immediate picture of the airplane's attitude, which is its position relative to Earth's (p. 28).
Gyroscopic Horizon Face: Attached to a gyroscope is a face with acontrasting horizon line (p. 28).
Tracking Pitch and Roll: This representation of the horizon moves to show the plane's position with respect to the real horizon (p. 28).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Inspect the Gyroscope Face: Attached to a gyroscope is a face with acontrasting horizon line (p. 28).
Step 2 - Read the Horizon Line: This representation of the horizon moves to show the plane's position with respect to the real horizon (p. 28).
Step 3 - Check the Heading Indicator: The heading indicator can take different forms but is basically a gyroscope that shows the plane's heading (p. 28).
Step 4 - Align With Magnetic Compass: The simplest heading indicators have to be set to match the magnetic compass (p. 28).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Aviation Requirement 1, how do the four aerodynamic forces act on an airplane in steady, level, unaccelerated flight, and how does the wing generate lift?
quiz_item.question: In Aviation Requirement 1, how do the four aerodynamic forces act on an airplane in steady, level, unaccelerated flight, and how does the wing generate lift?
options: A. Lift equals weight and thrust equals drag; the airfoil's camber and angle of attack accelerate airflow over the upper surface to lower static pressure (Bernoulli's principle) while deflecting air downward (Newton's third law).
B. Thrust must be four times greater than weight while drag equals lift; the wing generates lift solely from hot exhaust gases blowing across the ailerons.
C. Weight exceeds lift by twenty percent to keep the aircraft stable, and lift is produced by spinning the propeller in reverse at cruising altitude.
D. Drag propels the aircraft forward while lift pushes the nose down, relying on atmospheric vacuum above the fuselage.
choices: A. Lift equals weight and thrust equals drag; the airfoil's camber and angle of attack accelerate airflow over the upper surface to lower static pressure (Bernoulli's principle) while deflecting air downward (Newton's third law).
B. Thrust must be four times greater than weight while drag equals lift; the wing generates lift solely from hot exhaust gases blowing across the ailerons.
C. Weight exceeds lift by twenty percent to keep the aircraft stable, and lift is produced by spinning the propeller in reverse at cruising altitude.
D. Drag propels the aircraft forward while lift pushes the nose down, relying on atmospheric vacuum above the fuselage.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Lift equals weight and thrust equals drag; the airfoil's camber and angle of attack accelerate airflow over the upper surface to lower static pressure (Bernoulli's principle) while deflecting air downward (Newton's third law).
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In steady, level flight, opposing forces are balanced (lift equals weight, thrust equals drag), and wings generate lift through pressure differentials described by Bernoulli's principle combined with downward airflow deflection under Newton's third law.

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Choose Departure and Destination: Select a departure point and a destination point that will allow for a flight of no more than an hour (p. 78).

Step 3 - Record and Share Observations: When you complete the flight, write down your experiences and share your observations with your counselor (p. 78).
Step 4 - Build and Test Models: A great way to learn about airplanes and the principles of flying is to build model planes (p. 78).

quiz_item.question: What happens when you bend both elevons slightly upward on an FPG-9 foam plate glider before launching it?
options: A. The glider rolls rapidly in a clockwise spiral
B. The airflow pushes the tail down and raises the nose to reduce diving
C. The wings generate extra thrust to double the flight speed
D. The rudder locks in place and prevents any left or right turns
choices: A. The glider rolls rapidly in a clockwise spiral
B. The airflow pushes the tail down and raises the nose to reduce diving
C. The wings generate extra thrust to double the flight speed
D. The rudder locks in place and prevents any left or right turns
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. The airflow pushes the tail down and raises the nose to reduce diving
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Upward elevons deflect passing air upward at the trailing edge, pushing the tail down and pitching the nose up for a gentler glide slope (p. 78).

requirements.lead_text: Flight Operations. Do TWO of the following:
requirements.req_text: Flight Operations. Do TWO of the following: (a) Using a flight simulator software package, set a course and fly the headings you have established with a successful take-off and landing. (b) Under supervision, perform a preflight inspection of an aircraft. (c) Observe and/or participate in an aircraft maintenance activity. Describe the maintenance schedule and requirements for an aircraft of your choice. (d) Obtain and learn how to read an aeronautical chart. Measure a true course on the chart; correct it for magnetic variation, compass deviation, and wind drift to determine a navigational heading for an aircraft. (e) With your parent or guardian's permission, take a discovery flight in an aircraft. Record the date, place, type of aircraft, and duration of flight. Report on your impressions of the flight.

common_misconception_pair.fact: Magnetic variation is the angle between true north and magnetic north on a chart, whereas compass deviation is caused by magnetic interference from electronics and metal inside the airplane (p. 50).

pamphlet_excerpts: Calculating Aircraft Compass Deviation: Technicians can calculate closely just how much the deviation will be for any airplane (p. 50).
The Cockpit Deviation Card: In every aircraft, you will find a deviation card mounted near the compass that tells us how to correct the magnetic course for deviation (p. 50).
Sample Magnetic Course Heading: Remember, the magnetic course from Indianapolis International (IND) to Crawfordsville Airport (CFJ) is 300 degrees (p. 50).
Applying the Compass Correction: Our deviation card tells us that for a magnetic course of 300 degrees, we should steer a course of 301 degrees (p. 50).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Determine the Magnetic Course: Remember, the magnetic course from Indianapolis International (IND) to Crawfordsville Airport (CFJ) is 300 degrees (p. 50).
Step 2 - Consult the Deviation Card: Our deviation card tells us that for a magnetic course of 300 degrees, we should steer a course of 301 degrees (p. 50).
Step 3 - Calculate the Compass Heading: In other words the compass deviation in our airplane at this course is 1 degree higher than the magnetic course (p. 50).
Step 4 - Steer the Corrected Heading: We can now proceed to steer at 301 degrees, confident that we will soon see the Crawfordsville Airport (p. 50).

pamphlet_excerpts: Flight Service Station Role: Providing weather and information services for all pilots is the primary responsibility of the flight service station (p. 73).
Airport Control Tower Structure: As its name suggests, a control tower is an elevated structure from which airport controllers operate (p. 73).
Core Tower Controller Duties: The people in the control tower have four primary responsibilities (p. 73).
Off-Site TRACON Radar Locations: The actual TRACON facility might not be located in the control tower or even on the airport site (p. 73).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Review Controller Core Duties: The people in the control tower have four primary responsibilities (p. 73).
Step 2 - Locate the TRACON Facility: The actual TRACON facility might not be located in the control tower or even on the airport site (p. 73).
Step 3 - Enter the Radar Room: When you visit a terminal radar control facility, expect to enter a darkened room lit only by the glow of radar screens (p. 73).
Step 4 - Observe Aircraft Radar Blips: Controllers skillfully observe and maneuver the "blips" that appear on their screens; each blip represents an aircraft (p. 73).

requirements.req_text: Personal & Professional Aviation Opportunities. Do the following: (a) Explain the following: the student pilot, the recreational pilot, the remote pilot, and the private pilot certificates. (b) Describe the benefits of the instrument rating. pamphlet_excerpts: Recreational Pilot Certificate Limits: The recreational pilot certificate has some important restrictions (p. 57).
Daylight and Airspace Rules: Most importantly, the pilot can fly only during daylight hours and in airspace where he or she does not need to communicate with airtraffic control (p. 57).
Accessible Entry-Level Certificate: Of all the certificates and ratings, the recreational pilot certificate is the easiest to obtain (p. 57).
Thirty-Hour Training Requirement: It requires 30 hours of flight instruction (three hours of which must be solo flight time) (p. 57).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Compare Entry-Level Certificates: Of all the certificates and ratings, the recreational pilot certificate is the easiest to obtain (p. 57).
Step 2 - Complete Thirty Instruction Hours: It requires 30 hours of flight instruction (three hours of which must be solo flight time) (p. 57).
Step 3 - Earn Additional Flight Privileges: The recreational pilot may earn additional privileges (p. 57).
Step 4 - Explore Sport Pilot Options: The FAA created the sport pilot's license in 2004 to help lower the barriers of entry-level aviation by making flying more affordable and accessible (p. 57).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Aviation Requirement 1, how do the four aerodynamic forces act on an airplane in steady, level, unaccelerated flight, and how does the wing generate lift?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Aviation Requirement 1, how do the four aerodynamic forces act on an airplane in steady, level, unaccelerated flight, and how does the wing generate lift?
options: A. Lift equals weight and thrust equals drag; the airfoil's camber and angle of attack accelerate airflow over the upper surface to lower static pressure (Bernoulli's principle) while deflecting air downward (Newton's third law).
B. Thrust must be four times greater than weight while drag equals lift; the wing generates lift solely from hot exhaust gases blowing across the ailerons.
C. Weight exceeds lift by twenty percent to keep the aircraft stable, and lift is produced by spinning the propeller in reverse at cruising altitude.
D. Drag propels the aircraft forward while lift pushes the nose down, relying on atmospheric vacuum above the fuselage.
choices: A. Lift equals weight and thrust equals drag; the airfoil's camber and angle of attack accelerate airflow over the upper surface to lower static pressure (Bernoulli's principle) while deflecting air downward (Newton's third law).
B. Thrust must be four times greater than weight while drag equals lift; the wing generates lift solely from hot exhaust gases blowing across the ailerons.
C. Weight exceeds lift by twenty percent to keep the aircraft stable, and lift is produced by spinning the propeller in reverse at cruising altitude.
D. Drag propels the aircraft forward while lift pushes the nose down, relying on atmospheric vacuum above the fuselage.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Lift equals weight and thrust equals drag; the airfoil's camber and angle of attack accelerate airflow over the upper surface to lower static pressure (Bernoulli's principle) while deflecting air downward (Newton's third law).
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In steady, level flight, opposing forces are balanced (lift equals weight, thrust equals drag), and wings generate lift through pressure differentials described by Bernoulli's principle combined with downward airflow deflection under Newton's third law.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens when you bend both elevons slightly upward on an FPG-9 foam plate glider before launching it?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens when you bend both elevons slightly upward on an FPG-9 foam plate glider before launching it?
options: A. The glider rolls rapidly in a clockwise spiral
B. The airflow pushes the tail down and raises the nose to reduce diving
C. The wings generate extra thrust to double the flight speed
D. The rudder locks in place and prevents any left or right turns
choices: A. The glider rolls rapidly in a clockwise spiral
B. The airflow pushes the tail down and raises the nose to reduce diving
C. The wings generate extra thrust to double the flight speed
D. The rudder locks in place and prevents any left or right turns
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. The airflow pushes the tail down and raises the nose to reduce diving
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Upward elevons deflect passing air upward at the trailing edge, pushing the tail down and pitching the nose up for a gentler glide slope (p. 78).

pamphlet_excerpts: North American Venomous Snakes: There are two types of venomous snakes in the United States (p. 22).
Pit Viper Head Anatomy: Pit vipers (rattlesnakes, copperheads, and cottonmouths) have triangular heads with pit marks on both sides of the head (p. 22).
Coral Snake Color Bands: Coral snakes have black snouts and bands of red and yellow separated by bands of black (p. 22).
Neurotoxic and Hemotoxic Venoms: Coral snakes inject powerful venom that works on the victim's nervous system; pit-viper venom affects the circulatory system (p. 22).

Step 2 - Distinguish Venom Body Effects: Coral snakes inject powerful venom that works on the victim's nervous system; pit-viper venom affects the circulatory system (p. 22).
Step 3 - Carry a Hiking Stick: A hiking stick does double duty when you walk through places where snakes might lurk (p. 22).
Step 4 - Probe Brush Ahead Slowly: Walk slowly and use the stick to poke amongst ones and brush ahead (p. 22).

B. Pour untreated stream water into the boot to cool the heel and tighten the bootlaces as hard as possible.
C. Cut a hole in the hiking sock over the heel and apply antibiotic ointment directly to the wet wool.
D. Stop immediately, remove the boot and sock to let the foot dry, and apply moleskin or adhesive athletic tape over the hot spot before a fluid blister forms.

pamphlet_excerpts: Advance Emergency Planning Value: Developing an emergency response plan in advance gives you and your crew important information to use if you encounter backcountry difficulties (p. 17).
Frontcountry Contact Plan Copies: Along with copies of your trip plan, provide copies of your emergency response plan to people in the frontcountry who can assist your group should you need (p. 17).
Communicating Trail Schedule Delays: If you are delayed, notify your contacts so that they don't initiate an emergency response (p. 17).
Confirming Safe Trek Return: Upon your return, let them know you are back so they won't report you missing (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Notify Contacts of Delays: If you are delayed, notify your contacts so that they don't initiate an emergency response (p. 17).
Step 2 - Report Your Safe Return: Upon your return, let them know you are back so they won't report you missing (p. 17).
Step 3 - Organize Using Patrol Method: The patrol method is an effective way to organize a trek (p. 17).
Step 4 - Share Crew Leadership Responsibilities: It allows everyone to take responsibility for making each trip successful, so everyone gets the most out of the experience (p. 17).

pamphlet_excerpts: Backcountry Trail Courtesy Habits: Extending courtesy to other outdoor visitors is a natural habit of backpackers (p. 61).
Stowing Emergency Mobile Phones: If you carry a mobile telephone for emergency communication, turn it off and stow it in your pack until you need (p. 61).
Respecting Quiet and Solitude: Appreciate the company of those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, but respect their desire for quiet and solitude (p. 61).
Encountering Pack Animals Safely: If you encounter horseback riders or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider (p. 61).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Keep Trail Noise Low: Appreciate the company of those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, but respect their desire for quiet and solitude (p. 61).
Step 2 - Communicate With Lead Rider: If you encounter horseback riders or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider (p. 61).
Step 3 - Step Downhill For Horses: The lead rider will probably ask you to step a fewpaces downhill from the trail and stand quietly while the animals pass (p. 61).
Step 4 - Yield to Uphill Hikers: If you encounter other hikers or backpackers going uphill when you are going downhill, give them the right of-way (p. 61).

pamphlet_excerpts: Minimizing Backcountry Storm Risk: Minimizing Risk (p. 26).
Avoiding Conductive Metal Gear: Metal conducts electricity, so avoid metal poles (p. 26).
Seeking Low Ground Shelter: If astorm catches you, find a cave or a low spot among the rocks (p. 26).
Minimizing Your Lightning Target: Avoid prominent outcroppings, overhangs, and flood zones. If you cannot find shelter, become the smallest target (p. 26).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Locate Low Terrain Shelter: If astorm catches you, find a cave or a low spot among the rocks (p. 26).
Step 2 - Crouch Into Smallest Target: Avoid prominent outcroppings, overhangs, and flood zones. If you cannot find shelter, become the smallest target (p. 26).
Step 3 - Avoid Lying Flat Outdoors: Do not lie flat on the ground, because lying flat makes you a bigger target than crouching (p. 26).
Step 4 - Minimize Ground Contact Area: The less of you that is touching the ground, the better (p. 26).

Constant Position Awareness: This technique calls for your constant awareness of your position (p. 74).
Pocket Map Accessibility: You must carry atopographic map where you can easily refer to it, that is, in your shirt or pants pocket rather than in your pack (p. 74).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Maintain Constant Position Awareness: This technique calls for your constant awareness of your position (p. 74).
Step 2 - Keep Map in Pocket: You must carry atopographic map where you can easily refer to it, that is, in your shirt or pants pocket rather than in your pack (p. 74).
Step 3 - Match Terrain With Map: As you hike, you should continuously try to matchup features around you with points on your map (p. 74).
Step 4 - Verify Route at Junctions: Not only will this prevent you from getting too far off your route if you take a wrong turn, it will keep your map-readings kills sharp (p. 74).

common_misconception_pair.misconception: Heavy cotton jeans and sweatshirts are ideal for cold, wet backpacking weather because cotton is thick and durable.
common_misconception_pair.fact: Cotton absorbs water and loses all insulating value when wet, so backpackers must wear wool or synthetic layers topped by a waterproof, breathable shell (p. 22).

pamphlet_excerpts: Preparing for Trail Injuries: Getting injured while out on the trail is one of the biggest risks for which you need to be prepared (p. 16).
Common Minor Trail Ailments: Fortunately, many trail injuries, scrapes, bruises, blisters, and sunburn, usually are not very troublesome (p. 16).
Essential First Aid Supplies: Soap, water, bandages, and other items in your first-aid kit will take care of the majority of medical problems you may encounter (p. 16).
Remote Emergency Distance Risks: However, the danger of a more serious injury is magnified by your distance from emergency response (p. 16).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Treat Minor Wounds Promptly: Soap, water, bandages, and other items in your first-aid kit will take care of the majority of medical problems you may encounter (p. 16).
Step 2 - Factor In Remote Distance: However, the danger of a more serious injury is magnified by your distance from emergency response (p. 16).
Step 3 - Rely on Crew Resources: Miles up a trail, you must rely on your own resources and those of your companions (p. 16).
Step 4 - Recognize Weather Health Hazards: Know how to prevent, recognize, and treat the health hazards that may arise during a backpacking trip (p. 16).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why is a serious injury or sudden weather emergency much more dangerous on a backpacking trek than in town?
quiz_item.question: Why is a serious injury or sudden weather emergency much more dangerous on a backpacking trek than in town?
options: A. Standard first-aid supplies do not work at high elevations.
B. Backpacking first-aid kits are not allowed to contain bandages or soap.
C. The danger is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring you to rely on your own crew's resources.
D. Trail injuries never include minor issues like scrapes, blisters, or sunburn.
choices: A. Standard first-aid supplies do not work at high elevations.
B. Backpacking first-aid kits are not allowed to contain bandages or soap.
C. The danger is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring you to rely on your own crew's resources.
D. Trail injuries never include minor issues like scrapes, blisters, or sunburn.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The danger is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring you to rely on your own crew's resources.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): While soap, water, and bandages handle most minor issues, the danger of a serious injury is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring reliance on your own resources and companions (p. 16).

pamphlet_excerpts: Chemical Fuel Safety Guidelines: Follow these guidelines for the safe use of chemical-fuel stoves (p. 53).
Required Adult Stove Supervision: Use compressed- or liquid-gas stoves only with knowledgeable adult supervision and only where and when permitted (p. 53).
Home Fuel Storage Location: At home, store fuel containers in a shed, garage, or other uninhabited structure (p. 53).
Reading Stove Manufacturer Instructions: Read and understand the manufacturer's instructions before lighting any stove (p. 53).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Store Fuel Outside Dwellings: At home, store fuel containers in a shed, garage, or other uninhabited structure (p. 53).
Step 2 - Review Manufacturer Stove Manual: Read and understand the manufacturer's instructions before lighting any stove (p. 53).
Step 3 - Use Approved Fuel Bottles: Keep liquid fuels in well-marked, approved containers only and never in a glass container (p. 53).
Step 4 - Secure Fuel Twenty Feet Away: Store fuel in a ventilated, locked box a minimum of 20 feet from buildings and tents (p. 53).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which rule must be followed when storing liquid backpacking fuels at camp or at home?
quiz_item.question: Which rule must be followed when storing liquid backpacking fuels at camp or at home?
options: A. Keep liquid fuel in clear glass jars so you can inspect the fuel for sediment.
B. Store fuel inside your sleeping tent so morning frost does not chill the fuel.
C. Use only well-marked, approved containers and store them in a ventilated, locked box at least 20 feet from buildings and tents.
D. Mix leftover canister gas and white gas in the same container after a trip.
choices: A. Keep liquid fuel in clear glass jars so you can inspect the fuel for sediment.
B. Store fuel inside your sleeping tent so morning frost does not chill the fuel.
C. Use only well-marked, approved containers and store them in a ventilated, locked box at least 20 feet from buildings and tents.
D. Mix leftover canister gas and white gas in the same container after a trip.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Use only well-marked, approved containers and store them in a ventilated, locked box at least 20 feet from buildings and tents.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Liquid fuels must be kept in well-marked, approved containers (never glass) and stored in a ventilated, locked box a minimum of 20 feet from buildings and tents (p. 53).

pamphlet_excerpts: Pre-Departure Equipment Layout: A day or two before you depart on a backpacking trip, spread out all the equipment, clothing, and provisions you and your group intend to take (p. 56).
Identifying Nonessential Gear: Are there some items laid out that are not absolutely necessary (p. 56).
Dividing Crew Provisions: Figure out how you will divide up the food and group equipment you will be taking (p. 56).
Shared Group Load Responsibility: Everyone should share the responsibility of carrying the group's equipment (p. 56).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Divide Group Food Equally: Figure out how you will divide up the food and group equipment you will be taking (p. 56).
Step 2 - Assign Crew Equipment Shares: Everyone should share the responsibility of carrying the group's equipment (p. 56).
Step 3 - Verify Essential Gear Checklist: Check off each item on your list of food and gear, and be sure you have all the essentials (p. 56).
Step 4 - Remove Remaining Nonessential Items: Take a last look through the pile of nonessentials (p. 56).

pamphlet_excerpts: Practicing Trail Visitor Courtesy: Extending courtesy to other outdoor visitors is a natural habit of backpackers (p. 61).
Stowing Emergency Phones Away: If you carry a mobile telephone for emergency communication, turn it off and stow it in your pack until you need (p. 61).
Preserving Wilderness Solitude: Appreciate the company of those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, but respect their desire for quiet and solitude (p. 61).
Communicating With Horse Riders: If you encounter horseback riders or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider (p. 61).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Respect Neighboring Campsite Quiet: Appreciate the company of those you meet on the trail and at campsites near yours, but respect their desire for quiet and solitude (p. 61).
Step 2 - Ask Lead Rider Directions: If you encounter horseback riders or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider (p. 61).
Step 3 - Wait Quietly Downhill: The lead rider will probably ask you to step a fewpaces downhill from the trail and stand quietly while the animals pass (p. 61).
Step 4 - Give Uphill Hikers Right-of-Way: If you encounter other hikers or backpackers going uphill when you are going downhill, give them the right of-way (p. 61).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: According to trail etiquette, who has the right-of-way when two groups of backpackers meet on a steep slope?
quiz_item.question: According to trail etiquette, who has the right-of-way when two groups of backpackers meet on a steep slope?
options: A. Hikers traveling uphill have the right-of-way over hikers going downhill.
B. Hikers going downhill always have the right-of-way because stopping is harder.
C. Solo hikers must always yield to large patrol crews regardless of slope.
D. Whichever group is carrying heavier packs must step off the trail.
choices: A. Hikers traveling uphill have the right-of-way over hikers going downhill.
B. Hikers going downhill always have the right-of-way because stopping is harder.
C. Solo hikers must always yield to large patrol crews regardless of slope.
D. Whichever group is carrying heavier packs must step off the trail.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Hikers traveling uphill have the right-of-way over hikers going downhill.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): When you are hiking downhill and encounter other hikers or backpackers going uphill, you should step aside and give the uphill hikers the right-of-way (p. 61).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What should you include in a backpacking trek journal or logbook each day of your expedition?
quiz_item.question: What should you include in a backpacking trek journal or logbook each day of your expedition?
options: A. Only the exact weight of your pack at the start and end of the trip.
B. A description of your route, a list of your companions, and a paragraph or two each day about the highlights of that day's adventure.
C. Pressed leaves and wildflowers picked from inside national park boundaries.
D. Receipts for every piece of camping equipment owned by your troop.
choices: A. Only the exact weight of your pack at the start and end of the trip.
B. A description of your route, a list of your companions, and a paragraph or two each day about the highlights of that day's adventure.
C. Pressed leaves and wildflowers picked from inside national park boundaries.
D. Receipts for every piece of camping equipment owned by your troop.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. A description of your route, a list of your companions, and a paragraph or two each day about the highlights of that day's adventure.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A trek journal or logbook should include a description of your route, a list of your companions, and a paragraph or two written each day about the highlights of that day's adventure (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Three miles into a steep backpacking trek, a Scout feels a warm, rubbing 'hot spot' on their heel before any skin has blistered. According to Backpacking Requirement 1, what should the crew do?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Three miles into a steep backpacking trek, a Scout feels a warm, rubbing 'hot spot' on their heel before any skin has blistered. According to Backpacking Requirement 1, what should the crew do?
options: A. Hike faster for the next five miles until reaching camp so the foot becomes numb to the friction.
B. Pour untreated stream water into the boot to cool the heel and tighten the bootlaces as hard as possible.
C. Cut a hole in the hiking sock over the heel and apply antibiotic ointment directly to the wet wool.
D. Stop immediately, remove the boot and sock to let the foot dry, and apply moleskin or adhesive athletic tape over the hot spot before a fluid blister forms.
choices: A. Hike faster for the next five miles until reaching camp so the foot becomes numb to the friction.
B. Pour untreated stream water into the boot to cool the heel and tighten the bootlaces as hard as possible.
C. Cut a hole in the hiking sock over the heel and apply antibiotic ointment directly to the wet wool.
D. Stop immediately, remove the boot and sock to let the foot dry, and apply moleskin or adhesive athletic tape over the hot spot before a fluid blister forms.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Stop immediately, remove the boot and sock to let the foot dry, and apply moleskin or adhesive athletic tape over the hot spot before a fluid blister forms.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Backpacking Requirement 1 stresses stopping at the first sign of a friction hot spot, drying the skin, and applying moleskin or tape immediately to prevent a debilitating blister.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the maximum recommended weight for a fully loaded backpack relative to a hiker's body weight?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the maximum recommended weight for a fully loaded backpack relative to a hiker's body weight?
options: A. No more than 25 percent of your body weight.
B. Up to 35 percent of your body weight for multi-day treks.
C. Exactly 40 pounds regardless of the hiker's size.
D. Up to 50 percent of your body weight if using an internal frame pack.
choices: A. No more than 25 percent of your body weight.
B. Up to 35 percent of your body weight for multi-day treks.
C. Exactly 40 pounds regardless of the hiker's size.
D. Up to 50 percent of your body weight if using an internal frame pack.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. No more than 25 percent of your body weight.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): For comfort on the trail, a pack containing everything you need for a safe trek should weigh no more than 25 percent of your body weight (p. 53).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is it important to contact your frontcountry support person as soon as your crew returns from a trek?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is it important to contact your frontcountry support person as soon as your crew returns from a trek?
options: A. To have them log your mileage with the local Scout council office.
B. To return borrowed group equipment within 24 hours of leaving the trailhead.
C. To let them know you are back safely so they do not report you missing or launch a rescue.
D. To verify the weather forecast for the remainder of the week.
choices: A. To have them log your mileage with the local Scout council office.
B. To return borrowed group equipment within 24 hours of leaving the trailhead.
C. To let them know you are back safely so they do not report you missing or launch a rescue.
D. To verify the weather forecast for the remainder of the week.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. To let them know you are back safely so they do not report you missing or launch a rescue.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Upon your return, you must let your frontcountry contacts know you are back so they will not report you missing or initiate an unnecessary emergency response (p. 17).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What should a backpacking crew do when encountering horseback riders or pack animals on a narrow trail?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What should a backpacking crew do when encountering horseback riders or pack animals on a narrow trail?
options: A. Hike quickly ahead until the trail widens into a clearing.
B. Climb onto high rocks on the uphill side of the trail so the horses can see you clearly.
C. Clap your hands to alert the animals of your presence before they get close.
D. Stop, ask the lead rider for instructions, and step a few paces downhill while standing quietly.
choices: A. Hike quickly ahead until the trail widens into a clearing.
B. Climb onto high rocks on the uphill side of the trail so the horses can see you clearly.
C. Clap your hands to alert the animals of your presence before they get close.
D. Stop, ask the lead rider for instructions, and step a few paces downhill while standing quietly.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Stop, ask the lead rider for instructions, and step a few paces downhill while standing quietly.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): When meeting horses or pack animals, stop and ask the lead rider, who will typically ask you to step a few paces downhill and stand quietly while the animals pass (p. 61).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: If a lightning storm catches you in an open area without shelter, why should you crouch rather than lie flat on the ground?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: If a lightning storm catches you in an open area without shelter, why should you crouch rather than lie flat on the ground?
options: A. Lying flat makes you a bigger target for ground current, whereas crouching minimizes ground contact.
B. Crouching keeps your rain jacket from soaking through on wet soil.
C. Lying flat blocks your view of approaching thunderclouds.
D. Crouching allows you to hold onto metal trekking poles for balance.
choices: A. Lying flat makes you a bigger target for ground current, whereas crouching minimizes ground contact.
B. Crouching keeps your rain jacket from soaking through on wet soil.
C. Lying flat blocks your view of approaching thunderclouds.
D. Crouching allows you to hold onto metal trekking poles for balance.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Lying flat makes you a bigger target for ground current, whereas crouching minimizes ground contact.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Do not lie flat on the ground because lying flat makes you a bigger target than crouching; the less of your body touching the ground, the better (p. 26).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the practice of 'thumbnail navigation' during a backpacking trek?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the practice of 'thumbnail navigation' during a backpacking trek?
options: A. Measuring trail distances using the width of your thumb as a one-mile scale.
B. Keeping your map in your pocket and continuously matching surrounding terrain features to points on the map.
C. Pointing your thumb toward the sun to estimate cardinal directions without a compass.
D. Marking every campsite on the map margin with a thumbnail crease.
choices: A. Measuring trail distances using the width of your thumb as a one-mile scale.
B. Keeping your map in your pocket and continuously matching surrounding terrain features to points on the map.
C. Pointing your thumb toward the sun to estimate cardinal directions without a compass.
D. Marking every campsite on the map margin with a thumbnail crease.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Keeping your map in your pocket and continuously matching surrounding terrain features to points on the map.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Thumbnail navigation calls for constant awareness of your position by carrying your map in an accessible pocket and continuously matching terrain features around you with points on the map (p. 74).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is a serious injury or sudden weather emergency much more dangerous on a backpacking trek than in town?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is a serious injury or sudden weather emergency much more dangerous on a backpacking trek than in town?
options: A. Standard first-aid supplies do not work at high elevations.
B. Backpacking first-aid kits are not allowed to contain bandages or soap.
C. The danger is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring you to rely on your own crew's resources.
D. Trail injuries never include minor issues like scrapes, blisters, or sunburn.
choices: A. Standard first-aid supplies do not work at high elevations.
B. Backpacking first-aid kits are not allowed to contain bandages or soap.
C. The danger is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring you to rely on your own crew's resources.
D. Trail injuries never include minor issues like scrapes, blisters, or sunburn.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The danger is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring you to rely on your own crew's resources.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): While soap, water, and bandages handle most minor issues, the danger of a serious injury is magnified by your distance from emergency response, requiring reliance on your own resources and companions (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which rule must be followed when storing liquid backpacking fuels at camp or at home?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which rule must be followed when storing liquid backpacking fuels at camp or at home?
options: A. Keep liquid fuel in clear glass jars so you can inspect the fuel for sediment.
B. Store fuel inside your sleeping tent so morning frost does not chill the fuel.
C. Use only well-marked, approved containers and store them in a ventilated, locked box at least 20 feet from buildings and tents.
D. Mix leftover canister gas and white gas in the same container after a trip.
choices: A. Keep liquid fuel in clear glass jars so you can inspect the fuel for sediment.
B. Store fuel inside your sleeping tent so morning frost does not chill the fuel.
C. Use only well-marked, approved containers and store them in a ventilated, locked box at least 20 feet from buildings and tents.
D. Mix leftover canister gas and white gas in the same container after a trip.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Use only well-marked, approved containers and store them in a ventilated, locked box at least 20 feet from buildings and tents.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Liquid fuels must be kept in well-marked, approved containers (never glass) and stored in a ventilated, locked box a minimum of 20 feet from buildings and tents (p. 53).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When should a patrol spread out all equipment, clothing, and provisions for a prehike inspection?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When should a patrol spread out all equipment, clothing, and provisions for a prehike inspection?
options: A. At the first campsite on the evening of day one.
B. Halfway through the hike during the lunch break.
C. Only after returning home from the trek.
D. A day or two before departing on the backpacking trip.
choices: A. At the first campsite on the evening of day one.
B. Halfway through the hike during the lunch break.
C. Only after returning home from the trek.
D. A day or two before departing on the backpacking trip.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. A day or two before departing on the backpacking trip.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A day or two before departing on a backpacking trip, spread out all equipment, clothing, and provisions to eliminate nonessentials, check off essentials, and divide group gear fairly (p. 56).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to trail etiquette, who has the right-of-way when two groups of backpackers meet on a steep slope?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to trail etiquette, who has the right-of-way when two groups of backpackers meet on a steep slope?
options: A. Hikers traveling uphill have the right-of-way over hikers going downhill.
B. Hikers going downhill always have the right-of-way because stopping is harder.
C. Solo hikers must always yield to large patrol crews regardless of slope.
D. Whichever group is carrying heavier packs must step off the trail.
choices: A. Hikers traveling uphill have the right-of-way over hikers going downhill.
B. Hikers going downhill always have the right-of-way because stopping is harder.
C. Solo hikers must always yield to large patrol crews regardless of slope.
D. Whichever group is carrying heavier packs must step off the trail.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Hikers traveling uphill have the right-of-way over hikers going downhill.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): When you are hiking downhill and encounter other hikers or backpackers going uphill, you should step aside and give the uphill hikers the right-of-way (p. 61).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When weaving a reed or wood-splint basket for Basketry Requirement 1, why must you soak the reed beforehand, and how should you handle cutting tools and awls?
quiz_item.question: When weaving a reed or wood-splint basket for Basketry Requirement 1, why must you soak the reed beforehand, and how should you handle cutting tools and awls?
options: A. Soaking reed in boiling wax makes it brittle enough to snap by hand, and you should pull a pocketknife blade toward your chest for leverage.
B. Soaking dry reed in warm water makes the plant fibers pliable so they bend without cracking or splintering into your fingers, and you must always cut or push awls away from your body and hands.
C. Soaking reed in mineral spirits dissolves the bark, and you should hold the basket between your bare knees while stabbing downward with a sharp awl.
D. Reed should never touch water before weaving, and spokes should be trimmed by biting them or snapping them against a metal table edge.

pamphlet_excerpts: Common Basketry Weave Patterns: The following are common weaves used in this pamphlet (p. 11).
Over-Under Plain Weave Structure: Sometimes called over-under weave, the plain weave is done with rigid stakes or spokes, and weavers that wrap around the stakes in an over-one (p. 11).
Rigid Stakes Versus Weavers: Spokes and stakes usually are more rigid and thicker reed than weavers (p. 11).
Continuous Weave Visual Similarity: Continuous weave looks much the same as plain weave, but it is woven with a different technique (p. 11).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Select Rigid Structural Spokes: Spokes and stakes usually are more rigid and thicker reed than weavers (p. 11).
Step 2 - Distinguish Continuous Weave Method: Continuous weave looks much the same as plain weave, but it is woven with a different technique (p. 11).
Step 3 - Set Up Odd Stakes: This weave is created over an odd number of stakes (p. 11).
Step 4 - Weave Continuously Adding Reed: It is not done one row at a time, but continuously from beginning to end, with additional weavers added when more length is needed (p. 11).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How does a continuous weave differ in construction from a standard row-by-row plain weave?
quiz_item.question: How does a continuous weave differ in construction from a standard row-by-row plain weave?
options: A. It is woven over an even number of flat wooden slats without any spokes.
B. It uses weavers that are much thicker and stiffer than the upright stakes.
C. It is woven over an odd number of stakes from beginning to end rather than one separate row at a time.
D. It requires sewing coiled pine needles together with waxed thread.
choices: A. It is woven over an even number of flat wooden slats without any spokes.
B. It uses weavers that are much thicker and stiffer than the upright stakes.
C. It is woven over an odd number of stakes from beginning to end rather than one separate row at a time.
D. It requires sewing coiled pine needles together with waxed thread.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. It is woven over an odd number of stakes from beginning to end rather than one separate row at a time.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Continuous weave looks like plain weave, but it is created over an odd number of stakes and woven continuously from start to finish rather than one row at a time (p. 11).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: When weaving a reed or wood-splint basket for Basketry Requirement 1, why must you soak the reed beforehand, and how should you handle cutting tools and awls?
options: A. Soaking reed in boiling wax makes it brittle enough to snap by hand, and you should pull a pocketknife blade toward your chest for leverage.
B. Soaking dry reed in warm water makes the plant fibers pliable so they bend without cracking or splintering into your fingers, and you must always cut or push awls away from your body and hands.
C. Soaking reed in mineral spirits dissolves the bark, and you should hold the basket between your bare knees while stabbing downward with a sharp awl.
D. Reed should never touch water before weaving, and spokes should be trimmed by biting them or snapping them against a metal table edge.

options: A. It is woven over an even number of flat wooden slats without any spokes.
B. It uses weavers that are much thicker and stiffer than the upright stakes.
C. It is woven over an odd number of stakes from beginning to end rather than one separate row at a time.
D. It requires sewing coiled pine needles together with waxed thread.
choices: A. It is woven over an even number of flat wooden slats without any spokes.
B. It uses weavers that are much thicker and stiffer than the upright stakes.
C. It is woven over an odd number of stakes from beginning to end rather than one separate row at a time.
D. It requires sewing coiled pine needles together with waxed thread.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. It is woven over an odd number of stakes from beginning to end rather than one separate row at a time.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Continuous weave looks like plain weave, but it is created over an odd number of stakes and woven continuously from start to finish rather than one row at a time (p. 11).

pamphlet_excerpts: Ecosystem Health and Vitality: Birds lend life, color, and music to the outdoors, and they are an important part of the ecosystems that keep this planet healthy (p. 10).
Sensitivity to Environmental Trouble: Because they are sensitive to changes in the environment, birds are valuable indicators of trouble, including pollution and habitat loss (p. 10).
Historical Rap tor and Pelican Declines: It was the near-disappearance of bald eagles, peregrine falcons, and brown pelicans decades ago that alerted people to the dangers (p. 10).
Songbird Declines and Habitat: Major, rapid declines in the number of songbirds have shown that we must preserve large areas for wildlife habitat (p. 10).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Review Historical Rap tor Declines: It was the near-disappearance of bald eagles, peregrine falcons, and brown pelicans decades ago that alerted people to the dangers (p. 10).
Step 2 - Track Songbird Population Trends: Major, rapid declines in the number of songbirds have shown that we must preserve large areas for wildlife habitat (p. 10).
Step 3 - Group Species Into Genera: Each species is lumped with its closest relatives to form a genus, usually on the basis of physical characteristics like the shapes of certain bones (p. 10).
Step 4 - Classify Genera Into Families: Closely related genera (the plural of "genus") are grouped together to form a family (p. 10).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Bird Study Requirement 1, why do ecologists regard wild bird populations as vital bioindicators of environmental health?
quiz_item.question: In Bird Study Requirement 1, why do ecologists regard wild bird populations as vital bioindicators of environmental health?
options: A. Because birds never migrate outside a single square mile, making them immune to weather or habitat changes elsewhere.
B. Because birds feed exclusively on inorganic soil minerals and are unaffected by agricultural pesticides or wetland loss.

C. Because birds occupy diverse trophic levels, respond rapidly to habitat fragmentation, insect declines, and chemical pollutants (such as DDT thinning eggshells), and perform critical seed dispersal and pest control.
D. Because wild birds can survive indefinitely in polluted industrial zones without clean water or native plant cover.
choices: A. Because birds never migrate outside a single square mile, making them immune to weather or habitat changes elsewhere.
B. Because birds feed exclusively on inorganic soil minerals and are unaffected by agricultural pesticides or wetland loss.

C. Because birds occupy diverse trophic levels, respond rapidly to habitat fragmentation, insect declines, and chemical pollutants (such as DDT thinning eggshells), and perform critical seed dispersal and pest control.
D. Because wild birds can survive indefinitely in polluted industrial zones without clean water or native plant cover.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Because birds occupy diverse trophic levels, respond rapidly to habitat fragmentation, insect declines, and chemical pollutants (such as DDT thinning eggshells), and perform critical seed dispersal and pest control.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Birds are sensitive to changes in insect abundance, water quality, climate, and chemical contaminants across ecosystems, making population trends a reliable early warning of environmental stress.

pamphlet_excerpts: European House Sparrow Releases: In an attempt to control insects that damage crops, people released house sparrows from Europe in many parts of the United States between 1850 and 1900 (p. 18).
Competition With Native Cavities: Instead of controlling insect pests, these small, drab birds made life difficult for native cavity-nesting species (p. 18).
Preference for Human Settlements: Like starlings, they do best around humans and are not found in deep forest or wilderness areas (p. 18).
Western Native Range Origins: These birds are native to the western United States and Mexico (p. 18).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Urban Bird Habitats: Like starlings, they do best around humans and are not found in deep forest or wilderness areas (p. 18).
Step 2 - Identify Native Regional Origins: These birds are native to the western United States and Mexico (p. 18).
Step 3 - Trace House Finch Expansion: However they were first introduced, house finches rapidly spread across the East, South, and Midwest; today the species is found throughout (p. 18).
Step 4 - Note Escaped Exotic Flocks: Escaped parrots, parakeets, cockatiels, and even macaws now thrive in many urban areas, particularly southern Florida, southern Texas (p. 18).

pamphlet_excerpts: Compensating for Eye Strength: Because each eye differs in its strength, you can adjust one of the ocular lenses (usually the right one) to match (p. 45).
Covering the Adjustable Barrel: Hold the binoculars to your eyes, but use one hand to cover the side with the adjustable lens (p. 45).
Center Focus Wheel Alignment: Then use the center focus knob to make the view through the other side clear (p. 45).
Diopter Ring Fine Tuning: Take away your hand, and slowly turn the ring around the adjustable lens until there is no more blurriness and your eyes feel comfortable, with no strain (p. 45).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Focus Fixed Barrel First: Then use the center focus knob to make the view through the other side clear (p. 45).

Step 2 - Turn Adjustable Eyepiece Ring: Take away your hand, and slowly turn the ring around the adjustable lens until there is no more blurriness and your eyes feel comfortable, with no strain (p. 45).
Step 3 - Use Center Focus Knob: Once you have adjusted the eyepiece, you will do all your focusing with the center focus knob (p. 45).
Step 4 - Practice Spotting Moving Birds: Learning to use binoculars well, especially finding birds quickly and easily, takes time (p. 45).

quiz_item.question: What is the correct procedure for calibrating the adjustable diopter eyepiece on a pair of binoculars?
options: A. Turn both the center knob and diopter ring simultaneously while looking at the sky
B. Cover the fixed lens first, adjust the diopter ring, and lock the center focus wheel
C. Cover the adjustable lens side, focus the fixed side with the center knob, then uncover and tune the adjustable ring
D. Close both eyes, set the diopter ring to maximum magnification, and focus only with the right barrel
choices: A. Turn both the center knob and diopter ring simultaneously while looking at the sky
B. Cover the fixed lens first, adjust the diopter ring, and lock the center focus wheel
C. Cover the adjustable lens side, focus the fixed side with the center knob, then uncover and tune the adjustable ring

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Cover the adjustable lens side, focus the fixed side with the center knob, then uncover and tune the adjustable ring
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): You first cover the adjustable lens and sharpen the image for your other eye using the center focus knob, then uncover the adjustable side and turn its ring until the view is clear and strain-free (p. 45).

quiz_item.question: Why does a comprehensive bird field guide include multiple illustrations and written descriptions for a single species?
options: A. To fill extra pages when a bird family has very few species
B. Because males, females, juveniles, and seasonal plumages often look very different
C. Because birds change their bone structure when flying between summer and winter ranges
D. To show how the bird looks under different brands of binoculars
choices: A. To fill extra pages when a bird family has very few species
B. Because males, females, juveniles, and seasonal plumages often look very different
C. Because birds change their bone structure when flying between summer and winter ranges
D. To show how the bird looks under different brands of binoculars
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Because males, females, juveniles, and seasonal plumages often look very different
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Field guides show multiple plumages and written field marks because males, females, and immature birds often differ in color, and many species change appearance across seasons (p. 10).

pamphlet_excerpts: Outer Tail Flash Marks: Juncos have white flash marks on the sides of their tails (p. 29).
Facial Mustache Stripe Markings: A bird doesn't really have a mustache, that's just the nickname for dark markings that extend back from the base of the bill (p. 29).
Distinctive Rump Patch Colors: Rump patches are white or colorful feathers just above the tail, found on species such as northern flickers and yellow rumped warblers (p. 29).
Size References and Silhouettes: Common birds such as sparrows, robins, or crows can be used for size references, while shape can distinguish birds with similar markings (p. 29).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Spot Bright Rump Patches: Rump patches are white or colorful feathers just above the tail, found on species such as northern flickers and yellow rumped warblers (p. 29).
Step 2 - Compare Against Familiar Birds: Common birds such as sparrows, robins, or crows can be used for size references, while shape can distinguish birds with similar markings (p. 29).
Step 3 - Contrast Similar Breast Patterns: A wood thrush and abrown thrasher, for instance, are colored much the same, rusty brown on top, with a white breast spotted in black (p. 29).
Step 4 - Evaluate Body and Beak Shape: But the thrush is plump, with a fairly short tail and a short beak (p. 29).

B. Songs defend breeding territory and attract mates, while calls coordinate flock movement and warn of danger
C. Only juvenile birds sing songs, whereas only adult birds use calls
D. Songs are produced by clapping the beak, whereas calls are made by rustling wing feathers

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Songs defend breeding territory and attract mates, while calls coordinate flock movement and warn of danger

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Go on a field trip with a local club or with others who are knowledgeable about birds in your area. (1) Keep a list or fill out a checklist of all the birds your group observed during the field trip. (2) Tell your counselor which birds your group saw and why some species were common and some were present in small numbers. (3) Tell your counselor what makes the area you visited good for finding birds. (b) By using a public library, the internet, or contacting the National Audubon Society, find the name and location of the Christmas Bird Count nearest your home and obtain the results of a recent count. (1) Explain what kinds of information are collected during the annual event. (2) Tell your counselor which species are most common, and explain why these birds are abundant. (3) Tell your counselor which species are uncommon, and explain why these were present in small numbers. If the number of birds of these species is decreasing, explain why, and what, if anything, could be done to reverse their decline. (c) Participate in a bird banding program with an approved federal or state agency, university researcher, bird observatory, or certified private individual. (1) Explain who is able to band birds and why. (2) Explain why birds get banded. (3) Explain what kinds of birds get banded. (4) Tell how the birds were captured, the number of bird species recorded during your visit, and your role in the program.

Locating Local Audubon Counts: To find out about counts in your area, check with birders you know, askat a nearby nature center, or contact the National Audubon Society (p. 57).
Spring and Fall Migration Counts: Every spring and fall, birders across North America record the migrating birds they see (p. 57).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Contact Local Nature Centers: To find out about counts in your area, check with birders you know, askat a nearby nature center, or contact the National Audubon Society (p. 57).
Step 2 - Log Seasonal Migrating Flocks: Every spring and fall, birders across North America record the migrating birds they see (p. 57).
Step 3 - Join Warm-Weather Migration Counts: The North American Migration Count is a warm-weather version of the Christmas Bird Count and is designed to provide a kind of snapshot of bird (p. 57).
Step 4 - Survey County wide Bird Habitats: Unlike the CBC, however, the NAMC covers entire counties, and participation is free (p. 57).

options: A. The NAMC is a warm-weather count that covers entire counties and is free to join
B. The NAMC only counts flightless birds kept in municipal zoos
C. The NAMC takes place only in December within a 1-mile backyard circle
D. The NAMC requires every participant to hold a federal bird-banding license

requirements.description: Do ONE of the following: (a) Go on a field trip with a local club or with others who are knowledgeable about birds in your area. (1) Keep a list or fill out a checklist of all the birds your group observed during the field trip. (2) Tell your counselor which birds your group saw and why some species were common and some were present in small numbers. (3) Tell your counselor what makes the area you visited good for finding birds. (b) By using a public library, the internet, or contacting the National Audubon Society, find the name and location of the Christmas Bird Count nearest your home and obtain the results of a recent count. (1) Explain what kinds of information are collected during the annual event. (2) Tell your counselor which species are most common, and explain why these birds are abundant. (3) Tell your counselor which species are uncommon, and explain why these were present in small numbers. If the number of birds of these species is decreasing, explain why, and what, if anything, could be done to reverse their decline. (c) Participate in a bird banding program with an approved federal or state agency, university researcher, bird observatory, or certified private individual. (1) Explain who is able to band birds and why. (2) Explain why birds get banded. (3) Explain what kinds of birds get banded. (4) Tell how the birds were captured, the number of bird species recorded during your visit, and your role in the program.

common_misconception_pair.misconception: Dead standing trees in a yard are useless to wildlife and should always be cut down to improve bird habitat.
common_misconception_pair.fact: Standing dead trees, called snags, provide essential hunting perches for flycatchers, bluebirds, hawks, and owls as well as nesting cavities for woodpeckers (p. 82).

pamphlet_excerpts: Berry-Producing Native Trees: The best species are those like dogwoods, spice bush, sassafras, and mulberries that produce lots of berries in summer and early autumn (p. 82).
Nectar Flowers for Hummingbirds: They also enjoy impatiens, salvia, and coral bells (p. 82).
Standing Dead Tree Snags: Many birds, including flycatchers, bluebirds, hawks, and owls, use snags for hunting perches, and woodpeckers will drill nest holes in them (p. 82).
Attracting Cavity-Nesting Wildlife: A snag often attracts species you would otherwise never see in your yard (p. 82).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Preserve Safe Standing Snags: Many birds, including flycatchers, bluebirds, hawks, and owls, use snags for hunting perches, and woodpeckers will drill nest holes in them (p. 82).
Step 2 - Provide Natural Hunting Perches: A snag often attracts species you would otherwise never see in your yard (p. 82).
Step 3 - Select Thick Untreated Lumber: Use 3⁄4-inch, untreated lumber (p. 82).
Step 4 - Drill Ventilation and Drain Holes: Be sure to drill several 1⁄4-inch ventilation holes around the top of the side and back walls, and several more in the floor for drainage (p. 82).

Pack Hunting by Harris' Hawks: Harris' hawks in the Southwest hunt in packs and share the jackrabbits that they kill (p. 31).
Traditional Gull Shell-Dropping: In the past, gulls dropped clams on rocks to break open their shells (p. 31).
Gulls Using Paved Roads: Now gulls use roads for the same purpose, and also benefit from cars that run over and break the clams open (p. 31).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Natural Foraging Habits: In the past, gulls dropped clams on rocks to break open their shells (p. 31).
Step 2 - Note Behavioral Adaptations: Now gulls use roads for the same purpose, and also benefit from cars that run over and break the clams open (p. 31).
Step 3 - Study Green Heron Baiting: The most unusual hunting technique may be bait fishing (p. 31).
Step 4 - Identify Food Caching Species: Some birds store food when it is abundant to get them through leaner times (p. 31).
