pamphlet_excerpts: Cleaning Minor Cuts and Scrapes: Wash cuts, scratches, and scrapes with soap and water (p. 86).
Sterile Dressing for Larger Wounds: Cover larger wounds with a sterile gauzepad or a clean cloth folded into a pad (p. 86).
Long-Term Risks of Sun Exposure: Sunburn can cause lasting skin damage and the potential for skin cancer (p. 86).
Sunscreen and Protective Riding Apparel: Cover up to prevent sunburn, and use plenty of sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15 (p. 86).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Assess Sunburn and Heat Risks: Sunburn can cause lasting skin damage and the potential for skin cancer (p. 86).
Step 2 - Apply SPF 15 Sunscreen Protection: Cover up to prevent sunburn, and use plenty of sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15 (p. 86).
Step 3 - Cool Sunburned Skin With Cloths: To ease the pain of a mild sunburn, apply cool, wet cloths to the affected area (p. 86).
Step 4 - Soothe Skin With Aloe Lotion: A soothing lotion containing chamomile or aloe vera may provide relief (p. 86).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Before departing on a 25-mile troop road ride, you check a Scout's helmet and notice the front rim sits high on the forehead (4 fingers above the eyebrows) and the side straps form a loose loop below the chin. How must the helmet be adjusted?
quiz_item.question: Before departing on a 25-mile troop road ride, you check a Scout's helmet and notice the front rim sits high on the forehead (4 fingers above the eyebrows) and the side straps form a loose loop below the chin. How must the helmet be adjusted?
options: A. Tilt the helmet back further so the Scout can see traffic lights more easily.

B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
C. Wear a thick winter beanie underneath the loose straps without tightening the retention dial.
D. Unbuckle the chin strap during uphill climbs and refasten it only on downhill segments.
choices: A. Tilt the helmet back further so the Scout can see traffic lights more easily.

B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
C. Wear a thick winter beanie underneath the loose straps without tightening the retention dial.
D. Unbuckle the chin strap during uphill climbs and refasten it only on downhill segments.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A helmet tilted back exposes the frontal skull in a forward crash; the BSA Cycling Pamphlet's 2-V-1 fit check keeps the helmet level and secure during impact.

pamphlet_excerpts: Courteous Riding Around Faster Traffic: However, you should not delay faster drivers unnecessarily (p. 57).
Merging With Same-Speed Vehicle Traffic: If you are going the same speed as other vehicles, pull into line with them (p. 57).
Safe Clearance When Passing Vehicles: Don't ride too close to the vehicle you are passing (p. 57).
Returning to the Right Lane: After you pass, return to the right lane as soon as is convenient (p. 57).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Maintain Safe Passing Distance: Don't ride too close to the vehicle you are passing (p. 57).
Step 2 - Merge Back Into Right Lane: After you pass, return to the right lane as soon as is convenient (p. 57).
Step 3 - Identify Driveway and Road Intersections: An intersection is any point, including a driveway, where the paths of two vehicles can cross (p. 57).
Step 4 - Navigate Intersections Safely and Predictably: There are ways to get through an intersection as easily and safely as possible (p. 57).

options: A. Pull into line with the vehicles while matching their speed, and return to the right side when slower traffic resumes
B. Hop onto the pedestrian sidewalk at full speed to pass cars on the right at intersections
C. Cross the double yellow center line to ride against oncoming traffic in the left lane
D. Ride within six inches of the rear bumper of the car ahead to draft in its slip stream
choices: A. Pull into line with the vehicles while matching their speed, and return to the right side when slower traffic resumes
B. Hop onto the pedestrian sidewalk at full speed to pass cars on the right at intersections
C. Cross the double yellow center line to ride against oncoming traffic in the left lane
D. Ride within six inches of the rear bumper of the car ahead to draft in its slip stream
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Pull into line with the vehicles while matching their speed, and return to the right side when slower traffic resumes
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): When riding at the same speed as other traffic or preparing to pass or turn, cyclists pull into line with vehicles and return to the right lane once safe and convenient (p. 57).

pamphlet_excerpts: Purpose of Bike Safety Guidelines: The Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines are designed to make bicycle riding safer and more enjoyable for you and others (p. 94).
Counselor Safety Guideline Review: Review these guidelines with your merit badge counselor (p. 94).
Applying Safety Principles on Rides: As with all Scouting activities, these principles should be applied in your cycling event (p. 94).
Helmet Head Injury Reduction Statistics: Bicycle helmets can reduce head injuries by 85 percent, according to the NHTSA (p. 94).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Follow Scouting Bike Safety Rules: As with all Scouting activities, these principles should be applied in your cycling event (p. 94).
Step 2 - Fit and Fasten Approved Helmet: Bicycle helmets can reduce head injuries by 85 percent, according to the NHTSA (p. 94).
Step 3 - Verify Top Tube Stand over Clearance: Make sure you can stand over the top tube of your bicycle (p. 94).
Step 4 - Check Tire Pressure and Brakes: Assure that tires are fully inflated and brakes are working properly (p. 94).

quiz_item.question: According to the NHTSA statistics in the Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines, by how much can wearing a bicycle helmet reduce the risk of head injuries?
options: A. By about 15 percent, and only during high-speed downhill racing crashes
B. By 25 percent, which is why helmets are optional on paved bike paths
C. By 50 percent, provided the rider wears a baseball cap underneath the helmet shell
D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled
choices: A. By about 15 percent, and only during high-speed downhill racing crashes
B. By 25 percent, which is why helmets are optional on paved bike paths
C. By 50 percent, provided the rider wears a baseball cap underneath the helmet shell
D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled

pamphlet_excerpts: Scouting Bicycle Safety Standards: The Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines are designed to make bicycle riding safer and more enjoyable for you and others (p. 54).
Reviewing Inspection Checklists With Counselor: Review these guidelines with your merit badge counselor (p. 54).
Consistent Safety Habits Every Ride: As with all Scouting activities, these principles should be applied in your cycling event (p. 54).
Protective Value of Certified Helmets: Bicycle helmets can reduce head injuries by 85 percent, according to the NHTSA (p. 54).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Apply Inspection Checklist Before Riding: As with all Scouting activities, these principles should be applied in your cycling event (p. 54).
Step 2 - Inspect Helmet Straps and Shell: Bicycle helmets can reduce head injuries by 85 percent, according to the NHTSA (p. 54).
Step 3 - Confirm Frame Stand over Height Fit: Make sure you can stand over the top tube of your bicycle (p. 54).
Step 4 - Test Tire Pressure and Braking: Assure that tires are fully inflated and brakes are working properly (p. 54).

quiz_item.question: When repairing a flat tire on a ride, what critical step prevents the new or patched tube from immediately puncturing again once inflated?
options: A. Use a sharp metal screwdriver to pry the new tube over the rim bead as fast as possible
B. Carefully check the inside of the tire casing and remove the sharp object that caused the puncture, then slightly inflate the tube so it does not pinch
C. Pump the bare inner tube to 100 PSI outside the tire before forcing the tire bead onto the wheel rim
D. Coat the brake pads and wheel rims with chain lubricant so the tire slides into the frame easily

common_misconception_pair.fact: To start smoothly, straddle the top tube with brakes engaged, rotate the starting pedal backward to the 10 o'clock power position, release the brakes, and push down on the pedal while rising onto the saddle (p. 53).

pamphlet_excerpts: Locking Brakes Before Mounting: To mount the bicycle, engage the brakes to prevent the bike from rolling (p. 53).
Straddling the Bicycle Top Tube: Swing either leg up and over the bike and straddle the top tube (p. 53).
Pedal Power Position at Ten O'Clock: Use your foot to turn the crank backward until it reaches the 10 o'clock position (p. 53).
Smooth Transition Onto the Saddle: As your body moves up and the bike moves forward, the saddle will move (p. 53).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Set Crank at Ten O'Clock: Use your foot to turn the crank backward until it reaches the 10 o'clock position (p. 53).
Step 2 - Push Down and Rise Onto Saddle: As your body moves up and the bike moves forward, the saddle will move (p. 53).
Step 3 - Complete Second Pedal Stroke Smoothly: When the opposite pedal reaches the 12 o'clock position, make a second pedal stroke (p. 53).
Step 4 - Dismount Using Low Left Pedal: To dismount, place the left pedal straight down and stand on it like a step (p. 53).

fields.Straddling the Bicycle Top Tube: Swing either leg up and over the bike and straddle the top tube (p. 53).
fields.Pedal Power Position at Ten O'Clock: Use your foot to turn the crank backward until it reaches the 10 o'clock position (p. 53).
fields.Smooth Transition Onto the Saddle: As your body moves up and the bike moves forward, the saddle will move (p. 53).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the proper technique for executing an emergency stop on a bicycle without pitching over the handlebars?
quiz_item.question: What is the proper technique for executing an emergency stop on a bicycle without pitching over the handlebars?
options: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
choices: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): During an emergency stop, applying both brakes firmly while shifting your hips and body weight low and back over the rear wheel maximizes stopping power and prevents pitching over the handlebars (p. 53).

requirements.lead_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website)
requirements.req_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website) (a) Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride. (b) Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.text: Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride.

pamphlet_excerpts: Option A Road Biking Touring: Push your bike into the turn, keep your head up and look at your exit point, one finger on each brake lever (p. 80).

sub_requirements.label: (b)
sub_requirements.text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

pamphlet_excerpts: Side-to-Side Bike and Body Separation: Using side-to-side bike/body separation, you can control your bike through many tight turns on trails (p. 80).
Setting Up Ninety-Degree Practice Turns: Practice this skill on a relatively flat space with some markers (cones, half tennis balls, or rocks and sticks) and mark out a 90-degree turn (p. 80).
Cornering Off Saddle With Level Pedals: Practice riding through the turns several times, increasing your speed, off the saddle and with level pedals (p. 80).
Looking Ahead With Ready Brake Fingers: Push your bike into the turn, keep your head up and look at your exit point, one finger on each brake lever (p. 80).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Practice Turns With Level Pedals: Practice riding through the turns several times, increasing your speed, off the saddle and with level pedals (p. 80).
Step 2 - Lean Bike and Look Toward Exit: Push your bike into the turn, keep your head up and look at your exit point, one finger on each brake lever (p. 80).
Step 3 - Shift Between Seated and Standing Postures: Seated, crouched, or standing (p. 80).
Step 4 - Move Shoulders Forward on Steep Climbs: In the seated position, the rider'sshoulders move forward and the rider may move forward on the saddle (p. 80).

quiz_item.question: Which technique gives you the best control when riding through a tight 90-degree turn on a trail?

B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner
D. Shift your shoulders far behind the rear tire while turning the handlebars sharply without leaning the bicycle frame
choices: A. Sit back heavily on the saddle, drop the inside pedal to the ground, and lock the rear brake through the apex
B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before departing on a 25-mile troop road ride, you check a Scout's helmet and notice the front rim sits high on the forehead (4 fingers above the eyebrows) and the side straps form a loose loop below the chin. How must the helmet be adjusted?
options: A. Tilt the helmet back further so the Scout can see traffic lights more easily.

B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
C. Wear a thick winter beanie underneath the loose straps without tightening the retention dial.
D. Unbuckle the chin strap during uphill climbs and refasten it only on downhill segments.
choices: A. Tilt the helmet back further so the Scout can see traffic lights more easily.

B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
C. Wear a thick winter beanie underneath the loose straps without tightening the retention dial.
D. Unbuckle the chin strap during uphill climbs and refasten it only on downhill segments.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A helmet tilted back exposes the frontal skull in a forward crash; the BSA Cycling Pamphlet's 2-V-1 fit check keeps the helmet level and secure during impact.

B. Hop onto the pedestrian sidewalk at full speed to pass cars on the right at intersections

intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-11-01). Dancing is a fun and exciting way to express yourself, stay active, and connect with others. Every style of dance, from hip hop and ballet to cultural and partner dances, has its own rhythm, history, and story to tell. In the Dance Test Lab Badge, you’ll learn how to move safely, warm up properly, and understand what makes every dance unique. You’ll explore different styles of dance, learn about famous dancers, and even perform your own routine. Whether you’re new to dancing or already love it, this badge will help you build confidence, creativity, and coordination while having a great time moving to the beat.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
quiz_item.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
choices: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dynamic warm-ups increase muscle elasticity and joint synovial fluid, while a clean, dry sprung floor prevents ankle sprains and falls.

B. By avoiding group choreography and dancing exclusively alone
C. By keeping their eyes closed throughout the entire routine
D. By feeling bass vibrations through wooden studio floors and using visual counts

requirements.req_text: Learn and Perform a Dance. Do the following: (a) Learn a dance. Use at least THREE types of warm-ups prior to your routine to prepare different muscle groups for the exercise. The dance may be solo, group, or partner dance and can use a memorized choreographed routine or an improvised dance. It should be a minimum of 2 minutes long or several shorter dances that add up to at least 2 minutes. The dance should demonstrate at least three different dance moves/steps and should contain music with Scout-appropriate lyrics, if applicable. (b) Perform the dance for your counselor or submit a video of your performance to your counselor. Describe to your counselor what precautions you took to avoid injury before and during your performance. Name or describe the 3 different dance moves that you learned, the 3 different warm-ups you chose, and the 5 Elements of Dance in your routine.

requirements.description: Learn and Perform a Dance. Do the following: (a) Learn a dance. Use at least THREE types of warm-ups prior to your routine to prepare different muscle groups for the exercise. The dance may be solo, group, or partner dance and can use a memorized choreographed routine or an improvised dance. It should be a minimum of 2 minutes long or several shorter dances that add up to at least 2 minutes. The dance should demonstrate at least three different dance moves/steps and should contain music with Scout-appropriate lyrics, if applicable. (b) Perform the dance for your counselor or submit a video of your performance to your counselor. Describe to your counselor what precautions you took to avoid injury before and during your performance. Name or describe the 3 different dance moves that you learned, the 3 different warm-ups you chose, and the 5 Elements of Dance in your routine.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
choices: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dynamic warm-ups increase muscle elasticity and joint synovial fluid, while a clean, dry sprung floor prevents ankle sprains and falls.

Step 4 - Mark Api cal Nerve Entry: When extracting a tooth, the dentist cuts the periodontal ligament that connects the tooth to the bone (p. 14).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
quiz_item.question: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
options: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
choices: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Enamel protects the crown over dentin and the central neurovascular pulp while cementum covers the root; cariogenic bacteria in plaque metabolize dietary carbohydrates into acids that dissolve tooth enamel unless removed by brushing, flossing, and fluoride protection.

common_misconception_pair.fact: Scrubbing or drying the root kills the delicate periodontal ligament cells needed for reattachment, so you should hold the tooth by the crown and place it in cold milk or back in its socket (p. 33).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
quiz_item.question: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
options: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
choices: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Handling only the crown and keeping the root moist in its socket, milk, or saline preserves living root cells for successful reimplantation by a dentist (p. 33).

options: A. It coats the teeth in a permanent waterproof plastic layer
B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
C. It numbs the nerve endings inside the pulp chamber so cavities cannot hurt
D. It stops the salivary glands from secreting digestive enzymes
choices: A. It coats the teeth in a permanent waterproof plastic layer
B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
C. It numbs the nerve endings inside the pulp chamber so cavities cannot hurt
D. It stops the salivary glands from secreting digestive enzymes
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Topical fluoride attracts minerals from saliva back into microscopic areas of acid-weakened enamel, reversing the earliest stages of decay (p. 33).

common_misconception_pair.fact: Snapping or sawing floss cuts the delicate gum papilla, so you should curve the floss into a C-shape against the side of each tooth and glide it gently up and down below the gumline (p. 26).

quiz_item.question: When demonstrating proper flossing on a tooth model, how should the floss be shaped once it passes the contact point between two teeth?
options: A. Wrapped into a C-shape against one tooth surface and slid gently under the gumline
B. Pulled straight down into the gum point with a rapid sawing motion
C. Twisted into a tight knot and yanked sideways through the gap
D. Kept strictly above the contact point so it never touches the gumline
choices: A. Wrapped into a C-shape against one tooth surface and slid gently under the gumline
B. Pulled straight down into the gum point with a rapid sawing motion
C. Twisted into a tight knot and yanked sideways through the gap
D. Kept strictly above the contact point so it never touches the gumline
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Wrapped into a C-shape against one tooth surface and slid gently under the gumline
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Curving the floss into a C-shape around the side of each tooth allows you to scrape plaque out of the gingival sulcus without injuring the gums (p. 26).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
options: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
choices: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Enamel protects the crown over dentin and the central neurovascular pulp while cementum covers the root; cariogenic bacteria in plaque metabolize dietary carbohydrates into acids that dissolve tooth enamel unless removed by brushing, flossing, and fluoride protection.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the best immediate first-aid action when a permanent tooth is knocked completely out of the mouth?
options: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
choices: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
B. Scrub the root with a toothbrush and wrap the tooth in a dry paper towel
C. Soak the tooth in rubbing alcohol for thirty minutes before calling a dentist
D. File the tip of the root smooth so it fits back into the gum more easily
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and place it in the socket or cold milk
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Handling only the crown and keeping the root moist in its socket, milk, or saline preserves living root cells for successful reimplantation by a dentist (p. 33).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do dentists and hygienists use chewable disclosing tablets during a plaque-control demonstration?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do dentists and hygienists use chewable disclosing tablets during a plaque-control demonstration?
options: A. To numb the gums before taking dental radiographs
B. To bleach coffee stains out of the outer enamel
C. To harden soft dental stone impressions in the mouth
D. To dye invisible bacterial plaque so patients can see missed spots
choices: A. To numb the gums before taking dental radiographs
B. To bleach coffee stains out of the outer enamel
C. To harden soft dental stone impressions in the mouth
D. To dye invisible bacterial plaque so patients can see missed spots
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To dye invisible bacterial plaque so patients can see missed spots
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Disclosing dye colors nearly invisible plaque deposits on teeth, showing patients exactly where to improve their brushing and flossing technique (p. 31).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do you hold the impression tray against a mechanical dental vibrator while adding small amounts of mixed model stone?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do you hold the impression tray against a mechanical dental vibrator while adding small amounts of mixed model stone?
options: A. To heat the plaster so it sets in under ten seconds
B. To bring trapped air bubbles to the surface so the stone cast has no pits
C. To polish the metal impression tray before sterilization
D. To separate the water from the powder after mixing
choices: A. To heat the plaster so it sets in under ten seconds
B. To bring trapped air bubbles to the surface so the stone cast has no pits
C. To polish the metal impression tray before sterilization
D. To separate the water from the powder after mixing
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. To bring trapped air bubbles to the surface so the stone cast has no pits
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Gentle mechanical vibration flows the stone mixture into every tooth indentation while driving out air bubbles that would leave holes in the finished cast (p. 29).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does fluoride work together with saliva to protect teeth that have already erupted into the mouth?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does fluoride work together with saliva to protect teeth that have already erupted into the mouth?
options: A. It coats the teeth in a permanent waterproof plastic layer
B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
C. It numbs the nerve endings inside the pulp chamber so cavities cannot hurt
D. It stops the salivary glands from secreting digestive enzymes
choices: A. It coats the teeth in a permanent waterproof plastic layer
B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
C. It numbs the nerve endings inside the pulp chamber so cavities cannot hurt
D. It stops the salivary glands from secreting digestive enzymes
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It combines with calcium and phosphate in saliva to remineralize weakened enamel
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Topical fluoride attracts minerals from saliva back into microscopic areas of acid-weakened enamel, reversing the earliest stages of decay (p. 33).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Under the BSA Digital Safety guidelines in Digital Technology Requirement 1, what is the safest way to protect your accounts and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) online?
quiz_item.question: Under the BSA Digital Safety guidelines in Digital Technology Requirement 1, what is the safest way to protect your accounts and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) online?
options: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it, and accept friend requests from unknown adults.

B. Use long, unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
C. Disable firewall and operating system security updates because patches slow down video streaming and gaming.
D. Click on urgent pop-up links claiming your account is suspended and enter your credentials on the linked form immediately.

pamphlet_excerpts: Workplace Personal Computer Trend: This program, which was not available for mainframe computers, helped start a trend of companies installing personal computers in the workplace (p. 23).
The Original IBM PC: Two years later, IBM introduced its PC (or personal computer) based on the Intel 8088 microprocessor (p. 23).
Early Spreadsheet and Word Software: The PC ran it sown version of Visi Calc as well as other software programs, including a word processor (p. 23).
Historic Personal Computer Cost: The original IBM PC cost $3,000 when it debuted in 1981, around $7,500 in 2012, adjusted for inflation (p. 23).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Examine Early Productivity Software: The PC ran it sown version of Visi Calc as well as other software programs, including a word processor (p. 23).
Step 2 - Compare Historical Hardware Prices: The original IBM PC cost $3,000 when it debuted in 1981, around $7,500 in 2012, adjusted for inflation (p. 23).
Step 3 - Evaluate Modern Processing Power: Today's desktop computers, thousands of times more powerful, can be purchased for only a fewhundred dollars (p. 23).
Step 4 - Trace Operating System Standardization: Microsoft later created a similar operating system, MS-DOS, for use on computers made by many different companies (p. 23).

First Generation Defense Computing: The military used these first-generation digital computers to calculate weapon trajectories and help build atomic bombs (p. 22).
Massive Size and Power Consumption: Each of these computers weighed tons, filled an entire room, and consumed enough electricity to light up a small town (p. 22).
Fragile Vacuum Tube Hardware: They also required thousands of vacuum tubes, which tended to overheat and burn out, needing to be replaced often (p. 22).

Step 2 - Identify Vacuum Tube Limitations: They also required thousands of vacuum tubes, which tended to overheat and burn out, needing to be replaced often (p. 22).
Step 3 - Examine the Commercial UNIVAC: The first commercially built computer was Mauchly's and Eckert's UNIVAC (p. 22).
Step 4 - Understand General Purpose Computing: It was designed to be a general-purpose, or "universal," computer that would serve scientists, business people, and engineers alike (p. 22).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why would a software engineer choose lossless compression instead of lossy compression when archiving a financial spreadsheet or software program?
quiz_item.question: Why would a software engineer choose lossless compression instead of lossy compression when archiving a financial spreadsheet or software program?
options: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
choices: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Lossless compression reduces file size while preserving 100 percent of the original data, which is essential for text, spreadsheets, and executable programs where missing bytes would corrupt the file (p. 26).

pamphlet_excerpts: Mobile and Internet Device Vulnerability: This applies not only to your home computer but also to any device that can be connected to the internet such as cell phones (p. 49).
Web Tracking by Spyware: Such programs, often attached to some useful software, "spy" on you, tracking your movements on the web (p. 49).
Unauthorized Secret Program Installation: Spyware can also install secret programs on your computer (p. 49).
Database Management Software Purpose: Database manager (DBM) programs are used for organizing, storing, and keeping track of a set of information called a database (p. 49).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Guard Against Secret Spyware: Spyware can also install secret programs on your computer (p. 49).
Step 2 - Select a Database Manager: Database manager (DBM) programs are used for organizing, storing, and keeping track of a set of information called a database (p. 49).
Step 3 - Structure Data Into Records: The data are organized in lines called records, with each record consisting of a number of fields (p. 49).
Step 4 - Populate Consistent Record Fields: For each new record, the same set of fields is stored, with different contents in each field (p. 49).

requirements.lead_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor.
requirements.req_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor. (a) Using a spreadsheet or database program, develop a food budget for a patrol weekend campout OR create a troop roster that includes the name, rank, patrol, and telephone number of each Scout. Show your counselor that you can sort the roster by each of the following categories: rank, patrol, and alphabetically by name. (b) Using a word processor, write a draft letter inviting the parents or guardians of your troop's Scouts to a troop event. Resource: Word Processing Tutorial (video) (c) Using a graphics program, design and draw a campsite plan for your troop OR create a flyer for an upcoming troop event, incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (d) Using a presentation software program, develop a report about a topic approved by your counselor. For your presentation, create at least five slides, with each one incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (e) Using a digital device, take a picture of a troop activity. Send or transfer this image to a device where it can be shared with your counselor. (f) Make a digital recording of your voice, transfer the file to a different device, and have your counselor play back the recording. (g) Create a blog and use it as an online journal of your Scouting activities, including group discussions and meetings, campouts, and other events. Include at least five entries and two photographs or illustrations. Share your blog with your counselor. You need not post the blog to the internet; however, if you choose to go live with your blog, you must first share it with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval. (h) Create a webpage for your troop, patrol, school, or place of worship. Include at least three articles and two photographs or illustrations. Include at least one link to a website of interest to your audience. You need not post the page to the internet; however, if you decide to do so, you must first share the webpage with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval.

pamphlet_excerpts: Organizing Information With Databases: Database manager (DBM) programs are used for organizing, storing, and keeping track of a set of information called a database (p. 49).
Database Records and Fields: The data are organized in lines called records, with each record consisting of a number of fields (p. 49).
Uniform Field Structure Across Records: For each new record, the same set of fields is stored, with different contents in each field (p. 49).
Troop Attendance Database Design: A troop attendance database could be set up with a record for each Scout in the troop (p. 49).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Define Standard Database Fields: For each new record, the same set of fields is stored, with different contents in each field (p. 49).
Step 2 - Create Individual Scout Records: A troop attendance database could be set up with a record for each Scout in the troop (p. 49).
Step 3 - Add Patrol and Rank Columns: Each record would consist of fields for the Scout's name, patrol, rank, troop meeting attendance, campout attendance, and other events (p. 49).
Step 4 - Log Event Attendance Status: An entry of "present" or "absent" could be made in the appropriate field of each Scout's record after each activity (p. 49).

requirements.description: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor. (a) Using a spreadsheet or database program, develop a food budget for a patrol weekend campout OR create a troop roster that includes the name, rank, patrol, and telephone number of each Scout. Show your counselor that you can sort the roster by each of the following categories: rank, patrol, and alphabetically by name. (b) Using a word processor, write a draft letter inviting the parents or guardians of your troop's Scouts to a troop event. Resource: Word Processing Tutorial (video) (c) Using a graphics program, design and draw a campsite plan for your troop OR create a flyer for an upcoming troop event, incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (d) Using a presentation software program, develop a report about a topic approved by your counselor. For your presentation, create at least five slides, with each one incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (e) Using a digital device, take a picture of a troop activity. Send or transfer this image to a device where it can be shared with your counselor. (f) Make a digital recording of your voice, transfer the file to a different device, and have your counselor play back the recording. (g) Create a blog and use it as an online journal of your Scouting activities, including group discussions and meetings, campouts, and other events. Include at least five entries and two photographs or illustrations. Share your blog with your counselor. You need not post the blog to the internet; however, if you choose to go live with your blog, you must first share it with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval. (h) Create a webpage for your troop, patrol, school, or place of worship. Include at least three articles and two photographs or illustrations. Include at least one link to a website of interest to your audience. You need not post the page to the internet; however, if you decide to do so, you must first share the webpage with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval.

pamphlet_excerpts: The Four Rs of Disposal: Do your part to reduce e-waste by following the four R's of digital-device disposal, Reuse (p. 73).
Donating Working Digital Devices: The best form of recycling is to donate your old digital technology to a good cause (p. 73).
Precious Metals in Cell Phones: According to the EPA, for every million cell phones we recycle, 35,000 pounds of copper, 772 pounds of silver, 75 pounds of gold, and 33 pounds (p. 73).
Choosing Certified E-Waste Recyclers: Many companies will responsibly recycle digital e-waste for you; make sure you use a certified recycler (p. 73).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Recover Valuable Metals: According to the EPA, for every million cell phones we recycle, 35,000 pounds of copper, 772 pounds of silver, 75 pounds of gold, and 33 pounds (p. 73).
Step 2 - Verify Recycler Certification: Many companies will responsibly recycle digital e-waste for you; make sure you use a certified recycler (p. 73).
Step 3 - Refurbish Working Electronics: Several companies buy old digital technology, refurbish it, and then resell (p. 73).
Step 4 - Extend Device Lifespans: This is another form of recycling that helps everyone (p. 73).

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to the Digital Technology merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from the Digital Technology merit badge to pursue a hobby or interest. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

requirements.description: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to the Digital Technology merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from the Digital Technology merit badge to pursue a hobby or interest. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Under the BSA Digital Safety guidelines in Digital Technology Requirement 1, what is the safest way to protect your accounts and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) online?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Under the BSA Digital Safety guidelines in Digital Technology Requirement 1, what is the safest way to protect your accounts and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) online?
options: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it, and accept friend requests from unknown adults.

B. Use long, unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
C. Disable firewall and operating system security updates because patches slow down video streaming and gaming.
D. Click on urgent pop-up links claiming your account is suspended and enter your credentials on the linked form immediately.
choices: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it, and accept friend requests from unknown adults.

B. Use long, unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
C. Disable firewall and operating system security updates because patches slow down video streaming and gaming.
D. Click on urgent pop-up links claiming your account is suspended and enter your credentials on the linked form immediately.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Use long, unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Digital Technology Requirement 1 emphasizes safeguarding PII, using strong unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, keeping software updated, avoiding phishing links, and following BSA Youth Protection digital rules.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How did the availability of the VisiCalc spreadsheet program change business computing in the late 1970s and early 1980s?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How did the availability of the VisiCalc spreadsheet program change business computing in the late 1970s and early 1980s?
options: A. It forced small companies to rent time on government mainframes
B. It sparked a trend of companies installing personal computers in the workplace
C. It eliminated the need for operating systems like MS-DOS
D. It raised the price of desktop computers above $50,000
choices: A. It forced small companies to rent time on government mainframes
B. It sparked a trend of companies installing personal computers in the workplace
C. It eliminated the need for operating systems like MS-DOS
D. It raised the price of desktop computers above $50,000
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It sparked a trend of companies installing personal computers in the workplace
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Because VisiCalc was not available on mainframe systems, it helped start a major trend of companies adopting personal computers in the workplace (p. 23).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why would a software engineer choose lossless compression instead of lossy compression when archiving a financial spreadsheet or software program?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why would a software engineer choose lossless compression instead of lossy compression when archiving a financial spreadsheet or software program?
options: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
choices: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Lossless compression reduces file size while preserving 100 percent of the original data, which is essential for text, spreadsheets, and executable programs where missing bytes would corrupt the file (p. 26).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does spyware typically behave once it gets onto a computer or mobile device?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does spyware typically behave once it gets onto a computer or mobile device?
options: A. It organizes troop attendance records into fields and rows
B. It speeds up the CPU clock rate to improve gaming graphics
C. It tracks your movements on the web and can install secret programs
D. It encrypts your web browser connections using HTTPS
choices: A. It organizes troop attendance records into fields and rows
B. It speeds up the CPU clock rate to improve gaming graphics
C. It tracks your movements on the web and can install secret programs
D. It encrypts your web browser connections using HTTPS
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. It tracks your movements on the web and can install secret programs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Spyware is malicious software, often bundled with useful programs, that secretly tracks a user's web browsing and can install additional hidden programs (p. 49).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the key difference between a web address starting with HTTP and one starting with HTTPS?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the key difference between a web address starting with HTTP and one starting with HTTPS?
options: A. HTTP is reserved for government computers, while HTTPS is for schools
B. HTTP sends data as plain text, while HTTPS encrypts the communication
C. HTTPS disables images so web pages load faster on dial-up
D. HTTP requires a security certificate padlock, while HTTPS does not
choices: A. HTTP is reserved for government computers, while HTTPS is for schools
B. HTTP sends data as plain text, while HTTPS encrypts the communication
C. HTTPS disables images so web pages load faster on dial-up
D. HTTP requires a security certificate padlock, while HTTPS does not
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. HTTP sends data as plain text, while HTTPS encrypts the communication
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): HTTP exchanges data in unencrypted plain text, whereas HTTPS encrypts the data sent between your browser and the server to protect logins and personal information (p. 59).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In a troop attendance database, what is the line of information for a single Scout called, and what are the individual categories like Name, Patrol, and Rank called?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In a troop attendance database, what is the line of information for a single Scout called, and what are the individual categories like Name, Patrol, and Rank called?
options: A. The Scout's line is a browser, and the categories are protocols
B. The Scout's line is a field, and the categories are records
C. The Scout's line is a record, and the categories are fields
D. The Scout's line is a pixel, and the categories are vectors
choices: A. The Scout's line is a browser, and the categories are protocols
B. The Scout's line is a field, and the categories are records
C. The Scout's line is a record, and the categories are fields
D. The Scout's line is a pixel, and the categories are vectors
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The Scout's line is a record, and the categories are fields
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Database manager programs organize each item on a line called a record, with each record divided into consistent categories called fields (p. 49).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the legal term for making or trading unauthorized copies of copyrighted software, music, or movies?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the legal term for making or trading unauthorized copies of copyrighted software, music, or movies?
options: A. Lossless compression
B. Open-source licensing
C. Piracy
D. Trademark registration
choices: A. Lossless compression
B. Open-source licensing
C. Piracy
D. Trademark registration
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Piracy
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Copyright law prohibits making unauthorized copies of protected works, and trading in illegal copies is called piracy (p. 80).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the EPA, besides keeping toxic chemicals out of landfills, what is a major benefit of recycling one million cell phones?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the EPA, besides keeping toxic chemicals out of landfills, what is a major benefit of recycling one million cell phones?
options: A. It generates enough electricity to power a mainframe computer for a year
B. It recovers thousands of pounds of copper along with hundreds of pounds of silver and gold
C. It automatically erases all spyware from the internet
D. It converts old lithium batteries into fiber-optic cables
choices: A. It generates enough electricity to power a mainframe computer for a year
B. It recovers thousands of pounds of copper along with hundreds of pounds of silver and gold
C. It automatically erases all spyware from the internet
D. It converts old lithium batteries into fiber-optic cables
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It recovers thousands of pounds of copper along with hundreds of pounds of silver and gold
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The EPA reports that recycling one million cell phones recovers 35,000 pounds of copper, 772 pounds of silver, 75 pounds of gold, and 33 pounds of palladium (p. 73).

pamphlet_excerpts: Focusing on Personal Abilities: Many people with disabilities want to emphasize what they are able to do rather than emphasize their disabilities (p. 9).
Recognizing the Person First: Remember that people with disabilities are people first (p. 9).
Respecting Individual Self-Description: Each person gets to decide how he or she should be described (p. 9).
Applying Person-First Language: You should use person-first language when talking about people who are not personal acquaintances or about people with disabilities as a group (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Honor Personal Description Choices: Each person gets to decide how he or she should be described (p. 9).
Step 2 - Use Person-First Language: You should use person-first language when talking about people who are not personal acquaintances or about people with disabilities as a group (p. 9).
Step 3 - Ask New Friends Directly: When you make a new friend or talk about an individual, show a person-first attitude by calling the individual what he orshe wants to be called (p. 9).
Step 4 - Acknowledge Whole Personal Identity: Many people with disabilities see their condition as part of who they are, just like their gender, hair or eye color, or ethnicity (p. 9).

options: A. Speak only to the person's companion or interpreter in a loud voice, and assume anyone who does not use a wheelchair has no disability.
B. Push a person's wheelchair or grab a blind person's white cane without asking so you can move them through doorways faster.

C. Speak directly to the individual using respectful people-first or preferred language, ask before offering physical assistance, and recognize that many disabilities (such as autism, epilepsy, diabetes, hearing loss, or learning differences) are not immediately visible.
D. Avoid inviting Scouts with physical or sensory disabilities on campouts so the troop does not have to adjust trail plans.

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Speak directly to the individual using respectful people-first or preferred language, ask before offering physical assistance, and recognize that many disabilities (such as autism, epilepsy, diabetes, hearing loss, or learning differences) are not immediately visible.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Respectful disability etiquette means treating the individual as a peer, speaking directly to them, asking before assisting, respecting assistive equipment as personal space, and understanding that many conditions are non-apparent.

pamphlet_excerpts: Early Career Preparation: If a career in audiology interests you, you should begin early to get the background needed (p. 19).
Foundational High School Courses: In school, take biology, physical science, language, and physical education classes (p. 19).
Agency Volunteering and Employment: Get an after-schooljob or volunteer with an agency or organization that serves people who have disabilities (p. 19).
Audiology Diagnosis and Care: Audiologists are trained to detect and diagnose hearing problems (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Volunteer With Support Agencies: Get an after-schooljob or volunteer with an agency or organization that serves people who have disabilities (p. 19).
Step 2 - Observe Professional Hearing Diagnoses: Audiologists are trained to detect and diagnose hearing problems (p. 19).
Step 3 - Measure Hearing With Audio meters: An audiologist uses an instrument called anaudiometer to test a person's hearing (p. 19).
Step 4 - Conduct Behavioral Sound Assessments: An audiologist also may give behavioral tests to find out how a person reacts to various sounds and vibrations (p. 19).

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Talk with a Scout who has a disability and learn about the Scout's experiences taking part in Scouting activities and earning different merit badges. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor. (b) Talk with an individual who has a disability and learn about this person's experiences and the activities in which this person likes to participate. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor. (c) Learn how people with disabilities take part in a particular adaptive sport or recreational activity. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor. (d) Learn about independent living aids such as service animals, canes, and augmentative communication devices such as captioned telephones and videophones. Discuss with your counselor how people use such aids. (e) Plan or participate in an activity that helps others understand what a person with a visible or invisible disability experiences. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Assistive Signal Conversion Devices: These devices can amplify sounds, convert noises to lighted signals, or change speech to text or American Sign Language (p. 11).
Captioned Telephones for Speakers: ASL is its Captioned telephones are used by people with some hearing who are able to speak for themselves (p. 11).
Real-Time Conversation Text Screens: A built-in screen displays text (captions) for every word the other party speaks during the conversation (p. 11).
Video Phones for Signing: Video phones are used to communicate with American Sign Language (p. 11).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Read Live Telephone Captions: A built-in screen displays text (captions) for every word the other party speaks during the conversation (p. 11).
Step 2 - Connect via Video Phones: Video phones are used to communicate with American Sign Language (p. 11).
Step 3 - Communicate Using Sign Language: The screen allows people to sign rather than type or speak their messages (p. 11).
Step 4 - Use Smartphone Accessibility Apps: Cameras, microphones, and apps allow phones to become magnifiers and hearing aids as well (p. 11).

requirements.homework_verification_note: Ask the Scout to explain each concept in their own words using their completed organizer notes for Disabilities Awareness Requirement 3 (lived experiences and adaptive tools) across all 5 sub-requirements before signing the blue card.

requirements.description: Do TWO of the following: (a) Talk with a Scout who has a disability and learn about the Scout's experiences taking part in Scouting activities and earning different merit badges. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor. (b) Talk with an individual who has a disability and learn about this person's experiences and the activities in which this person likes to participate. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor. (c) Learn how people with disabilities take part in a particular adaptive sport or recreational activity. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor. (d) Learn about independent living aids such as service animals, canes, and augmentative communication devices such as captioned telephones and videophones. Discuss with your counselor how people use such aids. (e) Plan or participate in an activity that helps others understand what a person with a visible or invisible disability experiences. Discuss what you have learned with your counselor.

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following options:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following options: (a) Option A, Access. Visit TWO of the following locations and take notes about the accessibility to people with disabilities. In your notes, give examples of five things that could be done to improve upon the site and five things about the site that make it friendly to people with disabilities. Discuss your observations with your counselor. (1) Your school (2) Your place of worship (3) A Scouting event or campsite (4) A public exhibit or attraction (such as a theater, museum, or park) (b) Option B, Accommodation. Visit TWO of the following locations and take notes while observing features and methods that are used to accommodate people with invisible disabilities. While there, ask staff members to explain any accommodation features that may not be obvious. Note anything you think could be done to better accommodate people who have invisible disabilities. Discuss your observations with your counselor. (1) Your school (2) Your place of worship (3) A Scouting event or campsite (4) A public exhibit or attraction (such as a theater, museum, or park)
