pamphlet_excerpts: Tailored Individual Accommodations: An accommodation is just a different way of doing things that is tailored to the individual needs of a person with a disability (p. 36).
Classroom Learning Accommodations: Most schools are accommodating students with disabilities to make learning better (p. 36).
Workplace and Attraction Supports: Accommodations also happen in workplaces to make work easier and in public attractions to make experiences more enjoyable (p. 36).
Evaluating and Improving Accommodations: For requirement 4b, you are to identify accommodations that already exist at certain places and suggest better accommodations (p. 36).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Workplace Supports: Accommodations also happen in workplaces to make work easier and in public attractions to make experiences more enjoyable (p. 36).
Step 2 - Document Existing Facility Accommodations: For requirement 4b, you are to identify accommodations that already exist at certain places and suggest better accommodations (p. 36).

Step 3 - Interview On-Site Staff Members: You will need to talk with staff members at the locations or facilities to help you understand the accommodations, because they often are not obvious (p. 36).
Step 4 - Inspect Public Site Usability: Next time you are in a public place, look at how accessible (usable) the location is for people with disabilities (p. 36).

pamphlet_excerpts: Harm of Mistaken Stereotypes: We are all hurt by mistaken ideas and misunderstandings about people with disabilities and what they can and cannot (p. 19).
Sharing Accurate Factual Information: Learn the facts so you can share the correct information with others (p. 19).
Disability Versus Illness Distinction: Having a disability is not the same as being sick (p. 19).
Health and Athletic Strength: Many people with disabilities are in excellent physical condition, healthy, athletic, and strong (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Separate Disability From Illness: Having a disability is not the same as being sick (p. 19).
Step 2 - Recognize Physical Fitness: Many people with disabilities are in excellent physical condition, healthy, athletic, and strong (p. 19).
Step 3 - Distinguish Temporary Medical Conditions: Some people who have disabilities also have illnesses, just as some nondisabled people are ill (p. 19).
Step 4 - Refute Quality-of-Life Myths: A person with a disability has a poor quality of life or lives a life totally different from people without disabilities (p. 19).

pamphlet_excerpts: Core Meaning of Advocacy: Advocacy, Attitudes, and Awareness Advocacy means supporting, promoting, encouraging, or defending something (p. 44).
Promoting Positive Community Attitudes: To be an advocate for people with disabilities means you support and encourage positive attitudes about people with disabilities (p. 44).
Courage to Challenge Mistreatment: It can also mean that you are brave enough to challenge false and unfair beliefs or call to account those who mistreat people with disabilities (p. 44).
Removing Stereotypical Labels: You help strip away the labels so that people can see each other as individuals (p. 44).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Challenge Unfair Beliefs Bravely: It can also mean that you are brave enough to challenge false and unfair beliefs or call to account those who mistreat people with disabilities (p. 44).
Step 2 - Look Past Stereotypical Labels: You help strip away the labels so that people can see each other as individuals (p. 44).
Step 3 - Build Mutual Respect Daily: You help build bridges of understanding and respect among all people, regardless of their abilities (p. 44).
Step 4 - Teach Awareness to Others: In completing the requirements for the Disabilities Awareness merit badge, you have learned things that you can now teach to others (p. 44).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Disabilities Awareness Requirement 1, what is the respectful standard when communicating with or referring to a person with a disability, and why is it important to recognize invisible disabilities?
options: A. Speak only to the person's companion or interpreter in a loud voice, and assume anyone who does not use a wheelchair has no disability.
B. Push a person's wheelchair or grab a blind person's white cane without asking so you can move them through doorways faster.

C. Speak directly to the individual using respectful people-first or preferred language, ask before offering physical assistance, and recognize that many disabilities (such as autism, epilepsy, diabetes, hearing loss, or learning differences) are not immediately visible.
D. Avoid inviting Scouts with physical or sensory disabilities on campouts so the troop does not have to adjust trail plans.

pamphlet_excerpts: AKC Recognized Breed Groups: The groups, and many of the breeds within these groups, recognized by the AKC are as follows (p. 12).
Sporting Group Hunting Skills: These are dogs that "scent" and either track, point, or flush (reveal a bird's location and cause it to fly), and retrieve game birds on land or in water (p. 12).
Controlled Breeding and Selection: The wide range of shape, size, color, and personality of purebred dogs is the result of controlled breeding and selection (p. 12).
Specialized Working Canine Roles: Some dogs were bred to hunt, some to serve as guard or sled dogs, and some to be herders (p. 12).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Examine Selective Breeding Traits: The wide range of shape, size, color, and personality of purebred dogs is the result of controlled breeding and selection (p. 12).
Step 2 - Identify Traditional Canine Jobs: Some dogs were bred to hunt, some to serve as guard or sled dogs, and some to be herders (p. 12).
Step 3 - Classify Breeds by Function: In the late 1800s, at the same time that dog shows we regaining popularity, a system was developed for classifying breeds according to how they are used (p. 12).
Step 4 - Review AKC Registry Standards: In the United States, the American Kennel Club has maintained a registry of breeds since 1884 (p. 12).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
quiz_item.question: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
options: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
choices: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Stiff muscles, pinned ears, tucked tail, showing the whites of the eyes ('whale eye'), yawning/lip-licking under tension, and growling are clear canine warning signs of fear or defensiveness.

pamphlet_excerpts: Introducing Light Leash Pressure: After the dog is used to the leash, take up your end of it and walk around with your pet, applying little or no pressure (p. 37).
Building Leash Comfort Gradually: Gradually, over a short period, increase your control until your dog is completely comfortable being on the leash (p. 37).
Frequent Short Training Sessions: Multiple, short periods of training are most effective (p. 37).
Ideal Puppy Session Length: Four or five sessions a day, five to 10 minutes each, works well for puppies (p. 37).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Schedule Frequent Short Practice: Multiple, short periods of training are most effective (p. 37).
Step 2 - Limit Puppy Lessons: Four or five sessions a day, five to 10 minutes each, works well for puppies (p. 37).
Step 3 - Extend Adult Dog Sessions: Older dogs can tolerate sessions of up to 20 minutes long (p. 37).
Step 4 - Work Toward Good Citizen: The American Kennel Club's Canine Good Citizen® certification program rewards dogs that have good manners at home and in the community (p. 37).

Unusual Energy and Restlessness: Your active dog might be listless or your relaxed one restless (p. 55).
Appetite and Thirst Changes: Your dog might stop eating or start drinking a lot more water than usual (p. 55).
Irregular Digestive Habits: Bowel movements and feces might become irregular (p. 55).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Monitor Food and Water: Your dog might stop eating or start drinking a lot more water than usual (p. 55).
Step 2 - Check Daily Bowel Habits: Bowel movements and feces might become irregular (p. 55).
Step 3 - Inspect Early Illness Symptoms: If you think your dog is sick, take a closer look (p. 55).
Step 4 - Take Inner Thigh Pulse: You can a check a dog's pulse on the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh near where the leg meets the belly (p. 55).

requirements.description: Do the following: (a) Discuss the proper vaccination schedule for a dog in your area from puppyhood through adulthood. (b) Discuss the control methods for preventing fleas, ticks, heartworms, and intestinal parasites (worms) for a dog in your area from puppyhood through adulthood. (c) Explain the importance of dental care and tooth brushing to your pet's health. (d) Discuss the benefits of grooming your dog's coat and nails on a regular basis. (e) Discuss with your counselor any seasonal conditions (like hot summers, cold winters, or extreme humidity) where you live that need to be considered for your dog. (f) Discuss with your counselor the considerations and advantages of spaying or neutering your dog.

pamphlet_excerpts: Nationwide Heartworm Disease Risk: Keeping Your Dog Healthy. heartworm society. org Heart worm disease can affect dogs in every state (p. 57).
Intestinal Parasite Transmission Routes: In adult dogs most intestinal parasites are picked up from the stool of an infected dog (except tapeworms, which are spread by fleas) (p. 57).
Biannual Fecal Screening Checks: Because this can easily happen when dogs are sniffing around outside, adult dogs should also have a stool check a couple of times a year to screen (p. 57).
Microscopic Internal Parasite Detection: Remember, most internal parasites are not visible to the nakedeye, so don't assume they are not a problem just because you don't see them (p. 57).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Schedule Fecal Screening Checks: Because this can easily happen when dogs are sniffing around outside, adult dogs should also have a stool check a couple of times a year to screen (p. 57).
Step 2 - Screen for Hidden Parasites: Remember, most internal parasites are not visible to the nakedeye, so don't assume they are not a problem just because you don't see them (p. 57).
Step 3 - Prevent Mosquito Heartworm Bites: Dogs can get heart worms through the bite of a mosquito that carries the parasite (p. 57).
Step 4 - Test Early for Heartworms: A dog might be infected for a longtime before you know about it because it takes awhile for the worms to cause damage to the dog's heart (p. 57).

pamphlet_excerpts: Mia cis Early Carnivore Ancestor: The origin of dogs can be traced to an animal called Mia cis, which looked more like a weasel than a dog (p. 9).
Prehistoric Carnivore Physical Traits: This small, flesh-eating creature had short legs, a long tail, five toes, and teeth like those of today's carnivores (p. 9).
Cynodictis Canine Dentition Traits: The next important ancestor, called Cynodictis was the first to have doglikecharacteristics, such as a shortened fifth toe, 42 teeth, and longer legs (p. 9).
Tomarctus Modern Dog Resemblance: Then came a descendent of Cynodictis, called Tomarctus, which resembled today's dogs (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trace Early Canine Dentition: The next important ancestor, called Cynodictis was the first to have doglikecharacteristics, such as a shortened fifth toe, 42 teeth, and longer legs (p. 9).
Step 2 - Compare Tomarctus Physical Features: Then came a descendent of Cynodictis, called Tomarctus, which resembled today's dogs (p. 9).
Step 3 - Identify Evolved Dewclaw Anatomy: This animal had short, erect ears, long legs and tail, and adewclaw that had developed from the shortened fifth toe (p. 9).
Step 4 - Observe Modern Canine Instincts: Also, Tomarctus probably behaved much like today's dogs (p. 9).

Step 3 - Teach Owners and Dogs: Professional dog trainers train dogs to respond to commands and instruct people to train and handle their dogs (p. 74).

Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (b) Identify how you might use the skills and knowledge in working with dogs to pursue a personal hobby and/or healthy lifestyle. Research the additional training required, expenses, and affiliation with organizations that would help you maximize the enjoyment and benefit you might gain from it. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and share what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
options: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
choices: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Stiff muscles, pinned ears, tucked tail, showing the whites of the eyes ('whale eye'), yawning/lip-licking under tension, and growling are clear canine warning signs of fear or defensiveness.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does the typical lifespan of a small or medium dog compare to that of a large dog?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does the typical lifespan of a small or medium dog compare to that of a large dog?
options: A. Small and medium dogs live about 15 years, while large dogs typically live nine to 12 years
B. Large dogs live 18 to 20 years, while small dogs average eight to 10 years
C. All dog breeds share the same 12-year average lifespan regardless of body size
D. Medium dogs live half as long as giant working breeds
choices: A. Small and medium dogs live about 15 years, while large dogs typically live nine to 12 years
B. Large dogs live 18 to 20 years, while small dogs average eight to 10 years
C. All dog breeds share the same 12-year average lifespan regardless of body size
D. Medium dogs live half as long as giant working breeds
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Small and medium dogs live about 15 years, while large dogs typically live nine to 12 years
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Body size strongly affects canine longevity: small and medium dogs live around 15 years, whereas large dogs generally live nine to 12 years (p. 27).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the Dog Care merit badge pamphlet, what is the primary goal of training a family pet?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the Dog Care merit badge pamphlet, what is the primary goal of training a family pet?
options: A. Preparing the dog to win competitive agility ribbons
B. Teaching the dog complex police apprehension and scent-detection routines
C. Helping your dog fit in safely and happily with your family and society
D. Eliminating the dog's natural instinct to bark or play
choices: A. Preparing the dog to win competitive agility ribbons
B. Teaching the dog complex police apprehension and scent-detection routines
C. Helping your dog fit in safely and happily with your family and society
D. Eliminating the dog's natural instinct to bark or play
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Helping your dog fit in safely and happily with your family and society
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): While some dogs learn specialized service or police work, the fundamental goal of training your pet is helping it fit in safely with you, your family's activities, and the broader community (p. 35).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why does dry kibble provide more nutrition pound for pound than canned dog food?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why does dry kibble provide more nutrition pound for pound than canned dog food?
options: A. Canned food contains no protein or fat
B. Dry kibble is fortified with medicine while canned food is only for treats
C. Canned food is mostly water, even though it is more flavorful
D. Dogs cannot digest cooked meat in canned formulas
choices: A. Canned food contains no protein or fat
B. Dry kibble is fortified with medicine while canned food is only for treats
C. Canned food is mostly water, even though it is more flavorful
D. Dogs cannot digest cooked meat in canned formulas
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Canned food is mostly water, even though it is more flavorful
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Canned dog foods are very flavorful, but because they are mostly water, they deliver less nutrition pound for pound than dry kibble (p. 43).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What training schedule works best when teaching basic obedience commands to a puppy?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What training schedule works best when teaching basic obedience commands to a puppy?
options: A. One 60-minute session every Saturday morning
B. Two 45-minute drills each day before meals
C. Continuous training for two hours until the puppy masters every command
D. Four or five short sessions a day lasting five to 10 minutes each
choices: A. One 60-minute session every Saturday morning
B. Two 45-minute drills each day before meals
C. Continuous training for two hours until the puppy masters every command
D. Four or five short sessions a day lasting five to 10 minutes each
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Four or five short sessions a day lasting five to 10 minutes each
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Puppies have short attention spans, so four or five brief sessions per day of five to 10 minutes each are most effective, while older dogs can handle up to 20 minutes (p. 37).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Where on a dog's body should you place your fingers to check its pulse?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Where on a dog's body should you place your fingers to check its pulse?
options: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
B. On the tip of the muzzle right behind the nose pad
C. At the base of the tail on the top of the spine
D. Under the front paw pads between the toes
choices: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
B. On the tip of the muzzle right behind the nose pad
C. At the base of the tail on the top of the spine
D. Under the front paw pads between the toes
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. On the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh where the leg meets the belly
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The femoral artery runs close to the skin on the inside of the hind leg, high on the inner thigh near the belly, making it the best spot to feel a dog's pulse (p. 55).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How are heartworms and tapeworms transmitted to dogs?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How are heartworms and tapeworms transmitted to dogs?
options: A. Both are spread directly through coughing at dog parks
B. Heartworms are spread by mosquito bites, while tapeworms are spread by fleas
C. Heartworms come from drinking puddle water, while tapeworms come from ticks
D. Both are inherited only from an infected mother before birth
choices: A. Both are spread directly through coughing at dog parks
B. Heartworms are spread by mosquito bites, while tapeworms are spread by fleas
C. Heartworms come from drinking puddle water, while tapeworms come from ticks
D. Both are inherited only from an infected mother before birth
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Heartworms are spread by mosquito bites, while tapeworms are spread by fleas
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dogs contract heartworms from the bite of an infected mosquito, while tapeworms are transmitted when a dog swallows an infected flea (p. 57).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which prehistoric ancestor was the first to develop dog like features such as longer legs, a shortened fifth toe, and 42 teeth?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which prehistoric ancestor was the first to develop dog like features such as longer legs, a shortened fifth toe, and 42 teeth?
options: A. Mia cis
B. Eohippus
C. Cynodictis
D. Archaeopteryx
choices: A. Mia cis
B. Eohippus
C. Cynodictis
D. Archaeopteryx
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Cynodictis
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Cynodictis evolved from Mia cis and was the first ancestor to display distinct dog like features including longer legs, a shortened fifth toe, and 42 teeth (p. 9).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What are the two main functions of the thick pads on the bottom of a dog's paws?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What are the two main functions of the thick pads on the bottom of a dog's paws?
options: A. Releasing sweat to cool the body and gripping tree bark
B. Cushioning the impact of running and muffling noise
C. Detecting underground heartworms and storing fat for winter
D. Anchoring the dewclaw and lengthening the stride
choices: A. Releasing sweat to cool the body and gripping tree bark
B. Cushioning the impact of running and muffling noise
C. Detecting underground heartworms and storing fat for winter
D. Anchoring the dewclaw and lengthening the stride
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Cushioning the impact of running and muffling noise
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A dog's paw pads act as shock absorbers to cushion the impact of running while also muffling footsteps as the dog moves (p. 30).

options: A. Performing surgical procedures at veterinary hospitals
B. Instructing people on how to train and handle their own dogs
C. Issuing municipal dog licenses and enforcing local leash laws
D. Manufacturing commercial dry kibble formulas
choices: A. Performing surgical procedures at veterinary hospitals
B. Instructing people on how to train and handle their own dogs
C. Issuing municipal dog licenses and enforcing local leash laws
D. Manufacturing commercial dry kibble formulas
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Instructing people on how to train and handle their own dogs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Professional dog trainers not only teach dogs to obey commands but also instruct owners so they can effectively train and handle their pets at home (p. 74).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Drafting Requirement 1, how does third-angle orthographic projection represent a three-dimensional object on a flat drawing sheet, and how are object lines distinguished from hidden lines?
quiz_item.question: In Drafting Requirement 1, how does third-angle orthographic projection represent a three-dimensional object on a flat drawing sheet, and how are object lines distinguished from hidden lines?
options: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.

D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
choices: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.

D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Orthographic projection aligns multiple 2D views (typically front, top, and right side) to convey exact geometry to scale, using a standardized alphabet of lines where visible edges are thick solid lines and hidden edges are dashed.

requirements.lead_text: Using the formatted sheet of paper you prepared for your manual project, produce a pencil drawing as it would be used for manufacturing. Fill in all title block information. The manual drawing may be any one of the following drawing types:
requirements.req_text: Using the formatted sheet of paper you prepared for your manual project, produce a pencil drawing as it would be used for manufacturing. Fill in all title block information. The manual drawing may be any one of the following drawing types: (a) Architectural: Make a scale drawing of an architectural project. The architectural drawing may be a floor plan; electrical, plumbing, or mechanical service plan; elevation plan; or landscaping plan. Use an architect's scale and show dimensions to communicate the actual size of features. Include any important sectional drawings, notes, and considerations necessary for construction. Properly print a bill of materials for at least three of the raw materials or components in the project. (b) Mechanical: Make a scale drawing of some mechanical device or interesting object. The mechanical drawing may be of the orthographic (third-angle) or isometric style. Use an engineer's scale and show dimensions to communicate the actual size of features. Include any important sectional drawings, notes, and manufacturing considerations. Properly print a bill of materials for at least three of the raw materials or components in the assembly. (c) Electrical: Draw a simple schematic of a radio or electronic circuit. Properly print a bill of materials including all of the major electrical components used in the circuit. Use standard drawing symbols to represent the electronic components.

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a facility or industry workplace where drafting is part of the business. Ask to see an example of the work that is done there, the different drafting facilities, and the tools used. (1) Find out how much of the drafting done there is manual and how much is done using CAD. If CAD is used, find out what software is used and how and why it was chosen. (2) Ask about the drafting services provided. Ask who uses the designs produced in the drafting area and how those designs are used. Discuss how the professionals who perform drafting cooperate with other individuals in the drafting area and other areas of the business. (3) Ask how important the role of drafting is to producing the end product or service that this business supplies. Find out how drafting contributes to the company's end product or service. (b) Using resources you find on your own such as at the library and on the internet (with your parent or guardian's permission), learn more about the drafting trade and discuss the following with your counselor. (1) The drafting tools used in the past, why and how they were used. Explain which tools are still used today and how their use has changed with the advent of new tools. Discuss which tools are being made obsolete by newer tools in the industry. (2) Tell what media types were used in the past and how drawings were used, stored, and reproduced. Tell how the advent of CAD has changed the media used, and discuss how these changes affect the storage or reproduction of drawings. (3) Discuss whether the types of media have changed such that there are new uses the drawings, or other outputs, produced by designers. Briefly discuss how new media types are used in the industry today.

sub_requirements.text: Using resources you find on your own such as at the library and on the internet (with your parent or guardian's permission), learn more about the drafting trade and discuss the following with your counselor. pamphlet_excerpts: Compact Computer Workstation Footprint: Computers take up less space than the drafting boards needed for manual drafting (p. 16).
Modern Engineering Office Layouts: This allows engineering offices, for example, to be filled with normal-size desks and work spaces, instead of needing a large room filled (p. 16).
Company-Wide Drawing Style Consistency: With CAD, all designers in the same company can produce drawings with the same style of lettering and drawing (p. 16).
Uniform Multi-Designer Project Output: This allows all jobs to have a common feel to them instead of reflecting a mix of styles depending on which designer worked on the project (p. 16).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Standardized Company Templates: With CAD, all designers in the same company can produce drawings with the same style of lettering and drawing (p. 16).
Step 2 - Examine Team Collaboration Standards: This allows all jobs to have a common feel to them instead of reflecting a mix of styles depending on which designer worked on the project (p. 16).
Step 3 - Review Digital Printing Workflows: Specialized printers and papers are not needed with CAD (p. 16).
Step 4 - Discuss Document Output Methods: You can simply print out a design as you would any other document created on a computer (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Drafting Requirement 1, how does third-angle orthographic projection represent a three-dimensional object on a flat drawing sheet, and how are object lines distinguished from hidden lines?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Drafting Requirement 1, how does third-angle orthographic projection represent a three-dimensional object on a flat drawing sheet, and how are object lines distinguished from hidden lines?
options: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.

D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
choices: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.

D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Orthographic projection aligns multiple 2D views (typically front, top, and right side) to convey exact geometry to scale, using a standardized alphabet of lines where visible edges are thick solid lines and hidden edges are dashed.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Regardless of whether you choose an architectural, mechanical, or electrical format for your manual project, what information do all standard drawing formats share?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Regardless of whether you choose an architectural, mechanical, or electrical format for your manual project, what information do all standard drawing formats share?
options: A. A list of retail prices for every tool used by the drafter
B. Full-color perspective renderings of the finished building or device
C. The drawing's name or identification number, the date drawn, and the designer's name
D. A wiring schematic paired with a plumbing elevation plan
choices: A. A list of retail prices for every tool used by the drafter
B. Full-color perspective renderings of the finished building or device
C. The drawing's name or identification number, the date drawn, and the designer's name
D. A wiring schematic paired with a plumbing elevation plan
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The drawing's name or identification number, the date drawn, and the designer's name
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): All standard drafting formats convey essential identification details in the title block, including the drawing name or number, the date it was drawn, and the designer's name (p. 24).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: When producing a CAD drawing for manufacturing under Requirement 3, which element must be completed regardless of the discipline you choose?
options: A. All title block information, including the drawing identification, date, and designer's name
B. A hand-lettered border drawn with a mechanical pencil after printing
C. A three-dimensional animation of the manufacturing assembly line
D. A separate soil survey for the factory building
choices: A. All title block information, including the drawing identification, date, and designer's name
B. A hand-lettered border drawn with a mechanical pencil after printing
C. A three-dimensional animation of the manufacturing assembly line
D. A separate soil survey for the factory building
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. All title block information, including the drawing identification, date, and designer's name
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Just like manual drawings, CAD drawings used in manufacturing require a complete title block showing the drawing's name or number, date, and designer's name (p. 25).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why must a drafter check multiple orthographic views when updating a dimension during a redline revision?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why must a drafter check multiple orthographic views when updating a dimension during a redline revision?
options: A. Because each single view shows all three dimensions at once
B. Because side views are drawn at twice the scale of front views
C. Because revision blocks can only be placed inside the side view
D. Because each view gives only two-dimensional information and shares dimensions with adjacent views
choices: A. Because each single view shows all three dimensions at once
B. Because side views are drawn at twice the scale of front views
C. Because revision blocks can only be placed inside the side view
D. Because each view gives only two-dimensional information and shares dimensions with adjacent views
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Because each view gives only two-dimensional information and shares dimensions with adjacent views
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Each orthographic view provides only two-dimensional information, and dimensions such as width and length appear across paired views like the front, side, and top views (p. 22).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the Drafting merit badge pamphlet, how precise can a computer-aided drafting (CAD) system be when depicting lines and features?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the Drafting merit badge pamphlet, how precise can a computer-aided drafting (CAD) system be when depicting lines and features?
options: A. Accurate only to the nearest sixteenth of an inch
B. Accurate to units of millionths of an inch or even smaller
C. Exactly the same accuracy as a sharpened 2H wooden pencil
D. Accurate only to the nearest millimeter
choices: A. Accurate only to the nearest sixteenth of an inch
B. Accurate to units of millionths of an inch or even smaller
C. Exactly the same accuracy as a sharpened 2H wooden pencil
D. Accurate only to the nearest millimeter
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Accurate to units of millionths of an inch or even smaller
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Computers running CAD software can depict lines and features in units of millionths of an inch or even smaller (p. 15).

requirements.req_text: Demonstrate that you know how to respond to electrical emergencies by doing the following: (a) Explain how to turn off power for a particular circuit and the whole house in the event of an emergency. (b) Demonstrate how to rescue a person touching a live wire in the home. (c) Describe how to safely get out of a car in an accident if you suspect a utility wire is on the car. (d) Show how to render first aid to a person who is unconscious from an apparent electrical shock. (e) Show how to treat an electrical burn. (f) Explain what to do in the event of an electrical fire. (g) Explain what to do if caught out in the open during an electrical storm.

pamphlet_excerpts: Using the Recovery Position: Place a victim who is unconscious but who is breathing normally in a recovery position (p. 46).
Keeping the Airway Clear: This will prevent the person from choking on saliva, blood (from a bitten tongue), or vomit, and will help keep the airway open (p. 46).
Monitoring Victim Breathing: Continue to monitor the person's breathing until medical help arrives (p. 46).
Spinal Injury Precautions: However, do not move a person with suspected spinal injury unless it is absolutely necessary (p. 46).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Monitor Breathing Continuously: Continue to monitor the person's breathing until medical help arrives (p. 46).
Step 2 - Protect Suspected Spinal Injuries: However, do not move a person with suspected spinal injury unless it is absolutely necessary (p. 46).
Step 3 - Position Victim Carefully: Recovery position for a person who may have a spinal injury (p. 46).
Step 4 - Locate Main Power Feeds: Electric current comes into your home on overhead or underground wires (p. 46).

options: A. Grab the victim's bare shoulders with both hands and pull them briskly away from the wire before calling 911.

B. Do not touch the victim with bare hands; immediately disconnect the power source by shutting off the main circuit breaker or unplugging the cord (or use a dry, nonconductive wooden pole if power cannot be shut off), then call 911 and check for breathing.
C. Throw a bucket of tap water over the extension cord to cool the sparks and extinguish the electrical arc.
D. Use a metal pry bar to lift the live copper wire off the person's hand while standing on a damp garage floor.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why is it important to check for outlets that have loose-fitting plugs during your home electrical safety inspection?
quiz_item.question: Why is it important to check for outlets that have loose-fitting plugs during your home electrical safety inspection?
options: A. Loose plugs reduce the voltage frequency from 60 hertz to 30 hertz
B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
C. Loose plugs cause the household electric meter to spin backward
D. Loose-fitting plugs convert alternating current into direct current
choices: A. Loose plugs reduce the voltage frequency from 60 hertz to 30 hertz
B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
C. Loose plugs cause the household electric meter to spin backward
D. Loose-fitting plugs convert alternating current into direct current
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Outlets with loose-fitting plugs create resistance and arcing at the contact points, which can overheat and lead to a fire (p. 51).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What causes the striker in a standard DC electric bell to move back and forth repeatedly instead of striking the gong just once?
quiz_item.question: What causes the striker in a standard DC electric bell to move back and forth repeatedly instead of striking the gong just once?
options: A. The battery rapidly reverses its positive and negative terminals
B. The homeowner must tap the push button dozens of times per second
C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
D. The metal gong repels the iron striker as soon as they touch
choices: A. The battery rapidly reverses its positive and negative terminals
B. The homeowner must tap the push button dozens of times per second
C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
D. The metal gong repels the iron striker as soon as they touch
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): When the electromagnet pulls the striker toward the gong, the armature breaks contact with the interrupter screw, shutting off the magnetism so the spring pulls the armature back to repeat the cycle (p. 49).

pamphlet_excerpts: Overhead and Underground Service: Electric current comes into your home on overhead or underground wires (p. 46).
Main Distribution Breaker Box: From your electrical meter, heavy, well-insulated wires run to a main distribution center or breaker box, where the main disconnect switch is located (p. 46).
Main Power Disconnect Switch: If necessary, you can use that switch to shut off all electric current in your house (p. 46).
Finding the Breaker Panel: The fuse box or circuit breaker panel is typically located in a utility room, in an electric room, in a mechanical room, or near the main power feed (p. 46).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Use Main Disconnect Switch: If necessary, you can use that switch to shut off all electric current in your house (p. 46).
Step 2 - Locate the Breaker Panel: The fuse box or circuit breaker panel is typically located in a utility room, in an electric room, in a mechanical room, or near the main power feed (p. 46).
Step 3 - Block Excessive Branch Currents: They prevent currents that are too strong from traveling into your home's branch circuits (p. 46).

requirements.lead_text: Do TWO of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Connect a buzzer, bell, or light with a battery. Have a key or switch in the line. (b) Make and run a simple electric motor (from a kit is acceptable, if approved by your counselor ahead of time). (c) Build a simple rheostat. Show that it works. (d) Build a single-pole, double-throw switch. Show that it works. (e) Explain how 3-way switch wiring works in a lighting circuit. (f) Connect two lights together in a series circuit along with a battery and a switch. Then connect the same circuit in parallel. Discuss the differences in the two circuits.

pamphlet_excerpts: Defective or Frayed Cords: One common cause for a blown fuse or tripped circuit breaker is a defective or frayed cord (p. 48).
Worn Insulation Short Circuits: Insulation wears off and the bare wires short-circuit (p. 48).
Warning Signs of Shorts: A flash of light and a smell of burning insulation indicate a short circuit (p. 48).
Low Resistance Current Surge: Since the current suddenly encounters lower resistance, more current transfers, and that blows a fuse or trips the circuit breaker (p. 48).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Watch for Short Circuit Signs: A flash of light and a smell of burning insulation indicate a short circuit (p. 48).
Step 2 - Prevent Low-Resistance Current Surges: Since the current suddenly encounters lower resistance, more current transfers, and that blows a fuse or trips the circuit breaker (p. 48).
Step 3 - Push Breaker Handle: Some circuit breakers used in homes are the push-push type; others have a handle that must be pushed to the off position before the breaker (p. 48).
Step 4 - Follow Panel Reset Instructions: Follow the instructions on your home's circuit breaker panel to properly reset whatever type (p. 48).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What happens when you connect two lamps in a parallel circuit with a battery and then unscrew one of the lamps?
quiz_item.question: What happens when you connect two lamps in a parallel circuit with a battery and then unscrew one of the lamps?
options: A. Both lamps go out immediately because the single loop is broken
B. The remaining lamp stays lit because parallel branches provide independent paths for current
C. The battery short-circuits and melts the switch
D. The remaining lamp flickers at 60 cycles per second
choices: A. Both lamps go out immediately because the single loop is broken
B. The remaining lamp stays lit because parallel branches provide independent paths for current
C. The battery short-circuits and melts the switch
D. The remaining lamp flickers at 60 cycles per second
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. The remaining lamp stays lit because parallel branches provide independent paths for current
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In a parallel circuit, each lamp has its own branch path connected across the battery, so removing one bulb does not interrupt current to the other bulb (p. 49).

pamphlet_excerpts: General Electrical Industry Areas: The electrical industry has several general areas with many types of careers available in each area (p. 73).
Manufacturing Construction and Engineering: These areas include manufacturing, construction, merchandising, operating, servicing or maintaining, and engineering electrical parts, equipment (p. 73).
College and Vocational Education: Some positions require a college degree, while a degree from a vocational school is adequate for other careers (p. 73).
Diploma and Training Requirements: Some companies allow on-the-job training, but almost all require at least a high school diploma (p. 73).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Compare Degree and Trade Paths: Some positions require a college degree, while a degree from a vocational school is adequate for other careers (p. 73).
Step 2 - Complete High School Education: Some companies allow on-the-job training, but almost all require at least a high school diploma (p. 73).
Step 3 - Explore Power Generation Stations: In electricity manufacturing (electrical generating stations, transmission, and distribution substation systems) positions are available (p. 73).
Step 4 - Research Electrical Equipment Assembly: Occupations include assemblers, that is, the people who help build electrical equipment and/or systems (p. 73).

quiz_item.question: Which statement accurately describes the education and training requirements across different careers in the electrical industry?
options: A. Every job in the electrical industry requires a master's degree in physics
B. No formal schooling or high school diploma is needed for any electrical career
C. Some positions require a college degree, while vocational schooling and on-the-job training prepare workers for other electrical careers
D. Only power plant operators are required to learn electrical safety rules
choices: A. Every job in the electrical industry requires a master's degree in physics
B. No formal schooling or high school diploma is needed for any electrical career
C. Some positions require a college degree, while vocational schooling and on-the-job training prepare workers for other electrical careers
D. Only power plant operators are required to learn electrical safety rules
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Some positions require a college degree, while vocational schooling and on-the-job training prepare workers for other electrical careers
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The electrical industry includes roles requiring a university degree as well as skilled trade positions where vocational training, apprenticeships, and a high school diploma provide entry (p. 73).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: You discover a person in contact with a damaged, live 120-volt extension cord who is unable to let go due to muscular tet any. According to Electricity Requirement 1, what must you do first?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: You discover a person in contact with a damaged, live 120-volt extension cord who is unable to let go due to muscular tet any. According to Electricity Requirement 1, what must you do first?
options: A. Grab the victim's bare shoulders with both hands and pull them briskly away from the wire before calling 911.

B. Do not touch the victim with bare hands; immediately disconnect the power source by shutting off the main circuit breaker or unplugging the cord (or use a dry, nonconductive wooden pole if power cannot be shut off), then call 911 and check for breathing.
C. Throw a bucket of tap water over the extension cord to cool the sparks and extinguish the electrical arc.
D. Use a metal pry bar to lift the live copper wire off the person's hand while standing on a damp garage floor.
choices: A. Grab the victim's bare shoulders with both hands and pull them briskly away from the wire before calling 911.

B. Do not touch the victim with bare hands; immediately disconnect the power source by shutting off the main circuit breaker or unplugging the cord (or use a dry, nonconductive wooden pole if power cannot be shut off), then call 911 and check for breathing.
C. Throw a bucket of tap water over the extension cord to cool the sparks and extinguish the electrical arc.
D. Use a metal pry bar to lift the live copper wire off the person's hand while standing on a damp garage floor.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Do not touch the victim with bare hands; immediately disconnect the power source by shutting off the main circuit breaker or unplugging the cord (or use a dry, nonconductive wooden pole if power cannot be shut off), then call 911 and check for breathing.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Touching an electrocuted victim while they are still energized will pass lethal current through the rescuer; always de-energize the circuit at the breaker or plug (or separate with a dry nonconductor) before rendering first aid.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is it important to check for outlets that have loose-fitting plugs during your home electrical safety inspection?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is it important to check for outlets that have loose-fitting plugs during your home electrical safety inspection?
options: A. Loose plugs reduce the voltage frequency from 60 hertz to 30 hertz
B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
C. Loose plugs cause the household electric meter to spin backward
D. Loose-fitting plugs convert alternating current into direct current
choices: A. Loose plugs reduce the voltage frequency from 60 hertz to 30 hertz
B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
C. Loose plugs cause the household electric meter to spin backward
D. Loose-fitting plugs convert alternating current into direct current
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Loose-fitting plugs can overheat and start an electrical fire
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Outlets with loose-fitting plugs create resistance and arcing at the contact points, which can overheat and lead to a fire (p. 51).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens when you close the circuit in a simple electromagnet wrapped around a tube containing a compass?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens when you close the circuit in a simple electromagnet wrapped around a tube containing a compass?
options: A. The electric current produces magnetism in the coil and deflects the compass needle
B. The cardboard tube becomes an electrical conductor that powers the compass
C. The compass needle loses its magnetism permanently
D. The plastic insulation melts off the wire immediately
choices: A. The electric current produces magnetism in the coil and deflects the compass needle
B. The cardboard tube becomes an electrical conductor that powers the compass
C. The compass needle loses its magnetism permanently
D. The plastic insulation melts off the wire immediately
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. The electric current produces magnetism in the coil and deflects the compass needle
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Closing the circuit allows electric current to flow through the coiled wire, producing a magnetic field that deflects the compass needle (p. 18).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How many complete cycles per second does ordinary household alternating current experience in the United States?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How many complete cycles per second does ordinary household alternating current experience in the United States?
options: A. 12 cycles per second
B. 60 cycles per second
C. 100 cycles per second
D. 120 cycles per second
choices: A. 12 cycles per second
B. 60 cycles per second
C. 100 cycles per second
D. 120 cycles per second
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. 60 cycles per second
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Ordinary household alternating current completes 60 cycles of forward and backward flow every second, which is 60 hertz (p. 28).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What causes the striker in a standard DC electric bell to move back and forth repeatedly instead of striking the gong just once?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What causes the striker in a standard DC electric bell to move back and forth repeatedly instead of striking the gong just once?
options: A. The battery rapidly reverses its positive and negative terminals
B. The homeowner must tap the push button dozens of times per second
C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
D. The metal gong repels the iron striker as soon as they touch
choices: A. The battery rapidly reverses its positive and negative terminals
B. The homeowner must tap the push button dozens of times per second
C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
D. The metal gong repels the iron striker as soon as they touch
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The armature movement opens a contact point, cutting off current to the electromagnet so a spring pulls it back
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): When the electromagnet pulls the striker toward the gong, the armature breaks contact with the interrupter screw, shutting off the magnetism so the spring pulls the armature back to repeat the cycle (p. 49).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens inside a fuse when the electric current on a circuit becomes greater than the fuse is designed to handle?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens inside a fuse when the electric current on a circuit becomes greater than the fuse is designed to handle?
options: A. A spring-loaded plastic lever flips to the middle position
B. The glass window turns dark blue to warn the homeowner
C. The metal element inside the fuse melts and opens the circuit
D. The fuse increases circuit resistance to slow down the electrons
choices: A. A spring-loaded plastic lever flips to the middle position
B. The glass window turns dark blue to warn the homeowner
C. The metal element inside the fuse melts and opens the circuit
D. The fuse increases circuit resistance to slow down the electrons
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The metal element inside the fuse melts and opens the circuit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): When excessive current flows through a fuse, the calibrated metal strip inside melts and breaks the circuit before the house wiring can overheat (p. 46).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What must your room floor plan wiring diagram show in addition to the locations of all lights, switches, and outlets?

options: A. The exact length in feet of every copper wire inside the walls
B. The monthly kilowatt-hour cost of each individual wall socket
C. Which fuse or circuit breaker protects each light, switch, and outlet
D. The manufacturer name and serial number of every light bulb
choices: A. The exact length in feet of every copper wire inside the walls
B. The monthly kilowatt-hour cost of each individual wall socket
C. Which fuse or circuit breaker protects each light, switch, and outlet
D. The manufacturer name and serial number of every light bulb
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Which fuse or circuit breaker protects each light, switch, and outlet
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Requirement 7 specifies that your floor plan wiring diagram must identify which fuse or circuit breaker protects each light, switch, and outlet in the room (p. 55).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When reading an analog dial electric meter and the pointer is between 9 and 0, which digit should you write down?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When reading an analog dial electric meter and the pointer is between 9 and 0, which digit should you write down?
options: A. Write down 9 because 0 acts as 10 and 9 is the number just passed
B. Write down 0 because 0 is always smaller than 9
C. Write down 10 and add 1 to the dial on the right
D. Round to whichever digit the pointer is closer to touching
choices: A. Write down 9 because 0 acts as 10 and 9 is the number just passed
B. Write down 0 because 0 is always smaller than 9
C. Write down 10 and add 1 to the dial on the right
D. Round to whichever digit the pointer is closer to touching
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Write down 9 because 0 acts as 10 and 9 is the number just passed
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): When a pointer lies between 9 and 0, you treat 9 as smaller than 0 because 0 represents 10, and you always record the number the pointer has just passed (p. 57).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which electrical device converts direct current from a battery or solar panel into alternating current for household appliances?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which electrical device converts direct current from a battery or solar panel into alternating current for household appliances?
options: A. A rectifier
B. A rheostat
C. A capacitor
D. An inverter
choices: A. A rectifier
B. A rheostat
C. A capacitor
D. An inverter
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. An inverter
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): An inverter is a device that converts direct current into alternating current, whereas a rectifier converts alternating current into direct current (p. 29).

options: A. Hold extra solder wire in your mouth while working, lean directly over the rising flux smoke, and rest the hot iron on the workbench mat.
B. Wear wool sweaters to build up static charge, flick excess molten solder off the tip with your wrist, and touch capacitor terminals immediately after unplugging a power supply.

C. Wear ANSI safety glasses to guard against solder splashes, use lead-free rosin-core solder in a well-ventilated area (avoiding flux fumes), return the iron to its heat-resistant stand, wear a grounded ESD wrist strap for static-sensitive chips, and wash hands after working.
D. Dip the hot soldering iron tip into a cup of cold water between joints and test whether the tip is hot by touching it with a fingertip.

options: A. Permanently converting alternating current into mechanical motion
B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
C. Increasing the total voltage of a battery without an oscillator circuit
D. Acting as a sacrificial link that melts when current exceeds a safe limit
choices: A. Permanently converting alternating current into mechanical motion
B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
C. Increasing the total voltage of a battery without an oscillator circuit
D. Acting as a sacrificial link that melts when current exceeds a safe limit
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Capacitors consist of conductive plates separated by an insulator, allowing them to store electrical charge and block direct current (p. 38).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Connect Voltmeter Across Load: The voltmeter is connected across the voltage to be measured (p. 76).
Step 2 - Match Probe Polarity: To measure voltage between two points, touch the negative lead to the more negative point and the positive lead to the more positive point (p. 76).
Step 3 - Keep Circuit Path Intact: The circuit under test need not be broken or interfered with in any way (p. 76).
Step 4 - Read Meter Scale Value: A low voltage can be applied directly to the meter movement (p. 76).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When soldering electronic components onto a printed circuit board for Electronics Requirement 1, which safety practices protect your eyes, lungs, and static-sensitive integrated circuits?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When soldering electronic components onto a printed circuit board for Electronics Requirement 1, which safety practices protect your eyes, lungs, and static-sensitive integrated circuits?
options: A. Hold extra solder wire in your mouth while working, lean directly over the rising flux smoke, and rest the hot iron on the workbench mat.
B. Wear wool sweaters to build up static charge, flick excess molten solder off the tip with your wrist, and touch capacitor terminals immediately after unplugging a power supply.

C. Wear ANSI safety glasses to guard against solder splashes, use lead-free rosin-core solder in a well-ventilated area (avoiding flux fumes), return the iron to its heat-resistant stand, wear a grounded ESD wrist strap for static-sensitive chips, and wash hands after working.
D. Dip the hot soldering iron tip into a cup of cold water between joints and test whether the tip is hot by touching it with a fingertip.
choices: A. Hold extra solder wire in your mouth while working, lean directly over the rising flux smoke, and rest the hot iron on the workbench mat.
B. Wear wool sweaters to build up static charge, flick excess molten solder off the tip with your wrist, and touch capacitor terminals immediately after unplugging a power supply.

C. Wear ANSI safety glasses to guard against solder splashes, use lead-free rosin-core solder in a well-ventilated area (avoiding flux fumes), return the iron to its heat-resistant stand, wear a grounded ESD wrist strap for static-sensitive chips, and wash hands after working.
D. Dip the hot soldering iron tip into a cup of cold water between joints and test whether the tip is hot by touching it with a fingertip.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Wear ANSI safety glasses to guard against solder splashes, use lead-free rosin-core solder in a well-ventilated area (avoiding flux fumes), return the iron to its heat-resistant stand, wear a grounded ESD wrist strap for static-sensitive chips, and wash hands after working.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Electronics safety requires eye protection, fume ventilation, always placing the hot iron in its stand, using electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection for sensitive semiconductors, and washing hands after handling solder.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the primary electrical function of a capacitor in an electronic circuit?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the primary electrical function of a capacitor in an electronic circuit?
options: A. Permanently converting alternating current into mechanical motion
B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
C. Increasing the total voltage of a battery without an oscillator circuit
D. Acting as a sacrificial link that melts when current exceeds a safe limit
choices: A. Permanently converting alternating current into mechanical motion
B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
C. Increasing the total voltage of a battery without an oscillator circuit
D. Acting as a sacrificial link that melts when current exceeds a safe limit
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Capacitors consist of conductive plates separated by an insulator, allowing them to store electrical charge and block direct current (p. 38).

B. Clip a metal heat sink or alligator clip onto the lead between the joint and the component body
C. Dip the soldering iron tip into cold water immediately before touching the solder
D. Use a high-wattage soldering gun and heat the connection for at least twenty seconds
choices: A. Apply acid flux generously and hold the iron against the plastic body

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Clip a metal heat sink or alligator clip onto the lead between the joint and the component body
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Attaching a small metal heat sink or alligator clip to the lead absorbs heat before it reaches the delicate component body (p. 49).

sub_requirements.label: (b)
sub_requirements.text: Using a chart, spreadsheet, or another method approved by your counselor, demonstrate your understanding of each aspect of emergency preparedness listed in requirement 1(a) (prevention, protection, mitigation, response, and recovery) for 10 emergency situations from the list below. Discuss your findings with your counselor. (1) Home stovetop or oven fire (2) Home flammable liquid fire (3) Gas leak in or near a home or with outside cooking (4) Food poisoning (5) Automobile crash (6) Vehicle stalled in the desert (7) Vehicle trapped in a blizzard (8) Backcountry injury (9) Boating or water accident (10) Toxic chemical spills and releases (11) Nuclear power plant emergency (12) Fire or explosion in a public place (13) Violence in a public place (14) Wildland fire (15) Avalanche (snowslide or rockslide) (16) Earthquake (17) Tsunami (18) Major flooding or a flash flood with water outage (19) Hurricane with power outage (20) Tornado (21) Lightning storm.

common_misconception_pair.misconception: Many Scouts confuse prevention and mitigation, assuming both terms simply mean stopping an emergency from happening in the first place.
common_misconception_pair.fact: Prevention focuses on stopping an emergency from occurring at all, whereas mitigation reduces the loss of life and property by lessening the impact of disasters that do happen (p. 22).

pamphlet_excerpts: U.S. Nuclear Power Plants: About 100 nuclear power plants currently operate in the United States (p. 22).

Cascading Natural Disaster Triggers: While there have been few nuclear accidents at these plants, an earthquake and tsunami in March 2011 triggered a serious accident at a nuclear power plant (p. 22).
Exclusion Zone Evacuations: A 12-mile exclusion zone around the plant displaced 78,000 people (p. 22).
Hazardous Radiation Releases: During an emergency at a nuclear facility, radiation can be released that is dangerous to people near the plant (p. 22).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Respect Official Exclusion Zones: A 12-mile exclusion zone around the plant displaced 78,000 people (p. 22).
Step 2 - Recognize Radiation Exposure Risks: During an emergency at a nuclear facility, radiation can be released that is dangerous to people near the plant (p. 22).
Step 3 - Review Plume Exposure Zones: State and local governments have preparedness plans for areas in a 10-mile radius and 50-mile radius from all nuclear power plants (p. 22).
Step 4 - Contact Local Emergency Management: You can get emergency information from the power company that operates the plant or from the local Office of Emergency Management (p. 22).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Emergency Preparedness Requirement 1, emergency management is organized around five mission areas: Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, and Recovery. Which action is an example of Mitigation before a disaster strikes?
quiz_item.question: In Emergency Preparedness Requirement 1, emergency management is organized around five mission areas: Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, and Recovery. Which action is an example of Mitigation before a disaster strikes?
options: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, elevating utilities above flood level, or clearing defensible brush space around a home to reduce future disaster damage.
B. Dispatching search-and-rescue helicopters during the peak of a hurricane to pull stranded residents from rooftops.
C. Applying for long-term federal rebuilding loans six months after a tornado destroys a town business district.
D. Waiting until a wildfire evacuation order is issued to start looking for flashlights, water bottles, and family phone numbers.
choices: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, elevating utilities above flood level, or clearing defensible brush space around a home to reduce future disaster damage.
B. Dispatching search-and-rescue helicopters during the peak of a hurricane to pull stranded residents from rooftops.
C. Applying for long-term federal rebuilding loans six months after a tornado destroys a town business district.
D. Waiting until a wildfire evacuation order is issued to start looking for flashlights, water bottles, and family phone numbers.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Strapping a home water heater to wall studs in an earthquake zone, elevating utilities above flood level, or clearing defensible brush space around a home to reduce future disaster damage.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Mitigation consists of sustained actions taken before an emergency (such as seismic bracing, flood elevation, and fuel reduction) that eliminate or reduce the long-term risk and severity of loss of life and property.

requirements.lead_text: Planning for Family Emergencies. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Planning for Family Emergencies. Do the following: (a) At a family meeting, discuss the situations on the chart you created for requirement 1(b) and make emergency plans for sheltering-in-place and for evacuation of your home. Discuss your family meeting and plans with your counselor. (b) Develop and practice a plan of escape for your family in case of fire in your home. Draw a floor plan with escape routes and a map with a safe meeting place. Discuss your family's home escape plan with your counselor. (c) Using a checklist in the Emergency Preparedness merit badge pamphlet or one approved by your counselor, prepare or inspect a family disaster kit for sheltering-in-place and for evacuation of your home. Review the needs and uses of the items in a kit with your counselor.

requirements.lead_text: Preventing Accidents and Emergencies. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Preventing Accidents and Emergencies. Do ONE of the following: (a) Using a home safety checklist included in the Emergency Preparedness merit badge pamphlet or one approved by your counselor, inspect a home (or a similar building near where you live or at a camp) for safety hazards with the help of an adult. Present your completed checklist to and discuss your findings with your counselor. (b) Develop emergency prevention plans for five family activities outside the home, as approved by your counselor. (Examples are taking a picnic to a park, seeing a movie, attending a worship service, an outing at a beach, traveling to visit a relative, or attending a ball game or concert.) Each plan should include an analysis of possible hazards, proposals to prevent, protect from, mitigate, respond to, and recover from emergencies, and the reasons for the actions that you propose.

Mitigating Home Fire Severity: If a fire does break out, smoke alarms and a preplanned escape route will help mitigate the situation (p. 19).
Reducing Life Safety Consequences: In other words, the emergency is less severe if everyone gets out of the house alive (p. 19).
Automatic Fire Sprinkler Systems: In public buildings such as schools, automatic sprinkler systems can mitigate a fire by keeping it from spreading throughout the building (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Prioritize Rapid Safe Evacuation: In other words, the emergency is less severe if everyone gets out of the house alive (p. 19).
Step 2 - Verify Building Fire Suppression: In public buildings such as schools, automatic sprinkler systems can mitigate a fire by keeping it from spreading throughout the building (p. 19).
Step 3 - Identify Regional Weather Hazards: Let's say you live in an area that has a high tornado risk (p. 19).
Step 4 - Establish Severe Weather Plans: You can protect yourself and your family by recognizing that a tornado emergency could happen and making a plan in case of that emergency (p. 19).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In emergency preparedness, how do automatic sprinkler systems in schools and smoke alarms in homes function when a fire breaks out?
quiz_item.question: In emergency preparedness, how do automatic sprinkler systems in schools and smoke alarms in homes function when a fire breaks out?
options: A. They act as prevention measures by stopping electrical sparks from igniting
B. They serve as mitigation measures by limiting fire spread and helping occupants escape alive
C. They replace the need for a preplanned family escape route
D. They represent the recovery phase of disaster management
choices: A. They act as prevention measures by stopping electrical sparks from igniting
B. They serve as mitigation measures by limiting fire spread and helping occupants escape alive
C. They replace the need for a preplanned family escape route
D. They represent the recovery phase of disaster management
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. They serve as mitigation measures by limiting fire spread and helping occupants escape alive
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Smoke alarms, escape routes, and automatic sprinkler systems mitigate an emergency by keeping the fire from spreading and ensuring occupants get out alive, making the outcome less severe (p. 19).

pamphlet_excerpts: Proactive Public Safety Awareness: As much as possible, be prepared before trouble strikes in public (p. 71).
Locating Public Building Exits: For instance, get into the habit of looking for exits in any public building you enter (p. 71).
Protecting Rescuer Personal Safety: Be aware that in some situations, the best thing to do is to keep yourself safe and possibly leave the scene (p. 71).
Applying First Aid Knowledge: During an emergency, you may help save lives by using your knowledge of first aid and of situations that might be dangerous (p. 71).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Assess Scene Safety First: Be aware that in some situations, the best thing to do is to keep yourself safe and possibly leave the scene (p. 71).
Step 2 - Evaluate Hazards Before Acting: During an emergency, you may help save lives by using your knowledge of first aid and of situations that might be dangerous (p. 71).
Step 3 - Use Nonswimming Water Rescues: Earning the Lifesaving merit badge, for instance, will prepare you to react safely and effectively in the event of water emergencies (p. 71).
Step 4 - Inspect Frayed Electrical Cords: Electrical appliances usually are safe, but eventually wires fray, plugs break, and parts loosen (p. 71).

pamphlet_excerpts: Visual Pilot Body Signals: You can also "talk" to a pilot with body signals (p. 40).
Eleven Standard Body Signals: Learn the 11 standard body signals illustrated in this chapter (p. 40).
Affirmative Aircraft Nose Dip: A pilot says "yes" by dipping the nose of the plane (p. 40).
Aircraft Acknowledgment Wing Rocking: Zigzagging, or fishtailing, the plane means "no." If your message has been understood, the pilot will rock the plane from side to side or flash green (p. 40).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Watch for Nose Dips: A pilot says "yes" by dipping the nose of the plane (p. 40).
Step 2 - Identify Wing Rocking Signals: Zigzagging, or fishtailing, the plane means "no." If your message has been understood, the pilot will rock the plane from side to side or flash green (p. 40).
Step 3 - Repeat Unclear Ground Signals: If your message has not been understood, the pilot will make a complete right-hand circle or flash red lights (p. 40).
Step 4 - Signal Ground Search Teams: In places where people get lost frequently, such as in mountainous or wilderness areas, volunteer search-and-rescue teams have formed to meet the need (p. 40).

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. By making a complete right-hand circle or flashing red lights
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): If a pilot does not understand your ground signal, the aircraft will fly a complete right-hand circle or flash red lights, while wing-rocking or green lights mean the message was understood (p. 40).
