requirements.description: Do ONE of the following special-interest options: (a) Option A, Model Railroading. With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, do TWO of the following: (1) Draw a layout of your own model railroad or one that could be built in your home. Design a point-to-point track or loop with different routings. Include one of the following: turnaround or terminal or yard or siding. (2) Build one model railroad car kit or one locomotive kit. (3) Name the scale of four popular model railroad gauges. Identify the scale of four model cars or locomotives. (4) Locate the websites of four model railroad-related manufacturers or magazine publishers. Print information about their products and services, and discuss the information with your counselor. (5) Build one railroad structure (from scratch or using a kit), paint and weather the structure, mount it on your layout or diorama, and make the surrounding area on the diorama scenic. (6) Alone or with others, build a model railroad or modular layout including ballast and scenery. Make electrical connections and operate a train. Describe what you enjoyed most. (7) Participate in a switching contest on a timesaver layout and record your time. (8) Explain the difference between powering and controlling a model railroad by using direct current, and powering and controlling a model railroad using digital command control. (b) Option B, Railfanning. With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, do TWO of the following: (1) Visit a railroad museum, historical display, or a prototype railroad-sponsored public event. With permission, photograph, digitally record, or sketch items of interest. Explain what you saw and describe your photos, sketches, or video. (2) Purchase tickets and ride a scenic or historic railroad. Under supervision, photograph the equipment and discuss with your counselor the historic significance of the operation. (3) Locate the websites of four rail historical groups, then find information on the history of the rail preservation operations and purpose of each group. Talk with a member of one of the groups and find out how you might help. (4) Plan a trip by rail between two points. Obtain a schedule and explain when the train should arrive at two intermediate points. Purchase the tickets and make the trip. Explain to your counselor what you saw.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why does Operation Lifesaver emphasize that pedestrians and drivers must never walk along railroad tracks or drive around lowered crossing gates?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why does Operation Lifesaver emphasize that pedestrians and drivers must never walk along railroad tracks or drive around lowered crossing gates?
options: A. Trains can easily swerve onto adjacent tracks, making it hard to predict which rail they will use.
B. A freight train overhangs the rails by at least three feet on both sides, can approach quietly, and often requires more than a mile to stop even with emergency braking.
C. Railroad tracks carry high-voltage third-rail traction power on all rural diesel freight lines across North America.
D. Crossing gates lower only after the locomotive is within 50 feet of the intersection.
choices: A. Trains can easily swerve onto adjacent tracks, making it hard to predict which rail they will use.
B. A freight train overhangs the rails by at least three feet on both sides, can approach quietly, and often requires more than a mile to stop even with emergency braking.
C. Railroad tracks carry high-voltage third-rail traction power on all rural diesel freight lines across North America.
D. Crossing gates lower only after the locomotive is within 50 feet of the intersection.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. A freight train overhangs the rails by at least three feet on both sides, can approach quietly, and often requires more than a mile to stop even with emergency braking.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Trains cannot steer, overhang the crossties, appear slower and farther away than they actually are, and require a mile or more to come to a full stop.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Who owns the vast majority of the 22,000 miles of track over which Amtrak operates its intercity passenger trains?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Who owns the vast majority of the 22,000 miles of track over which Amtrak operates its intercity passenger trains?
options: A. Municipal transit authorities in each state
B. Class I freight railroads
C. The Federal Highway Administration
D. Private intercity bus companies
choices: A. Municipal transit authorities in each state
B. Class I freight railroads
C. The Federal Highway Administration
D. Private intercity bus companies
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Class I freight railroads
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Almost all of the more than 22,000 miles of track used by Amtrak is owned by Class I freight railroads, except for Amtrak-owned segments like the Northeast Corridor (p. 27).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which department within a railroad company is responsible for maintaining the fixed plant, including track beds, bridges, tunnels, and signal systems?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which department within a railroad company is responsible for maintaining the fixed plant, including track beds, bridges, tunnels, and signal systems?
options: A. The transportation department
B. The mechanical department
C. The engineering department
D. The marketing and sales department
choices: A. The transportation department
B. The mechanical department
C. The engineering department
D. The marketing and sales department
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The engineering department
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The engineering department maintains the railroad's fixed plant, which includes track, roadbed, bridges, trestles, tunnels, and wayside signal systems (p. 51).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why should passengers never sit on the edge of a station platform or stand right next to the steel rails when a train approaches?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why should passengers never sit on the edge of a station platform or stand right next to the steel rails when a train approaches?
options: A. Platform edges are electrified with high-voltage current
B. Station platforms sink several inches under train weight
C. The locomotive engineer cannot see passengers on platforms
D. Trains overhang the tracks and are wider than the rails
choices: A. Platform edges are electrified with high-voltage current
B. Station platforms sink several inches under train weight
C. The locomotive engineer cannot see passengers on platforms
D. Trains overhang the tracks and are wider than the rails
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Trains overhang the tracks and are wider than the rails
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Trains are wider than the tracks and overhang the rails on both sides, so passengers must always stand behind the safety line and never sit on the platform edge (p. 38).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What should a driver of a lowboy trailer do when approaching a yellow warning sign showing a trailer bottoming out on a raised bump over tracks?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What should a driver of a lowboy trailer do when approaching a yellow warning sign showing a trailer bottoming out on a raised bump over tracks?
options: A. Accelerate to jump across the raised rails before the gates lower
B. Avoid the crossing because low-clearance vehicles risk getting hung up on the tracks
C. Lower the trailer's tire pressure to increase traction on the steel rails
D. Stop on the tracks and call the railroad dispatcher for a pilot car
choices: A. Accelerate to jump across the raised rails before the gates lower
B. Avoid the crossing because low-clearance vehicles risk getting hung up on the tracks
C. Lower the trailer's tire pressure to increase traction on the steel rails
D. Stop on the tracks and call the railroad dispatcher for a pilot car
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Avoid the crossing because low-clearance vehicles risk getting hung up on the tracks
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The Low Ground Clearance Grade Crossing sign warns that raised crossings can trap lowboy trailers or other low-clearance vehicles on the tracks (p. 39).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do modern train crew members primarily communicate with each other during daily switching and train operations?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do modern train crew members primarily communicate with each other during daily switching and train operations?
options: A. By swinging oil-burning kerosene lanterns
B. By pulling a signal cord running through the freight cars
C. Using two-way walkie-talkie radios
D. Using telegraph keys mounted on wayside signal masts
choices: A. By swinging oil-burning kerosene lanterns
B. By pulling a signal cord running through the freight cars
C. Using two-way walkie-talkie radios
D. Using telegraph keys mounted on wayside signal masts
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Using two-way walkie-talkie radios
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): While crews still carry battery-powered lanterns as standard equipment, railroad employees rarely use hand signals today and instead communicate directly using walkie-talkies (p. 30).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When using a library catalog to locate nonfiction research materials, how does the Dewey Decimal Classification system organize books on the shelves?
quiz_item.question: When using a library catalog to locate nonfiction research materials, how does the Dewey Decimal Classification system organize books on the shelves?
options: A. Alphabetically by the publisher's city of origin, followed by the book's page count.
B. Chronologically by the year the book was acquired by the local library branch.
C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
D. By cover size and binding color so reference encyclopedias are shelved next to paperback fiction.
choices: A. Alphabetically by the publisher's city of origin, followed by the book's page count.
B. Chronologically by the year the book was acquired by the local library branch.
C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
D. By cover size and binding color so reference encyclopedias are shelved next to paperback fiction.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The Dewey Decimal system groups nonfiction books by subject using three-digit numbers (000-999) and decimal extensions, making it easy to browse related works on the same topic.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: When using a library catalog to locate nonfiction research materials, how does the Dewey Decimal Classification system organize books on the shelves?
options: A. Alphabetically by the publisher's city of origin, followed by the book's page count.
B. Chronologically by the year the book was acquired by the local library branch.
C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
D. By cover size and binding color so reference encyclopedias are shelved next to paperback fiction.
choices: A. Alphabetically by the publisher's city of origin, followed by the book's page count.
B. Chronologically by the year the book was acquired by the local library branch.
C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
D. By cover size and binding color so reference encyclopedias are shelved next to paperback fiction.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Numerically by subject into ten main classes (000 to 999) with decimal subdivisions, followed by the author's cutter code so books on the same topic sit together.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The Dewey Decimal system groups nonfiction books by subject using three-digit numbers (000-999) and decimal extensions, making it easy to browse related works on the same topic.

intro_notes: NOTE: Scouts must remember to follow the Leave No Trace Seven Principles and the Outdoor Code while on field trips and when collecting specimens. Make sure you have permission of the land manager prior to taking any samples for your collections. Collecting is prohibited in most National and State Parks. Scouts must not use venomous reptiles in fulfilling requirement 8(a). When you decide that keeping your specimen is no longer possible or desired, be sure to find another appropriate home for it or return it to the wild at the location of capture. Check with your counselor for those instances where the return of these specimens would not be appropriate. Under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, some plants and animals are, or may be, protected by federal law. The same ones and/or others may be protected by state law. Be sure that you do not collect protected species. Your state may require that you purchase and carry a license to collect certain species. Check with the wildlife and fish and game officials in your state regarding species regulations before you begin to collect.
NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

quiz_item.question: Which biological traits distinguish reptiles (such as snakes, lizards, and turtles) from amphibians (such as frogs, toads, and salamanders)?
options: A. Reptiles have dry skin covered in scales or scutes and lay shelled amniotic eggs on land, whereas amphibians have moist, permeable skin without scales and typically lay shell-less eggs in water before undergoing metamorphosis.
B. Reptiles are warm-blooded endothermic vertebrates that nurse their young, whereas amphibians are cold-blooded invertebrates.
C. Amphibians breathe exclusively through lungs from the moment they hatch, whereas reptiles breathe through external gills throughout adulthood.
D. Reptiles must keep their skin wet in freshwater ponds to absorb oxygen, whereas amphibians have waterproof keratin claws and shells.
choices: A. Reptiles have dry skin covered in scales or scutes and lay shelled amniotic eggs on land, whereas amphibians have moist, permeable skin without scales and typically lay shell-less eggs in water before undergoing metamorphosis.
B. Reptiles are warm-blooded endothermic vertebrates that nurse their young, whereas amphibians are cold-blooded invertebrates.
C. Amphibians breathe exclusively through lungs from the moment they hatch, whereas reptiles breathe through external gills throughout adulthood.
D. Reptiles must keep their skin wet in freshwater ponds to absorb oxygen, whereas amphibians have waterproof keratin claws and shells.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Reptiles have dry skin covered in scales or scutes and lay shelled amniotic eggs on land, whereas amphibians have moist, permeable skin without scales and typically lay shell-less eggs in water before undergoing metamorphosis.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Both groups are ectothermic vertebrates, but reptiles possess dry scaly skin and amniotic eggs adapted to land, while amphibians have scaleless permeable skin and an aquatic larval stage.

options: A. Legless lizards have venomous fangs and heat-sensing facial pits
B. Legless lizards have wet, slimy skin and lay shell-less eggs in water
C. Legless lizards breathe through external gills throughout their adult lives
D. Legless lizards possess movable eyelids and external ear openings, which snakes lack
choices: A. Legless lizards have venomous fangs and heat-sensing facial pits
B. Legless lizards have wet, slimy skin and lay shell-less eggs in water
C. Legless lizards breathe through external gills throughout their adult lives
D. Legless lizards possess movable eyelids and external ear openings, which snakes lack
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Legless lizards possess movable eyelids and external ear openings, which snakes lack
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Most lizards, including legless glass lizards, have movable eyelids and external ear openings, whereas snakes have clear fixed eye caps and no external ear openings (p. 7).

B. Their permeable skin and dual aquatic-terrestrial life cycle make them highly sensitive to water and air pollutants
C. They migrate thousands of miles between continents every winter
D. They are the only vertebrates capable of surviving in heavily polluted industrial ponds
choices: A. Their thick, waterproof shells trap airborne heavy metals for decades
B. Their permeable skin and dual aquatic-terrestrial life cycle make them highly sensitive to water and air pollutants
C. They migrate thousands of miles between continents every winter
D. They are the only vertebrates capable of surviving in heavily polluted industrial ponds
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Their permeable skin and dual aquatic-terrestrial life cycle make them highly sensitive to water and air pollutants
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Because amphibians live both in water and on land and breathe or absorb moisture through thin permeable skin, they react quickly to chemical contamination and habitat degradation (p. 6).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What key adaptation allows reptiles to reproduce on dry land without returning to standing water?
quiz_item.question: What key adaptation allows reptiles to reproduce on dry land without returning to standing water?
options: A. Jelly-covered eggs that absorb morning dew through an open membrane
B. External fertilization during heavy summer rainstorms
C. Internal fertilization combined with an amniotic egg protected by a leathery or calcareous shell
D. A free-swimming gill-breathing larval stage that burrows into dry sand
choices: A. Jelly-covered eggs that absorb morning dew through an open membrane
B. External fertilization during heavy summer rainstorms
C. Internal fertilization combined with an amniotic egg protected by a leathery or calcareous shell
D. A free-swimming gill-breathing larval stage that burrows into dry sand
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Internal fertilization combined with an amniotic egg protected by a leathery or calcareous shell
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Reptiles use internal fertilization and produce amniotic eggs enclosed in a leathery or calcium-rich shell (or give live birth), preventing the developing embryo from drying out on land (p. 6).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How do heavy-bodied snakes like large boas or rattlesnakes creep forward in a straight line (rectilinear locomotion) when stalking prey?
quiz_item.question: How do heavy-bodied snakes like large boas or rattlesnakes creep forward in a straight line (rectilinear locomotion) when stalking prey?
options: A. By alternately lifting, pulling forward, and anchoring sections of their overlapping belly plates using skin-attached muscles
B. By swinging their ribs back and forth like rowboat oars inside their body cavity
C. By coiling into a tight spring and launching their entire body into the air
D. By secreting a slippery mucus trail similar to a garden slug
choices: A. By alternately lifting, pulling forward, and anchoring sections of their overlapping belly plates using skin-attached muscles
B. By swinging their ribs back and forth like rowboat oars inside their body cavity
C. By coiling into a tight spring and launching their entire body into the air
D. By secreting a slippery mucus trail similar to a garden slug
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. By alternately lifting, pulling forward, and anchoring sections of their overlapping belly plates using skin-attached muscles
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In rectilinear locomotion, muscles linking the ribs to the ventral skin alternately lift batches of belly plates (scutes), pull them forward, anchor their rear edges against the ground, and pull the body along in a straight line (p. 7).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the correct first-aid procedure if a hiker is bitten by a venomous snake on the trail?
quiz_item.question: What is the correct first-aid procedure if a hiker is bitten by a venomous snake on the trail?
options: A. Pack the bite area in ice and tie a tight belt tourniquet above the joint
B. Make shallow incisions across the fang punctures and use a suction pump
C. Keep the victim calm, remove rings or tight clothing, immobilize the limb below heart level, and seek immediate medical evacuation
D. Have the victim run quickly down the trail to reach the parking lot before swelling begins
choices: A. Pack the bite area in ice and tie a tight belt tourniquet above the joint
B. Make shallow incisions across the fang punctures and use a suction pump
C. Keep the victim calm, remove rings or tight clothing, immobilize the limb below heart level, and seek immediate medical evacuation
D. Have the victim run quickly down the trail to reach the parking lot before swelling begins
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Keep the victim calm, remove rings or tight clothing, immobilize the limb below heart level, and seek immediate medical evacuation
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Keeping the patient calm and still slows venom spread, removing constricting items prevents damage as swelling occurs, and rapid transport to a hospital for antivenom is essential (p. 7).

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Take custody of one or more reptiles or amphibians in a manner approved by your counselor. Maintain one or more reptiles or amphibians for at least a month. Record food accepted, eating methods, changes in coloration, shedding of skins, and general habits; or keep the eggs of a reptile from the time of laying until hatching; or keep the eggs of an amphibian from the time of laying until their transformation into tadpoles (frogs) or larvae (salamanders). Whichever you choose, keep records of and report to your counselor how you cared for your animal, eggs, or larvae, including lighting, habitat, temperature and humidity maintenance, and any veterinary care requirements. Unless you are the long-term owner, at the conclusion of this study, turn the animal(s) over to another responsible party approved by your counselor. (b) Choose a reptile or amphibian that you can observe or foster at a local zoo, aquarium, nature center, local rescue, or other such exhibit (such as your classroom or school). Study the specimen weekly for a period of three months. At each visit, sketch the specimen in its captive habitat and note any changes in its coloration, shedding of skins, and general habits and behavior. Discuss with your counselor how the animal you observed was cared for to include its housing and habitat, how the lighting, temperature, and humidity were maintained, and any veterinary care requirements. Find out, either from information you locate on your own or by talking to the caretaker, what this species eats and what are its native habitat and home range, preferred climate, average life expectancy, and natural predators. Also, identify any human-caused threats to its population and any laws that protect the species and its habitat. After the observation period, share what you have learned with your counselor.

common_misconception_pair.misconception: When a snake's eyes turn cloudy blue-white, it has gone permanently blind from an infection and should be handled frequently.
common_misconception_pair.fact: Cloudy eyes indicate that fluid has formed beneath the old eye cap prior to shedding (ecdysis), a time when the snake has poor vision and should be left undisturbed in proper humidity (p. 8).

B. By opening its mouth wide and exhaling air rapidly into the night air
C. By keeping its mouth and nostrils closed while forcing air over its vocal cords into an inflatable vocal sac
D. By snapping its tongue repeatedly against the surface of the water
choices: A. By rubbing its rough hind legs against the ridges on its sides like a cricket
B. By opening its mouth wide and exhaling air rapidly into the night air
C. By keeping its mouth and nostrils closed while forcing air over its vocal cords into an inflatable vocal sac
D. By snapping its tongue repeatedly against the surface of the water
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. By keeping its mouth and nostrils closed while forcing air over its vocal cords into an inflatable vocal sac
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Calling frogs and toads keep their mouth and nostrils shut, shuttling air over their vocal cords into a balloon-like vocal sac under the chin or cheeks to amplify the sound (p. 6).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which of the following is a verified biological adaptation rather than a superstition?
quiz_item.question: Which of the following is a verified biological adaptation rather than a superstition?
options: A. Milk snakes latching onto dairy cows in barns to drink warm milk
B. Eastern hognose snakes puffing up, hissing, and rolling onto their backs to play dead when threatened
C. Toads causing contagious skin warts on anyone who picks them up
D. Hoop snakes biting their tails and rolling down hills to chase hikers
choices: A. Milk snakes latching onto dairy cows in barns to drink warm milk
B. Eastern hognose snakes puffing up, hissing, and rolling onto their backs to play dead when threatened
C. Toads causing contagious skin warts on anyone who picks them up
D. Hoop snakes biting their tails and rolling down hills to chase hikers
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Eastern hognose snakes puffing up, hissing, and rolling onto their backs to play dead when threatened
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): While milk-drinking snakes, hoop snakes, and toad-induced warts are folklore myths, the hognose snake truly bluffs predators by spreading its neck and rolling onto its back with its tongue hanging out to feign death (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which biological traits distinguish reptiles (such as snakes, lizards, and turtles) from amphibians (such as frogs, toads, and salamanders)?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which biological traits distinguish reptiles (such as snakes, lizards, and turtles) from amphibians (such as frogs, toads, and salamanders)?
options: A. Reptiles have dry skin covered in scales or scutes and lay shelled amniotic eggs on land, whereas amphibians have moist, permeable skin without scales and typically lay shell-less eggs in water before undergoing metamorphosis.
B. Reptiles are warm-blooded endothermic vertebrates that nurse their young, whereas amphibians are cold-blooded invertebrates.
C. Amphibians breathe exclusively through lungs from the moment they hatch, whereas reptiles breathe through external gills throughout adulthood.
D. Reptiles must keep their skin wet in freshwater ponds to absorb oxygen, whereas amphibians have waterproof keratin claws and shells.
choices: A. Reptiles have dry skin covered in scales or scutes and lay shelled amniotic eggs on land, whereas amphibians have moist, permeable skin without scales and typically lay shell-less eggs in water before undergoing metamorphosis.
B. Reptiles are warm-blooded endothermic vertebrates that nurse their young, whereas amphibians are cold-blooded invertebrates.
C. Amphibians breathe exclusively through lungs from the moment they hatch, whereas reptiles breathe through external gills throughout adulthood.
D. Reptiles must keep their skin wet in freshwater ponds to absorb oxygen, whereas amphibians have waterproof keratin claws and shells.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Reptiles have dry skin covered in scales or scutes and lay shelled amniotic eggs on land, whereas amphibians have moist, permeable skin without scales and typically lay shell-less eggs in water before undergoing metamorphosis.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Both groups are ectothermic vertebrates, but reptiles possess dry scaly skin and amniotic eggs adapted to land, while amphibians have scaleless permeable skin and an aquatic larval stage.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why does the southeastern United States support a much higher diversity of amphibians than the arid Great Basin?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why does the southeastern United States support a much higher diversity of amphibians than the arid Great Basin?
options: A. Amphibians require permeable skin and moist habitats or standing water to prevent dehydration and lay eggs
B. Amphibians can only digest insects that grow in coastal salt marshes
C. Reptiles have completely outcompeted amphibians in every eastern forest
D. State wildlife agencies only stock amphibians in eastern rivers
choices: A. Amphibians require permeable skin and moist habitats or standing water to prevent dehydration and lay eggs
B. Amphibians can only digest insects that grow in coastal salt marshes
C. Reptiles have completely outcompeted amphibians in every eastern forest
D. State wildlife agencies only stock amphibians in eastern rivers
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Amphibians require permeable skin and moist habitats or standing water to prevent dehydration and lay eggs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Amphibians have moisture-permeable skin and typically require water or damp microhabitats for reproduction, making warm, wet regions like the Southeast ideal for high species diversity (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which anatomical features reliably distinguish a legless lizard from a true snake?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which anatomical features reliably distinguish a legless lizard from a true snake?
options: A. Legless lizards have venomous fangs and heat-sensing facial pits
B. Legless lizards have wet, slimy skin and lay shell-less eggs in water
C. Legless lizards breathe through external gills throughout their adult lives
D. Legless lizards possess movable eyelids and external ear openings, which snakes lack
choices: A. Legless lizards have venomous fangs and heat-sensing facial pits
B. Legless lizards have wet, slimy skin and lay shell-less eggs in water
C. Legless lizards breathe through external gills throughout their adult lives
D. Legless lizards possess movable eyelids and external ear openings, which snakes lack
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Legless lizards possess movable eyelids and external ear openings, which snakes lack
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Most lizards, including legless glass lizards, have movable eyelids and external ear openings, whereas snakes have clear fixed eye caps and no external ear openings (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do biologists consider amphibians especially important bioindicators of environmental health?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do biologists consider amphibians especially important bioindicators of environmental health?
options: A. Their thick, waterproof shells trap airborne heavy metals for decades
B. Their permeable skin and dual aquatic-terrestrial life cycle make them highly sensitive to water and air pollutants
C. They migrate thousands of miles between continents every winter
D. They are the only vertebrates capable of surviving in heavily polluted industrial ponds
choices: A. Their thick, waterproof shells trap airborne heavy metals for decades
B. Their permeable skin and dual aquatic-terrestrial life cycle make them highly sensitive to water and air pollutants
C. They migrate thousands of miles between continents every winter
D. They are the only vertebrates capable of surviving in heavily polluted industrial ponds
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Their permeable skin and dual aquatic-terrestrial life cycle make them highly sensitive to water and air pollutants
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Because amphibians live both in water and on land and breathe or absorb moisture through thin permeable skin, they react quickly to chemical contamination and habitat degradation (p. 6).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What key adaptation allows reptiles to reproduce on dry land without returning to standing water?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What key adaptation allows reptiles to reproduce on dry land without returning to standing water?
options: A. Jelly-covered eggs that absorb morning dew through an open membrane
B. External fertilization during heavy summer rainstorms
C. Internal fertilization combined with an amniotic egg protected by a leathery or calcareous shell
D. A free-swimming gill-breathing larval stage that burrows into dry sand
choices: A. Jelly-covered eggs that absorb morning dew through an open membrane
B. External fertilization during heavy summer rainstorms
C. Internal fertilization combined with an amniotic egg protected by a leathery or calcareous shell
D. A free-swimming gill-breathing larval stage that burrows into dry sand
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Internal fertilization combined with an amniotic egg protected by a leathery or calcareous shell
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Reptiles use internal fertilization and produce amniotic eggs enclosed in a leathery or calcium-rich shell (or give live birth), preventing the developing embryo from drying out on land (p. 6).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do heavy-bodied snakes like large boas or rattlesnakes creep forward in a straight line (rectilinear locomotion) when stalking prey?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do heavy-bodied snakes like large boas or rattlesnakes creep forward in a straight line (rectilinear locomotion) when stalking prey?
options: A. By alternately lifting, pulling forward, and anchoring sections of their overlapping belly plates using skin-attached muscles
B. By swinging their ribs back and forth like rowboat oars inside their body cavity
C. By coiling into a tight spring and launching their entire body into the air
D. By secreting a slippery mucus trail similar to a garden slug
choices: A. By alternately lifting, pulling forward, and anchoring sections of their overlapping belly plates using skin-attached muscles
B. By swinging their ribs back and forth like rowboat oars inside their body cavity
C. By coiling into a tight spring and launching their entire body into the air
D. By secreting a slippery mucus trail similar to a garden slug
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. By alternately lifting, pulling forward, and anchoring sections of their overlapping belly plates using skin-attached muscles
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In rectilinear locomotion, muscles linking the ribs to the ventral skin alternately lift batches of belly plates (scutes), pull them forward, anchor their rear edges against the ground, and pull the body along in a straight line (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the correct first-aid procedure if a hiker is bitten by a venomous snake on the trail?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the correct first-aid procedure if a hiker is bitten by a venomous snake on the trail?
options: A. Pack the bite area in ice and tie a tight belt tourniquet above the joint
B. Make shallow incisions across the fang punctures and use a suction pump
C. Keep the victim calm, remove rings or tight clothing, immobilize the limb below heart level, and seek immediate medical evacuation
D. Have the victim run quickly down the trail to reach the parking lot before swelling begins
choices: A. Pack the bite area in ice and tie a tight belt tourniquet above the joint
B. Make shallow incisions across the fang punctures and use a suction pump
C. Keep the victim calm, remove rings or tight clothing, immobilize the limb below heart level, and seek immediate medical evacuation
D. Have the victim run quickly down the trail to reach the parking lot before swelling begins
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Keep the victim calm, remove rings or tight clothing, immobilize the limb below heart level, and seek immediate medical evacuation
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Keeping the patient calm and still slows venom spread, removing constricting items prevents damage as swelling occurs, and rapid transport to a hospital for antivenom is essential (p. 7).

D. Food accepted, eating methods, changes in coloration, shedding of skin, and general habits
choices: A. Only the initial purchase price and weight of the terrarium

pamphlet_excerpts: Safety Above All Else: In marksmanship, nothing is more important than safety (p. 17).
Shooter Personal Responsibility: Participants in shooting sports assume a vital responsibility that affects the lives of others (p. 17).
Practicing Rifle Safety Rules: It is critically important to learn and practice all of the rifle safety rules (p. 17).
Proper Firearm Handling: When handled correctly and used properly, a rifle is not dangerous (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Memorize Core Safety Rules: It is critically important to learn and practice all of the rifle safety rules (p. 17).
Step 2 - Inspect Safe Firearm Condition: When handled correctly and used properly, a rifle is not dangerous (p. 17).
Step 3 - Wear Eye and Ear Gear: A rifle, like any other precision machine, instrument, or piece of sports equipment, is manufactured to perform a specific task (p. 17).
Step 4 - Follow Hygiene and Legal Rules: If arifle is handled incorrectly or recklessly, without regard for the safety rules, then accidents can happen (p. 17).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: On the firing line, you squeeze the trigger on a loaded .22 rimfire rifle and hear an audible 'click' with no discharge. What is the mandatory misfire safety procedure?
quiz_item.question: On the firing line, you squeeze the trigger on a loaded .22 rimfire rifle and hear an audible 'click' with no discharge. What is the mandatory misfire safety procedure?
options: A. Immediately open the bolt to eject the cartridge and inspect the firing pin indent.
B. Keep the rifle muzzle pointed safely downrange, raise your non-shooting hand to notify the Range Safety Officer, and wait at least 30 seconds before opening the action in case of a hangfire.
C. Lay the closed rifle down on the shooting mat pointed toward the waiting bench and walk over to the instructor.
D. Look down the muzzle end of the barrel to verify whether a bullet is lodged in the bore.

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Keep the rifle muzzle pointed safely downrange, raise your non-shooting hand to notify the Range Safety Officer, and wait at least 30 seconds before opening the action in case of a hangfire.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A delayed ignition (hangfire) can detonate seconds after the trigger pull; opening the breech immediately exposes the shooter's face and hands to a live rupture outside the chamber.

requirements.description: Do the following: (a) Explain what a projectile is, and why any device that shoots a projectile at high speed must be handled with care and respect, and used only in approved locations. (b) Explain the basic rules of safe gun handling that apply to all firearms. (c) Describe how you would react if a friend visiting your home asked to see your or your family's firearm. (d) Explain the need for, types, and use of eye protection and hearing protection. (e) Explain the main points of the laws for owning and using guns in your community and state. (f) Explain how hunting is related to the wise use of renewable wildlife resources. (g) Successfully complete a state hunter education course, or obtain a copy of the hunting laws for your state, then do the following: (1) Explain the main points of hunting laws in your state, and any special laws on the use of guns and ammunition, AND (2) List the kinds of wildlife that can be legally hunted in your state. (h) Explain to your counselor the proper hygienic guidelines followed while shooting. (i) Identify places in your community where you can join or be a part of range and target activities. (j) Discuss with your counselor a list of sources you could contact for information on firearms and their use.

requirements.lead_text: Working under the supervision of a certified National Rifle Association (NRA) rifle instructor and a certified range safety officer, at a nationally authorized camp property or at a commercial firearm range (as defined in the Scouting America National Range and Target Activities Manual ), do ONE of the following options:
requirements.req_text: Working under the supervision of a certified National Rifle Association (NRA) rifle instructor and a certified range safety officer, at a nationally authorized camp property or at a commercial firearm range (as defined in the Scouting America National Range and Target Activities Manual ), do ONE of the following options: (a) Option A, Rifle Shooting (Modern Cartridge Type). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify the three main parts of a rifle, and tell how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a rifle. (3) Identify the two types of cartridges, their parts, and how they function. (4) Explain to your counselor what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are, and explain the procedures to follow in response to each. (5) Explain and demonstrate the five fundamentals of shooting a rifle: aiming, breath control, hold control, trigger control, and follow-through. (6) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a rifle on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (7) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a rifle, and identify the materials needed. (8) Demonstrate how to clean a rifle properly and safely. (9) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a rifle. (10) Using a bolt-action.22 caliber rimfire rifle, and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position at 50 feet, fire five groups (three shots per group) that can be touched by a quarter. Using these targets, explain how to adjust sights to zero a rifle. (11) Adjust sights to center the group on the target and fire five groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire five groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be touched by a quarter. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: A-32 targets: 9; A-17 or TQ-1 targets: 7; A-36 targets: 5. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable. (b) Option B, Air Rifle Shooting (BB or Pellet). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify the three main parts of an air rifle, and explain how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling an air rifle. (3) Identify the two most common types of air rifle ammunition. (4) Explain and demonstrate the five fundamentals of shooting an air rifle: aiming, breath control, hold control, trigger control, and follow-through. (5) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (6) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning an air rifle, and identify the materials needed. (7) Demonstrate how to clean an air rifle properly and safely. (8) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting an air rifle. (9) Using a BB gun or pellet rifle and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position at 15 feet for BB guns or 33 feet for pellet rifles, fire five groups (three shots per group) that can be touched by a quarter. (10) Adjust sights to center the group on the target and fire five groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed air rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire five groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be touched by a quarter. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: BB rifle at 15 feet (or 5 meters) using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 25 feet using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 33 feet (or 10 meters) using AR-1 targets: 6. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable. (c) Option C, Muzzleloading Rifle Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Discuss with your counselor a brief history of the development of muzzleloading rifles. (2) Identify principal parts of muzzleloading rifles and discuss how they function. (3) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a muzzleloading rifle. (4) Identify the various grades of black powder and explain their proper and safe use. (5) Discuss proper safety procedures pertaining to black powder storage. (6) Discuss proper components of a load. (7) Identify proper procedures and accessories used for safely loading a muzzleloading rifle. (8) Identify the causes of a muzzleloading rifle's failure to fire, and explain what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are. Explain and demonstrate proper preventive measures, and the procedures to follow in response to each. (9) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a muzzleloading rifle on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (10) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a muzzleloading rifle, and identify the materials needed. (11) Demonstrate how to clean a muzzleloading rifle properly and safely. (12) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a muzzleloading rifle. (13) Using a muzzleloading rifle of.45 or.50 caliber and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position, fire three groups (three shots per group) at 50 feet that can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. (14) Adjust the sights to center the group on the target and fire three groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed muzzleloading rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire three groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: at 25 yards using NRA A-23 or NMLRA 50-yard targets: 7; at 50 yards using NRA A-25 or NMLRA 100-yard targets: 7. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option A, Rifle Shooting (Modern Cartridge Type). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify the three main parts of a rifle, and tell how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a rifle. (3) Identify the two types of cartridges, their parts, and how they function. (4) Explain to your counselor what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are, and explain the procedures to follow in response to each. (5) Explain and demonstrate the five fundamentals of shooting a rifle: aiming, breath control, hold control, trigger control, and follow-through. (6) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a rifle on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (7) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a rifle, and identify the materials needed. (8) Demonstrate how to clean a rifle properly and safely. (9) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a rifle. (10) Using a bolt-action.22 caliber rimfire rifle, and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position at 50 feet, fire five groups (three shots per group) that can be touched by a quarter. Using these targets, explain how to adjust sights to zero a rifle. (11) Adjust sights to center the group on the target and fire five groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire five groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be touched by a quarter. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: A-32 targets: 9; A-17 or TQ-1 targets: 7; A-36 targets: 5. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: Modern Cartridge Rifle Option: The gun, the targets, and the distances vary in the options offered for the cartridge rifle, the air rifle, and the muzzle loader (p. 19).

sub_requirements.text: Option B, Air Rifle Shooting (BB or Pellet). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify the three main parts of an air rifle, and explain how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling an air rifle. (3) Identify the two most common types of air rifle ammunition. (4) Explain and demonstrate the five fundamentals of shooting an air rifle: aiming, breath control, hold control, trigger control, and follow-through. (5) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (6) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning an air rifle, and identify the materials needed. (7) Demonstrate how to clean an air rifle properly and safely. (8) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting an air rifle. (9) Using a BB gun or pellet rifle and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position at 15 feet for BB guns or 33 feet for pellet rifles, fire five groups (three shots per group) that can be touched by a quarter. (10) Adjust sights to center the group on the target and fire five groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed air rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire five groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be touched by a quarter. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: BB rifle at 15 feet (or 5 meters) using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 25 feet using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 33 feet (or 10 meters) using AR-1 targets: 6. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option B, Air Rifle Shooting (BB or Pellet). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify the three main parts of an air rifle, and explain how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling an air rifle. (3) Identify the two most common types of air rifle ammunition. (4) Explain and demonstrate the five fundamentals of shooting an air rifle: aiming, breath control, hold control, trigger control, and follow-through. (5) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (6) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning an air rifle, and identify the materials needed. (7) Demonstrate how to clean an air rifle properly and safely. (8) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting an air rifle. (9) Using a BB gun or pellet rifle and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position at 15 feet for BB guns or 33 feet for pellet rifles, fire five groups (three shots per group) that can be touched by a quarter. (10) Adjust sights to center the group on the target and fire five groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed air rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire five groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be touched by a quarter. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: BB rifle at 15 feet (or 5 meters) using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 25 feet using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 33 feet (or 10 meters) using AR-1 targets: 6. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable.

sub_requirements.label: (c)
sub_requirements.text: Option C, Muzzleloading Rifle Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Discuss with your counselor a brief history of the development of muzzleloading rifles. (2) Identify principal parts of muzzleloading rifles and discuss how they function. (3) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a muzzleloading rifle. (4) Identify the various grades of black powder and explain their proper and safe use. (5) Discuss proper safety procedures pertaining to black powder storage. (6) Discuss proper components of a load. (7) Identify proper procedures and accessories used for safely loading a muzzleloading rifle. (8) Identify the causes of a muzzleloading rifle's failure to fire, and explain what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are. Explain and demonstrate proper preventive measures, and the procedures to follow in response to each. (9) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a muzzleloading rifle on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (10) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a muzzleloading rifle, and identify the materials needed. (11) Demonstrate how to clean a muzzleloading rifle properly and safely. (12) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a muzzleloading rifle. (13) Using a muzzleloading rifle of.45 or.50 caliber and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position, fire three groups (three shots per group) at 50 feet that can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. (14) Adjust the sights to center the group on the target and fire three groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed muzzleloading rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire three groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: at 25 yards using NRA A-23 or NMLRA 50-yard targets: 7; at 50 yards using NRA A-25 or NMLRA 100-yard targets: 7. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option C, Muzzleloading Rifle Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Discuss with your counselor a brief history of the development of muzzleloading rifles. (2) Identify principal parts of muzzleloading rifles and discuss how they function. (3) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a muzzleloading rifle. (4) Identify the various grades of black powder and explain their proper and safe use. (5) Discuss proper safety procedures pertaining to black powder storage. (6) Discuss proper components of a load. (7) Identify proper procedures and accessories used for safely loading a muzzleloading rifle. (8) Identify the causes of a muzzleloading rifle's failure to fire, and explain what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are. Explain and demonstrate proper preventive measures, and the procedures to follow in response to each. (9) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a muzzleloading rifle on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (10) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a muzzleloading rifle, and identify the materials needed. (11) Demonstrate how to clean a muzzleloading rifle properly and safely. (12) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a muzzleloading rifle. (13) Using a muzzleloading rifle of.45 or.50 caliber and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position, fire three groups (three shots per group) at 50 feet that can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. (14) Adjust the sights to center the group on the target and fire three groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed muzzleloading rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire three groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: at 25 yards using NRA A-23 or NMLRA 50-yard targets: 7; at 50 yards using NRA A-25 or NMLRA 100-yard targets: 7. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable.

requirements.description: Working under the supervision of a certified National Rifle Association (NRA) rifle instructor and a certified range safety officer, at a nationally authorized camp property or at a commercial firearm range (as defined in the Scouting America National Range and Target Activities Manual ), do ONE of the following options: (a) Option A, Rifle Shooting (Modern Cartridge Type). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify the three main parts of a rifle, and tell how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a rifle. (3) Identify the two types of cartridges, their parts, and how they function. (4) Explain to your counselor what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are, and explain the procedures to follow in response to each. (5) Explain and demonstrate the five fundamentals of shooting a rifle: aiming, breath control, hold control, trigger control, and follow-through. (6) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a rifle on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (7) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a rifle, and identify the materials needed. (8) Demonstrate how to clean a rifle properly and safely. (9) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a rifle. (10) Using a bolt-action.22 caliber rimfire rifle, and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position at 50 feet, fire five groups (three shots per group) that can be touched by a quarter. Using these targets, explain how to adjust sights to zero a rifle. (11) Adjust sights to center the group on the target and fire five groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire five groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be touched by a quarter. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: A-32 targets: 9; A-17 or TQ-1 targets: 7; A-36 targets: 5. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable. (b) Option B, Air Rifle Shooting (BB or Pellet). Do ALL of the following: (1) Identify the three main parts of an air rifle, and explain how they function. (2) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling an air rifle. (3) Identify the two most common types of air rifle ammunition. (4) Explain and demonstrate the five fundamentals of shooting an air rifle: aiming, breath control, hold control, trigger control, and follow-through. (5) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (6) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning an air rifle, and identify the materials needed. (7) Demonstrate how to clean an air rifle properly and safely. (8) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting an air rifle. (9) Using a BB gun or pellet rifle and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position at 15 feet for BB guns or 33 feet for pellet rifles, fire five groups (three shots per group) that can be touched by a quarter. (10) Adjust sights to center the group on the target and fire five groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed air rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire five groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be touched by a quarter. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: BB rifle at 15 feet (or 5 meters) using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 25 feet using TQ-5 targets: 8; Pellet rifle at 33 feet (or 10 meters) using AR-1 targets: 6. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable. (c) Option C, Muzzleloading Rifle Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Discuss with your counselor a brief history of the development of muzzleloading rifles. (2) Identify principal parts of muzzleloading rifles and discuss how they function. (3) Identify and demonstrate the rules for safely storing and handling a muzzleloading rifle. (4) Identify the various grades of black powder and explain their proper and safe use. (5) Discuss proper safety procedures pertaining to black powder storage. (6) Discuss proper components of a load. (7) Identify proper procedures and accessories used for safely loading a muzzleloading rifle. (8) Identify the causes of a muzzleloading rifle's failure to fire, and explain what a misfire, hangfire, and squib fire are. Explain and demonstrate proper preventive measures, and the procedures to follow in response to each. (9) Demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitude necessary to safely shoot a muzzleloading rifle on a range, including understanding and following range procedures and commands. (10) Explain the basic safety rules for cleaning a muzzleloading rifle, and identify the materials needed. (11) Demonstrate how to clean a muzzleloading rifle properly and safely. (12) Discuss what points you would consider in selecting a muzzleloading rifle. (13) Using a muzzleloading rifle of.45 or.50 caliber and shooting from a benchrest or supported prone position, fire three groups (three shots per group) at 50 feet that can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. (14) Adjust the sights to center the group on the target and fire three groups (five shots per group). In the event that your instructor determines it is not practical to adjust the sights, for instance, on a borrowed muzzleloading rifle, you may explain (rather than doing) how to adjust the sights, and then fire three groups (five shots per group) in which all shots can be covered by the base of a standard-size soft drink can. According to the target used, each shot in the group must meet the following minimum score: at 25 yards using NRA A-23 or NMLRA 50-yard targets: 7; at 50 yards using NRA A-25 or NMLRA 100-yard targets: 7. Note: Other suitable NRA targets may be used if the specified targets are unavailable.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: On the firing line, you squeeze the trigger on a loaded .22 rimfire rifle and hear an audible 'click' with no discharge. What is the mandatory misfire safety procedure?
options: A. Immediately open the bolt to eject the cartridge and inspect the firing pin indent.
B. Keep the rifle muzzle pointed safely downrange, raise your non-shooting hand to notify the Range Safety Officer, and wait at least 30 seconds before opening the action in case of a hangfire.
C. Lay the closed rifle down on the shooting mat pointed toward the waiting bench and walk over to the instructor.
D. Look down the muzzle end of the barrel to verify whether a bullet is lodged in the bore.
choices: A. Immediately open the bolt to eject the cartridge and inspect the firing pin indent.
B. Keep the rifle muzzle pointed safely downrange, raise your non-shooting hand to notify the Range Safety Officer, and wait at least 30 seconds before opening the action in case of a hangfire.
C. Lay the closed rifle down on the shooting mat pointed toward the waiting bench and walk over to the instructor.
D. Look down the muzzle end of the barrel to verify whether a bullet is lodged in the bore.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Keep the rifle muzzle pointed safely downrange, raise your non-shooting hand to notify the Range Safety Officer, and wait at least 30 seconds before opening the action in case of a hangfire.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A delayed ignition (hangfire) can detonate seconds after the trigger pull; opening the breech immediately exposes the shooter's face and hands to a live rupture outside the chamber.

D. Remove safety glasses for a closer view of the spinning pinion gear while toggling the transmitter stick.

requirements.lead_text: Design, Build, Program, Test. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Design, Build, Program, Test. Do the following: (a) With your counselor's approval, choose a task for the robot or robotic subsystem that you plan to build. Include sensor feedback and programming in the task. Document this information in your robot engineering notebook. (b) Design your robot. The robot design should use sensors and programming and have at least 2 degrees of freedom. Document the design in your robot engineering notebook using drawings and a written description. (c) Build a robot or robotic subsystem of your original design to accomplish the task you chose for requirement 4(a). (d) Discuss with your counselor the programming options available for your robot. Then do ONE of the following: (1) Program your robot to perform the task you chose for your robot in 4(a). Include a sample of your program's source code in your robot engineering notebook. (2) Prepare a flowchart of the desired steps to program your robot for accomplishing the task in 4(a). Include procedures that show activities based on sensor inputs. Place this in your robot engineering notebook. (e) Test your robot and record the results in your robot engineering notebook. Include suggestions on how you could improve your robot, as well as pictures or sketches of your finished robot.

requirements.description: Design, Build, Program, Test. Do the following: (a) With your counselor's approval, choose a task for the robot or robotic subsystem that you plan to build. Include sensor feedback and programming in the task. Document this information in your robot engineering notebook. (b) Design your robot. The robot design should use sensors and programming and have at least 2 degrees of freedom. Document the design in your robot engineering notebook using drawings and a written description. (c) Build a robot or robotic subsystem of your original design to accomplish the task you chose for requirement 4(a). (d) Discuss with your counselor the programming options available for your robot. Then do ONE of the following: (1) Program your robot to perform the task you chose for your robot in 4(a). Include a sample of your program's source code in your robot engineering notebook. (2) Prepare a flowchart of the desired steps to program your robot for accomplishing the task in 4(a). Include procedures that show activities based on sensor inputs. Place this in your robot engineering notebook. (e) Test your robot and record the results in your robot engineering notebook. Include suggestions on how you could improve your robot, as well as pictures or sketches of your finished robot.

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Per the Robotics Merit Badge Pamphlet (pp. 9-12), always wear ANSI Z87.1 eye protection, disconnect battery power before mechanical adjustments, brush dry chemical residue away with a gloved hand before flushing with water, and flush minor cuts with soap and water for 5 minutes before applying a sterile bandage.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why does the Robotics merit badge pamphlet compare an autonomous robot system to the human autonomic nervous system?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why does the Robotics merit badge pamphlet compare an autonomous robot system to the human autonomic nervous system?
options: A. Both systems require continuous manual joystick input from an external operator
B. Both operate and regulate themselves automatically through an internal controller without conscious interference
C. Both rely exclusively on pneumatic tubes rather than electrical signals
D. Both can only perform a single physical motion before shutting down permanently
choices: A. Both systems require continuous manual joystick input from an external operator
B. Both operate and regulate themselves automatically through an internal controller without conscious interference
C. Both rely exclusively on pneumatic tubes rather than electrical signals
D. Both can only perform a single physical motion before shutting down permanently
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Both operate and regulate themselves automatically through an internal controller without conscious interference
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Just as the human autonomic nervous system regulates involuntary functions like heartbeat on its own, an autonomous robot uses its onboard computer controller to operate and regulate itself without continuous human interference (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which major field of robotics focuses on how a robot physically interacts with objects, such as picking them up, placing them in containers, or spraying them with paint?

options: A. Human-robot interface

C. Manipulation
D. Sensor calibration
choices: A. Human-robot interface
B. Locomotion and mobility
C. Manipulation

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Manipulation
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Manipulation covers the parts of a robot that physically interact with objects to touch them, pick them up, place them in containers, or apply materials like paint, whereas mobility covers moving from place to place (p. 15).

pamphlet_excerpts: Hand Blister Risks: In rowing, blisters are most likely to occur on the hands (p. 13).
Early Blister Warning Signs: Pay attention to any tender or sensitive areas (hot spots) that indicate the start of a blister (p. 13).
Grip Friction Adjustment: You may be able to adjust or relax your grip to avoid friction on the sensitive area (p. 13).
Protective Rowing Gloves: If you are prone to blisters, prevent them by wearing rowing gloves (p. 13).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Relax Your Oar Grip: You may be able to adjust or relax your grip to avoid friction on the sensitive area (p. 13).
Step 2 - Wear Protective Rowing Gloves: If you are prone to blisters, prevent them by wearing rowing gloves (p. 13).
Step 3 - Cover and Protect Blisters: If you do get a blister, cover and protect the area from further irritation (p. 13).

Step 4 - Identify Overstretched Joint Ligaments: A sprain occurs when an ankle, wrist, or other joint is bent far enough to over stretch the ligaments, the tough bands that hold joints together (p. 13).

options: A. Pass the beginner swim test and carry a whistle on a lanyard.
B. Pass the Scouting America swimmer test and have a buddy with you or nearby in another boat.
C. Complete a one-mile open-water swim while towing an oar.
D. Obtain a lifeguard certification before sitting in a single-person shell.
choices: A. Pass the beginner swim test and carry a whistle on a lanyard.
B. Pass the Scouting America swimmer test and have a buddy with you or nearby in another boat.
C. Complete a one-mile open-water swim while towing an oar.
D. Obtain a lifeguard certification before sitting in a single-person shell.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Pass the Scouting America swimmer test and have a buddy with you or nearby in another boat.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Safety Afloat and the Rowing merit badge require all rowers to pass the Scouting America swimmer test and always have a buddy in the same boat or nearby in another boat (p. 15).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What type of lifejacket is most appropriate for rowing activities?
quiz_item.question: What type of lifejacket is most appropriate for rowing activities?
options: A. An inflatable belt pack worn loosely around the knees for balance.
B. A heavy offshore keyhole lifejacket left unbuckled for ventilation.
C. A properly fitted vest-style lifejacket with wide armholes that permits a full rowing stroke.
D. A throwable buoyant seat cushion strapped to the oarlocks.
choices: A. An inflatable belt pack worn loosely around the knees for balance.
B. A heavy offshore keyhole lifejacket left unbuckled for ventilation.
C. A properly fitted vest-style lifejacket with wide armholes that permits a full rowing stroke.
D. A throwable buoyant seat cushion strapped to the oarlocks.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. A properly fitted vest-style lifejacket with wide armholes that permits a full rowing stroke.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Rowers need a snug, properly fitted lifejacket with wide arm openings that will not chafe or restrict the rowing motion, and participants must have a complete health history on file (p. 16, p. 18).

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Alone or with a passenger, do the following in either a fixed-seat or sliding-seat rowboat: (1) Launch. (2) Row in a straight line for 100 yards. Stop, pivot, and return to the starting point. (3) Backwater in a straight line for 25 yards. Make a turn underway and return to the starting point. (4) Land and moor or rack your craft. (5) Tie the following mooring knots, clove hitch, roundturn with two half-hitches, bowline, Wellman's knot, and mooring hitch. (b) Participate as a rowing team member in a competitive rowing meet. The team may be sponsored by a school, club, or Scout unit. The meet must include competition between two or more teams with different sponsors. Complete at least 10 hours of team practice prior to the meet.

Helper Push-Off Role: The person assisting will play the role of the passenger, except that instead of getting in when you are ready, he or she will give you a gentle push (p. 67).

Step 3 - Ease In Over Transom: Sit on the dock and ease in over the transom while being careful to not lose your balance (p. 67).
Step 4 - Untie the Bow Painter: Move forward to the bow and untie the bowpainter (p. 67).

pamphlet_excerpts: Two-Person Counterbalance Reboarding: If you are with a friend and your boat capsizes, pull yourself up over the side of the swamped boat while your friend holds down the other side (p. 65).
Hip-Level Gunwale Press: Push down on the gunwale with both hands so that you bring yourself up to where your hips are about level with the gunwale (p. 65).
Roll Onto Boat Bottom: Then roll over so that you fall into the bottom of the swamped boat, landing on your backside (p. 65).
Counterbalancing Your Partner: You can then lean over the side to counterbalance as your friend follows the same steps to come in over the opposite side (p. 65).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Roll Onto Your Backside: Then roll over so that you fall into the bottom of the swamped boat, landing on your backside (p. 65).
Step 2 - Lean Over to Counterbalance: You can then lean over the side to counterbalance as your friend follows the same steps to come in over the opposite side (p. 65).
Step 3 - Press the Gunwale: Remember that when you pull yourself up on the gunwale, the gunwale will be forced down into the water (p. 65).
Step 4 - Shift Weight Off Gunwale: After you roll in and get your weight off the gunwale, it will rise back (p. 65).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How should you position your rowboat to rescue and tow a tired swimmer 20 yards from shore?
quiz_item.question: How should you position your rowboat to rescue and tow a tired swimmer 20 yards from shore?
options: A. Row at full speed bow-first and tell the swimmer to grab the moving oar blades.
B. Throw both oars into the water and dive overboard to push the swimmer ashore.
C. Pivot the boat so the stern faces the swimmer, instruct them to hold the transom, and tow them to shore.
D. Have the swimmer climb over the narrow bow deck while you stand in the stern.
choices: A. Row at full speed bow-first and tell the swimmer to grab the moving oar blades.
B. Throw both oars into the water and dive overboard to push the swimmer ashore.
C. Pivot the boat so the stern faces the swimmer, instruct them to hold the transom, and tow them to shore.
D. Have the swimmer climb over the narrow bow deck while you stand in the stern.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Pivot the boat so the stern faces the swimmer, instruct them to hold the transom, and tow them to shore.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): In a rowboat swimmer rescue, you row out to the swimmer, pivot the boat, and back the stern within reach while giving clear instructions so they can hold the transom for a tow to shore (p. 79).

pamphlet_excerpts: Common Hull Materials: Rowboats are made from a variety of materials, including aluminum, fiberglass, plastic, wood planking, and plywood (p. 25).
Low-Maintenance Aluminum Hulls: This lightweight, durable metal needs little maintenance (p. 25).
Built-In Flotation Chambers: Aluminum will not float, but all approved aluminum boats have flotation materials in chambers that keep the boat afloat if it capsizes or swamps (p. 25).
Workable Wood Planking: Easy to cut and drill, wood is probably the easiest boat building material to handle (p. 25).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Check Aluminum Flotation Chambers: Aluminum will not float, but all approved aluminum boats have flotation materials in chambers that keep the boat afloat if it capsizes or swamps (p. 25).
Step 2 - Shape and Drill Wood: Easy to cut and drill, wood is probably the easiest boat building material to handle (p. 25).
Step 3 - Rely on Wood Buoyancy: It is very buoyant, a boat made from wood planking floats even when it is full of water (p. 25).
Step 4 - Select Durable Planking Woods: Cedar, spruce, cypress, and pine are good planking woods (p. 25).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which statement accurately compares common rowboat hull materials?
quiz_item.question: Which statement accurately compares common rowboat hull materials?
options: A. Aluminum is naturally buoyant and floats without any internal air or foam chambers.
B. Fiberglass is the easiest material to cut and nail with hand tools at camp.
C. Wood planking sinks immediately when swamped unless fitted with metal air tanks.
D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
choices: A. Aluminum is naturally buoyant and floats without any internal air or foam chambers.
B. Fiberglass is the easiest material to cut and nail with hand tools at camp.
C. Wood planking sinks immediately when swamped unless fitted with metal air tanks.
D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Wood is easy to cut and drill and floats naturally even when the boat is full of water.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Wood planking is easy to cut and drill and has natural buoyancy that keeps a wooden rowboat afloat even when filled with water, whereas aluminum requires built-in flotation chambers (p. 25).
