pamphlet_excerpts: AVMA Program Accreditation Standards: The American Veterinary Medical Association accredits veterinary technician programs throughout the United States (p. 30).
Formal Technician Education Entry: Training to become a veterinary technician usually begins in one of these programs (p. 30).
Two-Year Associate Degree Path: Most accredited programs lead to an associate's degree after two years of study (p. 30).
Four-Year Bachelor Degree Advancement: However, veterinary technicians with a bachelor of science degree typically earn a higher salary and have more responsibilities (p. 30).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Complete an Accredited Degree Program: Most accredited programs lead to an associate's degree after two years of study (p. 30).
Step 2 - Consider a Bachelor Science Degree: However, veterinary technicians with a bachelor of science degree typically earn a higher salary and have more responsibilities (p. 30).

Step 3 - Gain Clinical Hands-On Training: In addition to course work, students of veterinary technician programs complete a certain amount of hands-on training, which is acritical part of all (p. 30).
Step 4 - Pass State and National Exams: Finally, nearly every state requires that veterinary technicians pass a state and/or national examination to be eligible to practice (p. 30).

Prepare a presentation and share what you have learned about this field of veterinary medicine with your counselor. Include how this field serves the needs of the general public.

pamphlet_excerpts: Connected Research Medicine Fields: Laboratory animal medicine and research veterinary medicine have much in common (p. 16).
Broad Scientific Skill Application: Both fields apply the skills learned in veterinary school to a number of areas of study (p. 16).
Medical Care in Research Facilities: A veterinarian working in laboratory animal medicine provides medical care for animals used in research (p. 16).
Collaborative Scientific Team Roles: The veterinarian sometimes is a member of the research team and helps design studies, interpret results, and publish articles about the research (p. 16).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Observe Research Animal Medical Care: A veterinarian working in laboratory animal medicine provides medical care for animals used in research (p. 16).
Step 2 - Examine Study Design Collaboration: The veterinarian sometimes is a member of the research team and helps design studies, interpret results, and publish articles about the research (p. 16).
Step 3 - Review Diagnostic and Medical Innovations: Research veterinarians investigate new medicines, biotechnical and diagnostic tests, food technologies, and other new technologies (p. 16).
Step 4 - Explore Infectious Disease Surveillance: Research veterinarians might also investigate the exotic and infectious diseases that threaten public health (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Beyond treating sick pets in a clinic, how do veterinarians protect human public health and the nation's food supply?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Beyond treating sick pets in a clinic, how do veterinarians protect human public health and the nation's food supply?
options: A. By prescribing human antibiotics to grocery store produce departments.
B. By controlling zoonotic diseases (such as rabies, brucellosis, and avian influenza) that can pass from animals to humans, and inspecting livestock health and food safety from farm to table.
C. By breeding wild predators to replace domestic cattle and poultry on commercial ranches.
D. By restricting vaccinations exclusively to indoor house cats and ornamental aquarium fish.
choices: A. By prescribing human antibiotics to grocery store produce departments.
B. By controlling zoonotic diseases (such as rabies, brucellosis, and avian influenza) that can pass from animals to humans, and inspecting livestock health and food safety from farm to table.
C. By breeding wild predators to replace domestic cattle and poultry on commercial ranches.
D. By restricting vaccinations exclusively to indoor house cats and ornamental aquarium fish.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. By controlling zoonotic diseases (such as rabies, brucellosis, and avian influenza) that can pass from animals to humans, and inspecting livestock health and food safety from farm to table.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Veterinarians play a vital One Health role by preventing zoonotic disease spill over between animals and people (such as rabies vaccination) and safeguarding livestock health and food safety.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: In addition to providing medical care for animals used in research, how do veterinarians contribute to laboratory research teams?
options: A. They help design studies, interpret data, and investigate new medicines and diagnostic tests
B. They restrict their work to facility sanitation and building maintenance
C. They only sell pharmaceutical supplies to private pet clinics
D. They enforce local pet licensing ordinances for county shelters
choices: A. They help design studies, interpret data, and investigate new medicines and diagnostic tests
B. They restrict their work to facility sanitation and building maintenance
C. They only sell pharmaceutical supplies to private pet clinics
D. They enforce local pet licensing ordinances for county shelters
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. They help design studies, interpret data, and investigate new medicines and diagnostic tests
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Veterinarians in laboratory animal medicine and research serve on scientific teams to design studies, interpret results, publish findings, and investigate new medicines, diagnostic tests, and infectious diseases (p. 30).

Relocating to Shade or Cooling: Move the person to an air-conditioned or shady area (p. 28).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Lower the Victim Body Temperature: While waiting for medical personnel to arrive, work to lower the victim's temperature (p. 28).
Step 2 - Move Victim to Shade Immediately: Move the person to an air-conditioned or shady area (p. 28).
Step 3 - Loosen Clothing and Apply Towels: Loosen tight clothing and further cool the victim by fanning and applying wet towels (p. 28).
Step 4 - Immerse or Spray With Water: If possible, immerse or spray the person with cold water (p. 28).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When towing a water-skier or wakeboarder behind a motorboat, what crew roles, lifejacket gear, and boarding procedures are required for safety?
quiz_item.question: When towing a water-skier or wakeboarder behind a motorboat, what crew roles, lifejacket gear, and boarding procedures are required for safety?
options: A. The boat driver watches the skier in a rear view mirror without a spotter, and the engine stays in neutral while the skier climbs the swim platform.
B. The skier wears an inflatable belt pack only if they cannot swim, and signals 'stop' by waving both arms up and down.

C. A dedicated observer must watch the skier and relay hand signals so the driver stays focused ahead, the skier must wear a USCG-approved PFD rated for water impact, and the engine must be shut off completely before anyone approaches the stern to board.
D. Two boats should tow the same skier side-by-side so one boat can block wakes from passing vessels.
choices: A. The boat driver watches the skier in a rear view mirror without a spotter, and the engine stays in neutral while the skier climbs the swim platform.
B. The skier wears an inflatable belt pack only if they cannot swim, and signals 'stop' by waving both arms up and down.

C. A dedicated observer must watch the skier and relay hand signals so the driver stays focused ahead, the skier must wear a USCG-approved PFD rated for water impact, and the engine must be shut off completely before anyone approaches the stern to board.
D. Two boats should tow the same skier side-by-side so one boat can block wakes from passing vessels.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. A dedicated observer must watch the skier and relay hand signals so the driver stays focused ahead, the skier must wear a USCG-approved PFD rated for water impact, and the engine must be shut off completely before anyone approaches the stern to board.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Safe water skiing and wakeboarding require a dedicated observer in addition to the operator, a USCG-approved Type III PFD, clear hand signals, and turning the engine completely off before a skier reboards near the propeller.

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Never Substitute Throwable Devices: They should never be used in place of a lifejacket (p. 17).

pamphlet_excerpts: Mandatory Swimmer Classification Requirement: Swimming Ability All water-skiers and wake boarders must have passed the Scouting America swimmer test (p. 12).
Rules for Boat Passengers: Anyone not classified as a swimmer may ride as a passenger in the boat when the operator is a skilled adult (p. 12).
Coast Guard Approved Life Jackets: Lifejackets Properly fitted U. S. Coast Guard-approved lifejackets must be worn by all persons engaged in boating activity (p. 12).
Recommended Recreational Type III Vests: Type III lifejackets are recommended for general recreational use (p. 12).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Wear Coast Guard Approved Vests: Lifejackets Properly fitted U. S. Coast Guard-approved lifejackets must be worn by all persons engaged in boating activity (p. 12).
Step 2 - Choose Type III Recreational Vests: Type III lifejackets are recommended for general recreational use (p. 12).
Step 3 - Verify Water Skiing Vest Rating: All participants in towed activity afloat (water skiing, wake boarding, knee boarding, tubing, etc.) must wear a lifejacket marked for water skiing (p. 12).
Step 4 - Maintain the Buddy System Afloat: Buddy System All participants in water sports activities must use the buddy system (p. 12).

pamphlet_excerpts: Driver Turn Alert Signal: The driver may use this signal to alert the skier that the boat is about to turn (p. 20).
Skier Directional Turn Request: If the skier wants the driver to turn, the skier uses the same signal followed by pointing in the direction he or she wants the driver (p. 20).
Overcoming Boat Engine and Wind Noise: Once a skier is under way, the noise from the boat makes hearing instructions difficult (p. 20).
Standardized Skier Hand Signals: The skier must learn to give directions by using the hand signals shown here (p. 20).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Account for Engine Noise Afloat: Once a skier is under way, the noise from the boat makes hearing instructions difficult (p. 20).
Step 2 - Demonstrate Standard Skier Hand Signals: The skier must learn to give directions by using the hand signals shown here (p. 20).
Step 3 - Communicate Through the Safety Observer: The observer serves as the eyes and the ears for the driver and skier (p. 20).
Step 4 - Apply Signals Across All Boards: Note that "skier" refers to both water-skiers and wake boarders (p. 20).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why does a boat towing a water-skier or wakeboarder require both a driver and a dedicated safety observer?
quiz_item.question: Why does a boat towing a water-skier or wakeboarder require both a driver and a dedicated safety observer?
options: A. Because two people are needed to hold the steering wheel during turns
B. Because the observer must swim behind the boat with a spare ski
C. Because the driver is not allowed to know the meanings of hand signals
D. Because engine noise blocks voice commands, so the observer watches the skier's hand signals and falls while the driver watches the water ahead
choices: A. Because two people are needed to hold the steering wheel during turns
B. Because the observer must swim behind the boat with a spare ski
C. Because the driver is not allowed to know the meanings of hand signals
D. Because engine noise blocks voice commands, so the observer watches the skier's hand signals and falls while the driver watches the water ahead
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Because engine noise blocks voice commands, so the observer watches the skier's hand signals and falls while the driver watches the water ahead
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Once under way, boat noise prevents verbal communication, so the observer serves as the eyes and ears for the driver and skier by watching hand signals and reporting them to the driver (p. 20).

pamphlet_excerpts: Front Foot Weight for Stability: To keep the board from wobbling, puts lightly more weight on your front foot than on your back foot as the boat begins Alternate Method for Deep water (p. 59).
Partially Rotated Wakeboard Start Option: You may prefer to start out with the wake board partially rotated uptoward the front foot (p. 59).
Parallel Board Starting Position: Begin with the wake board out in front of you and parallel to the water's surface (p. 59).
Bent Knees and Straight Arms: Keep your knees bent and hold the rope handle with your arms straight (p. 59).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Position Board Parallel in Front: Begin with the wake board out in front of you and parallel to the water's surface (p. 59).
Step 2 - Bend Knees With Arms Straight: Keep your knees bent and hold the rope handle with your arms straight (p. 59).
Step 3 - Signal Driver to Accelerate Smoothly: When you are in position and ready, shout out "Hit it!" to let the driver know to accelerate (p. 59).
Step 4 - Rotate Hips Into Riding Stance: As soon as the boat starts to pull, twist at the hips to turn the front of the board up and toward the boat (p. 59).

pamphlet_excerpts: Skill-Based Wakeboard Foot Angles: With wake boards, the angle of your feet on the board can be adjusted depending on your skill level (p. 17).
Finding a Comfortable Beginner Stance: As a beginner, you'll want to follow the steps below, fine-tuning the adjustments to find a stance that feels most comfortable (p. 17).
Shoulder-Width Binding Stance Spacing: Adjust the distance between the bindings to about shoulder-width apart, with your back foot slightly more toward the rear of the board for better (p. 17).
Back Foot Angle Alignment: Adjust the angle of the back foot so that it is straight across the board or turned outs lightly toward the back (at zero to 9 degrees) (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Set Bindings Shoulder-Width Apart: Adjust the distance between the bindings to about shoulder-width apart, with your back foot slightly more toward the rear of the board for better (p. 17).
Step 2 - Align Back Binding Angle: Adjust the angle of the back foot so that it is straight across the board or turned outs lightly toward the back (at zero to 9 degrees) (p. 17).
Step 3 - Angle Front Binding Outward: Adjust the angle of the front foot so that it is slightly turned outtoward the front (9 to 27 degrees) (p. 17).
Step 4 - Test Binding Fit on Shore: Try the board on for size before you hit the water (p. 17).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When towing a water-skier or wakeboarder behind a motorboat, what crew roles, lifejacket gear, and boarding procedures are required for safety?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When towing a water-skier or wakeboarder behind a motorboat, what crew roles, lifejacket gear, and boarding procedures are required for safety?
options: A. The boat driver watches the skier in a rear view mirror without a spotter, and the engine stays in neutral while the skier climbs the swim platform.
B. The skier wears an inflatable belt pack only if they cannot swim, and signals 'stop' by waving both arms up and down.

C. A dedicated observer must watch the skier and relay hand signals so the driver stays focused ahead, the skier must wear a USCG-approved PFD rated for water impact, and the engine must be shut off completely before anyone approaches the stern to board.
D. Two boats should tow the same skier side-by-side so one boat can block wakes from passing vessels.
choices: A. The boat driver watches the skier in a rear view mirror without a spotter, and the engine stays in neutral while the skier climbs the swim platform.
B. The skier wears an inflatable belt pack only if they cannot swim, and signals 'stop' by waving both arms up and down.

C. A dedicated observer must watch the skier and relay hand signals so the driver stays focused ahead, the skier must wear a USCG-approved PFD rated for water impact, and the engine must be shut off completely before anyone approaches the stern to board.
D. Two boats should tow the same skier side-by-side so one boat can block wakes from passing vessels.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. A dedicated observer must watch the skier and relay hand signals so the driver stays focused ahead, the skier must wear a USCG-approved PFD rated for water impact, and the engine must be shut off completely before anyone approaches the stern to board.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Safe water skiing and wakeboarding require a dedicated observer in addition to the operator, a USCG-approved Type III PFD, clear hand signals, and turning the engine completely off before a skier reboards near the propeller.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Your patrol is hiking across an open alpine ridgeline when towering cumulonimbus clouds build rapidly and you hear thunder 10 seconds after seeing a lightning flash (roughly 2 miles away). What is the safest immediate action for the patrol?
quiz_item.question: Your patrol is hiking across an open alpine ridgeline when towering cumulonimbus clouds build rapidly and you hear thunder 10 seconds after seeing a lightning flash (roughly 2 miles away). What is the safest immediate action for the patrol?
options: A. Stay on the ridgeline under a tall isolated pine tree to keep dry until the rain passes.

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.
D. Lie flat on wet granite at the summit so the wind blows over the patrol.
choices: A. Stay on the ridgeline under a tall isolated pine tree to keep dry until the rain passes.

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.
D. Lie flat on wet granite at the summit so the wind blows over the patrol.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Sound travels about 1 mile every 5 seconds; a 10-second flash-to-bang interval means lightning is within 2 miles and already in strike range, requiring immediate descent from ridges and avoidance of tall isolated objects.

pamphlet_excerpts: Routine Air Mass Changes: People readily adapt to routine weather changes that occur with the passage of air masses (p. 29).
Violent and Extreme Weather: Sometimes, however, the weather can become so violent or the temperature so extreme that people need to take special precautions (p. 29).
National Weather Service Alerts: Forecasters with the National Weather Service issue watches, warnings, and advisories to alert the public to potentially violent or hazardous (p. 29).
Watch Versus Warning Distinction: There is an important difference between a watch and a warning (p. 29).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Monitor Official Weather Alerts: Forecasters with the National Weather Service issue watches, warnings, and advisories to alert the public to potentially violent or hazardous (p. 29).
Step 2 - Distinguish Alert Levels: There is an important difference between a watch and a warning (p. 29).
Step 3 - Prepare During Weather Watches: A watch means that hazardous weather is possible or that conditions are favorable for it to develop (p. 29).
Step 4 - Seek Shelter Under Warnings: A warning is a more urgent notice that hazardous conditions already exist or are heading your way (p. 29).

pamphlet_excerpts: First Weather Satellite Launch: The first weather satellite, known as TIROS-1, was launched in the spring of 1960 (p. 33).
Viewing Complete Storm Systems: It was highly successful at giving meteorologists their first overall view of entire storm systems (p. 33).
Continuous Global Storm Monitoring: Since then, satellites have become much more sophisticated, allowing a nearly continuous watch over the entire Earth (p. 33).
Primary Weather Satellite Types: Polar-orbiting satellites and geostationary satellites (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Track Global Satellite Imagery: Since then, satellites have become much more sophisticated, allowing a nearly continuous watch over the entire Earth (p. 33).
Step 2 - Compare Satellite Orbit Types: Polar-orbiting satellites and geostationary satellites (p. 33).
Step 3 - Use POES and GOES: The satellite systems are named Polar Operational Environmental Satellites (POES) and Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (p. 33).
Step 4 - Analyze Polar Orbit Data: The polar-orbiting satellites circle Earth, passing over or near the poles at a height of approximately 520 miles (p. 33).

pamphlet_excerpts: Ecological Benefits of Lightning: Although lightning can be hazardous, it is not all bad (p. 34).
Atmospheric Nitrogen Fixation: It changes the air's nitrogen into a form that can be taken up by plants (p. 34).
Natural Thunderstorm Plant Fertilizer: Thus, athunderstorm can be a natural plant fertilizer as well as a water er (p. 34).
High-Risk Lightning Strike Zones: Although the location where lightning will strike is not predictable, some places are much more likely to be struck than others (p. 34).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Explain Thunderstorm Nitrogen Fixation: Thus, athunderstorm can be a natural plant fertilizer as well as a water er (p. 34).
Step 2 - Identify Exposed Strike Targets: Although the location where lightning will strike is not predictable, some places are much more likely to be struck than others (p. 34).
Step 3 - Trace Electrical Resistance Paths: Because lightning follows the path of least resistance, objects closer to the cloud are more likely to be struck (p. 34).
Step 4 - Avoid Isolated Tall Trees: Trees in an otherwise open space often are targets for lightning, so trees are not a good place to take shelter in a thunderstorm (p. 34).

pamphlet_excerpts: Four Altitude Cloud Families: Low clouds, middle clouds, high clouds, and clouds that develop vertically (p. 8).
High-Altitude Cirrus Clouds: Meteorologists also consider the shapes of clouds. clouds are The highest clouds are generally above 20,000 feet and are called cirrus clouds (p. 8).
Ice Crystal Cloud Composition: Cirrus clouds are composed entirely of ice crystals because of their low temperatures and the heights where they form (p. 8).
Wispy Mare's Tail Formations: Cirrocumulus clouds can be arranged in patches or aligned in rows. sometimes called "mare's tails" because they look a bit like ahorse's tail (p. 8).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Identify High Ice Clouds: Cirrus clouds are composed entirely of ice crystals because of their low temperatures and the heights where they form (p. 8).
Step 2 - Spot Wispy Cirrus Streaks: Cirrocumulus clouds can be arranged in patches or aligned in rows. sometimes called "mare's tails" because they look a bit like ahorse's tail (p. 8).
Step 3 - Observe Atmospheric Air Currents: Earth's atmosphere can be thought of as an ocean (p. 8).
Step 4 - Link Clouds to Weather: Its restless movement is the source of everything people call weather (p. 8).

pamphlet_excerpts: Atmospheric Moisture and Life: The most important thing about the weather is the moisture it brings (p. 16).
Essential Role of Rainfall: The wind could blow night and day and the temperature could rise and fall, but if no rain fell, Earth would be in real trouble (p. 16).
Earth's Water-Circulating System: Fortunately, in addition to a wonderful air-circulating system, Earth has a wonderful water-circulating system (p. 16).
Oceanic Evaporation Moisture Source: The water vapor that forms clouds and precipitation comes mostly from evaporation from Earth's oceans (p. 16).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Diagram Global Water Circulation: Fortunately, in addition to a wonderful air-circulating system, Earth has a wonderful water-circulating system (p. 16).
Step 2 - Label Ocean Evaporation Arrows: The water vapor that forms clouds and precipitation comes mostly from evaporation from Earth's oceans (p. 16).
Step 3 - Include Plant Leaf Transpiration: A small part comes from lakes, streams, and transpiration, that is, the giving off of water by the leaves of green plants (p. 16).
Step 4 - Trace Wind Vapor Transport: Most of the rain that falls over land evaporates and is transported as water vapor by the winds, often many thousands of miles from its source (p. 16).

pamphlet_excerpts: Short-Term Atmospheric Conditions: Recall that weather is the condition of the atmosphere over aparticular area for a short time (p. 66).
Thirty-Year Regional Climate Averages: Climate is the average of the weather over a region for a longer time, such as 30 years (p. 66).
Greek Origin Meaning Solar Angle: The word climate comes from the Greek word klima, meaning "angle." This name was used because the angle at which the sun strikes Earth largely determines (p. 66).
Direct Overhead Equatorial Sunlight: At the equator, the sun is nearly straight overhead most of the year, so most of the equatorial region is hot (p. 66).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Examine Solar Incidence Angles: The word climate comes from the Greek word klima, meaning "angle." This name was used because the angle at which the sun strikes Earth largely determines (p. 66).
Step 2 - Compare Equatorial Heating Intensity: At the equator, the sun is nearly straight overhead most of the year, so most of the equatorial region is hot (p. 66).
Step 3 - Trace Latitude Temperature Gradients: Pole ward from the equator, the climate gradually shifts from hot to cold (p. 66).
Step 4 - Model Earth's 23.5-Degree Tilt: This tilt (about 23.5 degrees from the perpendicular) remains the same all year as seen from deep space (top) but changes relative to the sun (p. 66).

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Make one of the following instruments: wind vane, anemometer, rain gauge, or hygrometer. Keep a daily weather log for one week using information from this instrument as well as from other sources such as local radio and television stations, NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards, and internet sources (with your parent or guardian's permission). Record the following information at the same time every day: wind direction and speed, temperature, precipitation, and types of clouds. Be sure to make a note of any morning dew or frost. In the log, also list the weather forecasts from radio or television at the same time each day and show how the weather really turned out. (b) Visit a National Weather Service office or talk with a local radio or television weathercaster, private meteorologist, local agricultural extension service officer, or university meteorology instructor. Find out what type of weather is most dangerous or damaging to your community. Determine how severe weather and flood warnings reach the homes in your community.

pamphlet_excerpts: Observing and Recording Weather: Measuring and Recording the Weather The most obvious way to study the weather is to observe actual events and keep a record of what you see (p. 61).
Tracking Daily Weather Elements: Daily observations of temperature, wind, pressure, clouds, and rainfall can help you understand how the atmosphere behaves (p. 61).
Maintaining Weekly Weather Logs: Keep a daily weatherlog, similar to the one shown, for at least a week (p. 61).
Extending Observations Over Months: If possible, record observations for a month (p. 61).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Log Daily Readings Weekly: Keep a daily weatherlog, similar to the one shown, for at least a week (p. 61).
Step 2 - Continue Monthly Weather Tracking: If possible, record observations for a month (p. 61).
Step 3 - Combine Instrument and Broadcast Data: You can obtain readings from your own instruments, from local television or radio, and from internet sites devoted to meteorology (p. 61).
Step 4 - Compare Day-to-Day Atmospheric Trends: By comparing readings from day to day, you can see how the various weather elements change at your location in response to passing weather (p. 61).

pamphlet_excerpts: Understanding Lightning Hazard Realities: Although lightning can be hazardous, it is not all bad (p. 37).
Nitrogen Conversion in Storms: It changes the air's nitrogen into a form that can be taken up by plants (p. 37).
Dual Role of Thunderstorms: Thus, athunderstorm can be a natural plant fertilizer as well as a water er (p. 37).
Predicting High-Probability Strike Locations: Although the location where lightning will strike is not predictable, some places are much more likely to be struck than others (p. 37).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Draft Five-Minute Safety Outline: Thus, athunderstorm can be a natural plant fertilizer as well as a water er (p. 37).
Step 2 - Highlight High-Risk Outdoor Locations: Although the location where lightning will strike is not predictable, some places are much more likely to be struck than others (p. 37).
Step 3 - Explain Path of Least Resistance: Because lightning follows the path of least resistance, objects closer to the cloud are more likely to be struck (p. 37).
Step 4 - Teach Proper Lightning Shelter: Trees in an otherwise open space often are targets for lightning, so trees are not a good place to take shelter in a thunderstorm (p. 37).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Your patrol is hiking across an open alpine ridgeline when towering cumulonimbus clouds build rapidly and you hear thunder 10 seconds after seeing a lightning flash (roughly 2 miles away). What is the safest immediate action for the patrol?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Your patrol is hiking across an open alpine ridgeline when towering cumulonimbus clouds build rapidly and you hear thunder 10 seconds after seeing a lightning flash (roughly 2 miles away). What is the safest immediate action for the patrol?
options: A. Stay on the ridgeline under a tall isolated pine tree to keep dry until the rain passes.

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.
D. Lie flat on wet granite at the summit so the wind blows over the patrol.
choices: A. Stay on the ridgeline under a tall isolated pine tree to keep dry until the rain passes.

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.
D. Lie flat on wet granite at the summit so the wind blows over the patrol.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Sound travels about 1 mile every 5 seconds; a 10-second flash-to-bang interval means lightning is within 2 miles and already in strike range, requiring immediate descent from ridges and avoidance of tall isolated objects.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What does a National Weather Service severe weather warning mean for your Scout unit when outdoors?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What does a National Weather Service severe weather warning mean for your Scout unit when outdoors?
options: A. Hazardous weather is possible later in the week, so continue outdoor activities normally
B. Seasonal climate averages suggest higher rainfall than normal this month
C. Hazardous weather is already occurring or imminent, and you must take immediate shelter
D. A cold front has completely passed and skies are clearing
choices: A. Hazardous weather is possible later in the week, so continue outdoor activities normally
B. Seasonal climate averages suggest higher rainfall than normal this month
C. Hazardous weather is already occurring or imminent, and you must take immediate shelter
D. A cold front has completely passed and skies are clearing
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Hazardous weather is already occurring or imminent, and you must take immediate shelter
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A National Weather Service warning is an urgent notice that hazardous weather conditions already exist or are heading directly toward your area (p. 29).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which satellite system circles Earth at an altitude of approximately 520 miles while passing over or near the North and South Poles?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which satellite system circles Earth at an altitude of approximately 520 miles while passing over or near the North and South Poles?
options: A. Polar Operational Environmental Satellites (POES)
B. Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES)
C. Local Doppler weather radar towers
D. Automated surface weather balloons
choices: A. Polar Operational Environmental Satellites (POES)
B. Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES)
C. Local Doppler weather radar towers
D. Automated surface weather balloons
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Polar Operational Environmental Satellites (POES)
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Polar-orbiting satellites circle Earth from pole to pole at roughly 520 miles high, whereas geostationary satellites remain above a fixed spot on the equator (p. 33).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens when an advancing cold front meets a mass of warmer air?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens when an advancing cold front meets a mass of warmer air?
options: A. Cold air rises high above the warm air mass and dissipates all clouds
B. Warm and cold air mix evenly without vertical motion or precipitation
C. Cold air glides gently on top of the warm air across hundreds of miles
D. Dense cold air stays near the surface and wedges beneath the warm air, forcing it upward
choices: A. Cold air rises high above the warm air mass and dissipates all clouds
B. Warm and cold air mix evenly without vertical motion or precipitation
C. Cold air glides gently on top of the warm air across hundreds of miles
D. Dense cold air stays near the surface and wedges beneath the warm air, forcing it upward
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Dense cold air stays near the surface and wedges beneath the warm air, forcing it upward
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Because cold air is denser than warm air, it stays near the surface and wedges beneath the warmer air, forcing the warm air to rise rapidly along a steep slope (p. 29).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Besides providing water from rain, how does a thunderstorm with lightning benefit plant life?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Besides providing water from rain, how does a thunderstorm with lightning benefit plant life?
options: A. It burns away excess oxygen in the upper stratosphere
B. It converts atmospheric nitrogen into a form that plants can absorb as fertilizer
C. It melts high-altitude cirrus clouds into warm summer rain
D. It neutralizes barometric pressure differences across the equator
choices: A. It burns away excess oxygen in the upper stratosphere
B. It converts atmospheric nitrogen into a form that plants can absorb as fertilizer
C. It melts high-altitude cirrus clouds into warm summer rain
D. It neutralizes barometric pressure differences across the equator
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It converts atmospheric nitrogen into a form that plants can absorb as fertilizer
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Lightning converts nitrogen in the air into compounds that dissolve in rain and can be absorbed by plants as natural fertilizer (p. 34).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which clouds generally form above 20,000 feet, are composed entirely of ice crystals, and are sometimes called "mare's tails"?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which clouds generally form above 20,000 feet, are composed entirely of ice crystals, and are sometimes called "mare's tails"?
options: A. Stratus clouds forming below 6,500 feet
B. Cumulus clouds with flat, low bases
C. Cirrus clouds forming above 20,000 feet
D. Nimbostratus rain clouds near the ground
choices: A. Stratus clouds forming below 6,500 feet
B. Cumulus clouds with flat, low bases
C. Cirrus clouds forming above 20,000 feet
D. Nimbostratus rain clouds near the ground
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Cirrus clouds forming above 20,000 feet
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Cirrus clouds form at high altitudes generally above 20,000 feet where cold temperatures cause them to be composed entirely of ice crystals (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In the water cycle, what is the name for the process in which the leaves of green plants give off water vapor into the atmosphere?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In the water cycle, what is the name for the process in which the leaves of green plants give off water vapor into the atmosphere?
options: A. Transpiration
B. Sublimation
C. Infiltration
D. Coalescence
choices: A. Transpiration
B. Sublimation
C. Infiltration
D. Coalescence
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Transpiration
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Transpiration is the process in which green plants release water vapor into the atmosphere through their leaves (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which human activities significantly increase atmospheric carbon dioxide levels and alter regional and global climate patterns?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which human activities significantly increase atmospheric carbon dioxide levels and alter regional and global climate patterns?
options: A. Planting shade trees in residential neighborhoods
B. Measuring rainfall with a backyard rain gauge
C. Rotating farm crops to preserve topsoil moisture
D. Burning fossil fuels and clearing large areas of forest
choices: A. Planting shade trees in residential neighborhoods
B. Measuring rainfall with a backyard rain gauge
C. Rotating farm crops to preserve topsoil moisture
D. Burning fossil fuels and clearing large areas of forest
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Burning fossil fuels and clearing large areas of forest
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Burning fossil fuels and clearing forests increase atmospheric carbon dioxide, while sulfur and nitrogen emissions react with cloud moisture to produce acid rain (p. 68).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is the climate near the equator consistently hot compared to the regions near the North and South Poles?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is the climate near the equator consistently hot compared to the regions near the North and South Poles?
options: A. The equator is thousands of miles closer to the sun than the poles
B. Sunlight strikes the equator nearly straight overhead all year, concentrating solar energy
C. Ocean currents prevent any clouds from forming over the equator
D. Earth spins slower at the poles than at the equator
choices: A. The equator is thousands of miles closer to the sun than the poles
B. Sunlight strikes the equator nearly straight overhead all year, concentrating solar energy
C. Ocean currents prevent any clouds from forming over the equator
D. Earth spins slower at the poles than at the equator
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Sunlight strikes the equator nearly straight overhead all year, concentrating solar energy
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The word climate comes from the Greek word klima, meaning "angle," because the angle at which sunlight strikes Earth largely determines regional temperatures (p. 66).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: If you build a hygrometer for Requirement 10a, which weather element does your instrument measure?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: If you build a hygrometer for Requirement 10a, which weather element does your instrument measure?
options: A. Wind direction in compass degrees
B. Peak wind gust speed in knots
C. Relative humidity of the air
D. Barometric air pressure in millibars
choices: A. Wind direction in compass degrees
B. Peak wind gust speed in knots
C. Relative humidity of the air
D. Barometric air pressure in millibars
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Relative humidity of the air
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A hygrometer measures the relative humidity of the air, often using the length change of a human hair or wet- and dry-bulb thermometers (p. 61).

pamphlet_excerpts: Post-Weld Fire Watch: Continue inspecting for fire for 30 minutes after welding (p. 21).
Superficial Skin Burns: Superficial burns are mild burns that affect only the outer layer of skin (p. 21).
Cooling Minor Burns: Treat them by holding the burn under cold water or applying cool, wet compresses until the pain eases (p. 21).
Partial-Thickness Burn Severity: Partial-thickness burns are more serious than superficial burns and affect the outer layer of skin and part of the layer of skin (p. 21).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Apply Cool Wet Compresses: Treat them by holding the burn under cold water or applying cool, wet compresses until the pain eases (p. 21).
Step 2 - Assess Deeper Skin Damage: Partial-thickness burns are more serious than superficial burns and affect the outer layer of skin and part of the layer of skin (p. 21).
Step 3 - Check for Skin Blistering: They typically include areddening and blistering of the skin (p. 21).
Step 4 - Remove From Heat Source: To treat such burns, first remove the person from the source of the burn (p. 21).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why must a welder wear a properly shaded welding helmet (such as Shade 10 to 13 for arc welding) and flame-resistant leather or heavy cotton clothing rather than synthetic polyester or fleece?
quiz_item.question: Why must a welder wear a properly shaded welding helmet (such as Shade 10 to 13 for arc welding) and flame-resistant leather or heavy cotton clothing rather than synthetic polyester or fleece?
options: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns, while sparks and hot slag can melt synthetic fabrics directly into the skin.
B. A clear plastic face shield blocks all ultraviolet arc rays, and polyester fleece reflects molten spatter better than leather.
C. Welding helmets are only needed to keep smoke out of your eyes, and synthetic gym shorts keep the welder cool during overhead passes.
D. Sunglasses provide enough shade protection for MIG and stick welding as long as you squint during the strike.
choices: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns, while sparks and hot slag can melt synthetic fabrics directly into the skin.
B. A clear plastic face shield blocks all ultraviolet arc rays, and polyester fleece reflects molten spatter better than leather.
C. Welding helmets are only needed to keep smoke out of your eyes, and synthetic gym shorts keep the welder cool during overhead passes.
D. Sunglasses provide enough shade protection for MIG and stick welding as long as you squint during the strike.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns, while sparks and hot slag can melt synthetic fabrics directly into the skin.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): An electric welding arc produces intense UV and IR radiation that burns unprotected retinas and corneas in seconds, and hot slag ignites or melts synthetic fabrics like nylon or polyester onto skin.

Step 4 - Select Correct Current Polarity: The current may be either alternating or direct (electrode positive or electrode negative), depending on the electrode being used (p. 32).

pamphlet_excerpts: Torch Valve Shutdown Sequence: Welding for the Novice When you are ready to close down the equipment, turn off the torch oxygen valve; then, turn off the fuel valve (p. 71).
Draining Oxygen Line Pressure: Close the cylinder valves, then open the torch oxygen valve to allow the oxygen to drain, and close the torch oxygen valve (p. 71).
Releasing Oxygen Regulator Tension: Release the adjusting screw on the oxygen regulator (p. 71).
Purging Fuel Gas Hoses: Open the torch-fuel valve to drain fuel gas, and then close (p. 71).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Back Out Oxygen Regulator: Release the adjusting screw on the oxygen regulator (p. 71).
Step 2 - Bleed Fuel Gas Line: Open the torch-fuel valve to drain fuel gas, and then close (p. 71).
Step 3 - Loosen Fuel Regulator Screw: Release the adjusting screw on the fuel-gas regulator (p. 71).
Step 4 - Assemble Standard Weld Joints: Common joints are butt joints, T-joints, and lap joints (p. 71).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why must a welder wear a properly shaded welding helmet (such as Shade 10 to 13 for arc welding) and flame-resistant leather or heavy cotton clothing rather than synthetic polyester or fleece?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why must a welder wear a properly shaded welding helmet (such as Shade 10 to 13 for arc welding) and flame-resistant leather or heavy cotton clothing rather than synthetic polyester or fleece?
options: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns, while sparks and hot slag can melt synthetic fabrics directly into the skin.
B. A clear plastic face shield blocks all ultraviolet arc rays, and polyester fleece reflects molten spatter better than leather.
C. Welding helmets are only needed to keep smoke out of your eyes, and synthetic gym shorts keep the welder cool during overhead passes.
D. Sunglasses provide enough shade protection for MIG and stick welding as long as you squint during the strike.
choices: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns, while sparks and hot slag can melt synthetic fabrics directly into the skin.
B. A clear plastic face shield blocks all ultraviolet arc rays, and polyester fleece reflects molten spatter better than leather.
C. Welding helmets are only needed to keep smoke out of your eyes, and synthetic gym shorts keep the welder cool during overhead passes.
D. Sunglasses provide enough shade protection for MIG and stick welding as long as you squint during the strike.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns, while sparks and hot slag can melt synthetic fabrics directly into the skin.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): An electric welding arc produces intense UV and IR radiation that burns unprotected retinas and corneas in seconds, and hot slag ignites or melts synthetic fabrics like nylon or polyester onto skin.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which section of a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) specifies the exposure limits and personal protective equipment required when working with welding consumables?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which section of a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) specifies the exposure limits and personal protective equipment required when working with welding consumables?
options: A. Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
B. Physical and Chemical Properties
C. Ecological and Disposal Information
D. Transport and Regulatory Information
choices: A. Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
B. Physical and Chemical Properties
C. Ecological and Disposal Information
D. Transport and Regulatory Information
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The Exposure Controls/Personal Protection section of an SDS identifies airborne exposure limits and specifies the protective gear needed to minimize worker exposure (p. 13).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Approximately how hot does the electric arc get to melt both the electrode tip and the base metal during arc welding?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Approximately how hot does the electric arc get to melt both the electrode tip and the base metal during arc welding?
options: A. Around 1,200 degrees Fahrenheit
B. Roughly 3,500 degrees Fahrenheit
C. Just under 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit
D. Above 9,000 degrees Fahrenheit
choices: A. Around 1,200 degrees Fahrenheit
B. Roughly 3,500 degrees Fahrenheit
C. Just under 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit
D. Above 9,000 degrees Fahrenheit
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Above 9,000 degrees Fahrenheit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): The electric arc generates intense heat measuring above 9,000 degrees Fahrenheit, which rapidly melts both the tip of the electrode and the base metal surface (p. 32).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is shielded metal arc equipment particularly well-suited for outdoor construction and remote repair work?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is shielded metal arc equipment particularly well-suited for outdoor construction and remote repair work?
options: A. It produces zero fumes and never requires ventilation
B. It is portable with engine generators and resists wind drafts
C. It uses an endless spool of wire that never needs changing
D. It operates without any electrical current or ground clamp
choices: A. It produces zero fumes and never requires ventilation
B. It is portable with engine generators and resists wind drafts
C. It uses an endless spool of wire that never needs changing
D. It operates without any electrical current or ground clamp
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It is portable with engine generators and resists wind drafts
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Shielded metal arc equipment can be powered by portable gasoline or diesel generators and is much less sensitive to outdoor wind and drafts than gas-shielded processes (p. 39).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why must you inspect oxygen regulators, hoses, and torch fittings to ensure they are completely free of oil and grease before connecting them?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why must you inspect oxygen regulators, hoses, and torch fittings to ensure they are completely free of oil and grease before connecting them?
options: A. Grease clogs the ground clamp and reduces electrical conductivity
B. Oil makes the torch handle slippery and harder to aim
C. Pure oxygen can react violently with oil or grease and explode
D. Lubricant turns the welding arc flame from blue to yellow
choices: A. Grease clogs the ground clamp and reduces electrical conductivity
B. Oil makes the torch handle slippery and harder to aim
C. Pure oxygen can react violently with oil or grease and explode
D. Lubricant turns the welding arc flame from blue to yellow
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Pure oxygen can react violently with oil or grease and explode
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Pressurized oxygen reacts violently with hydrocarbons, so all regulators, hoses, and fittings must be tight and completely free of oil or grease to prevent fires or explosions (p. 21).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: During oxy-fuel equipment shutdown, what should you do after closing the main cylinder valves and draining the gas from each hose?
options: A. Release the adjusting screws on both gas regulators
B. Disconnect the regulators from the cylinders immediately
C. Open both torch valves simultaneously and leave them open
D. Submerge the hot torch tip in a bucket of cold water
choices: A. Release the adjusting screws on both gas regulators
B. Disconnect the regulators from the cylinders immediately
C. Open both torch valves simultaneously and leave them open
D. Submerge the hot torch tip in a bucket of cold water
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Release the adjusting screws on both gas regulators
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): After closing the cylinder valves and bleeding each line individually, you must release the adjusting screws on both the oxygen and fuel-gas regulators to relieve spring tension (p. 71).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: If your canoe, kayak, or raft capsizes in moving whitewater rapids deeper than knee height, why must you never attempt to stand up on the riverbed?
quiz_item.question: If your canoe, kayak, or raft capsizes in moving whitewater rapids deeper than knee height, why must you never attempt to stand up on the riverbed?
options: A. Standing up scares downstream paddlers into dropping their throw bags.
B. River rocks are too slippery to push your boat upstream against the current.
C. Standing upright causes your lifejacket to lose buoyancy when splashed.

D. Your foot can wedge between rocks on the riverbed while the force of the current pushes your body downstream and holds your head underwater (foot entrapment); instead, float on your back with feet up and pointed downstream.
choices: A. Standing up scares downstream paddlers into dropping their throw bags.
B. River rocks are too slippery to push your boat upstream against the current.
C. Standing upright causes your lifejacket to lose buoyancy when splashed.

D. Your foot can wedge between rocks on the riverbed while the force of the current pushes your body downstream and holds your head underwater (foot entrapment); instead, float on your back with feet up and pointed downstream.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Your foot can wedge between rocks on the riverbed while the force of the current pushes your body downstream and holds your head underwater (foot entrapment); instead, float on your back with feet up and pointed downstream.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Foot entrapment in swift current is a deadly whitewater hazard; swimmers must assume the defensive whitewater swim position on their back with feet at the surface pointed downstream to fend off rocks until reaching an eddy.

pamphlet_excerpts: Lateral Ferrying Across Current: Upstream (forward) ferries and downstream (back) ferries move you sideways across the current (p. 30).
Upstream Ferry Angle: In an upstream ferry, you face upstream and paddle forward with your bow at an angle to the current (p. 30).
Bow Direction Movement: You move across the current in the direction your bowis pointing (p. 30).
Downstream Back-Paddling Ferry: To perform a downstream ferry, you face downstream and back paddle with your stern pointed upstream at an angle to the current (p. 30).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Point Bow Toward Target: You move across the current in the direction your bowis pointing (p. 30).
Step 2 - Angle Stern Into Current: To perform a downstream ferry, you face downstream and back paddle with your stern pointed upstream at an angle to the current (p. 30).
Step 3 - Backpaddle Across the Stream: You move across the current in the direction your stern is facing (p. 30).
Step 4 - Turn Boat Facing Upstream: To perform a successful upstream ferry, begin by turning your boat until it faces upstream (p. 30).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When performing a downstream ferry across a fast current, how should you position and propel your craft?
quiz_item.question: When performing a downstream ferry across a fast current, how should you position and propel your craft?
options: A. Face upstream and paddle backward so the water pushes the bow sideways.
B. Face downstream and backpaddle with your stern angled upstream toward your target bank.
C. Position the boat perpendicular to the current and use high braces on the upstream side.
D. Point the bow directly downstream and paddle forward at twice the speed of the river.
choices: A. Face upstream and paddle backward so the water pushes the bow sideways.
B. Face downstream and backpaddle with your stern angled upstream toward your target bank.
C. Position the boat perpendicular to the current and use high braces on the upstream side.
D. Point the bow directly downstream and paddle forward at twice the speed of the river.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Face downstream and backpaddle with your stern angled upstream toward your target bank.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): To execute a downstream ferry, you face downstream and backpaddle while holding your stern at an angle to the current, moving laterally in the direction your stern points (p. 30).

pamphlet_excerpts: Backstrokes for Speed Control: Canoeists and kayakers use backstrokes to back paddle, that is, to slow or reverse the forward motion of the boat (p. 56).
Stopping in River Eddies: As you paddle downstream, you will want to stop in an eddy to rest or to scout a rapid (p. 56).
Downstream Eddy Turn Maneuver: The maneuver to enter an eddy while heading downstream is called an eddy turn (p. 56).
Exiting via Peel: Later you will learn how to exit an eddy using a peel (p. 56).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Execute Clean Eddy Turns: The maneuver to enter an eddy while heading downstream is called an eddy turn (p. 56).
Step 2 - Practice Eddy Peel Outs: Later you will learn how to exit an eddy using a peel (p. 56).
Step 3 - Master Moving Water Transitions: When you have learned how to move in and out of eddies with confidence and ease, you will have passed a major whitewater skills milestone (p. 56).
Step 4 - Control Momentum in Current: Entering an eddy while moving downstream in a boat can be challenging, especially if the current is fast (p. 56).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which maneuver does a paddler use to leave the main downstream current and come to a stop in the calm water behind an obstacle?
quiz_item.question: Which maneuver does a paddler use to leave the main downstream current and come to a stop in the calm water behind an obstacle?
options: A. An upstream ferry
B. A peel out
C. An eddy turn
D. A portage carry
choices: A. An upstream ferry
B. A peel out
C. An eddy turn
D. A portage carry
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. An eddy turn
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Entering an eddy while paddling downstream to rest or scout a rapid below is called an eddy turn, whereas exiting the eddy is called a peel out (p. 56).

requirements.description: Before doing requirements 4 through 12, earn the Canoeing merit badge if you will be using a canoe to earn this merit badge. If you will be using a kayak, earn the Kayaking merit badge. Then do ONE of the following: (a) If you will be using a canoe to earn this merit badge, demonstrate strokes and maneuvers from the Canoeing merit badge to the satisfaction of your counselor. (b) If you will be using a kayak to earn this merit badge, demonstrate strokes and maneuvers from the Kayaking merit badge to the satisfaction of your counselor.

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Option A, Tandem Canoeist. Do ALL of the following strokes and techniques on calm water: (1) Demonstrate the following strokes in the bow: cross forward, bow draw, cross bow draw, bow pry, and sculling draw. (2) Demonstrate the following strokes in the stern: stern draw, stern pry, sculling draw, and forward with stern pry. (3) Demonstrate a high brace, low brace, and righting pry. (b) Option B, Solo Canoeist. Do ALL of the following strokes and techniques on calm water: (1) Demonstrate the following strokes: cross forward, bow draw, cross bow draw, stern draw, pry, stern pry, sculling draw, and forward with stern pry. (2) Demonstrate a high brace, low brace, and righting pry. (c) Option C, Solo Kayaker. Do ALL of the following strokes and techniques on calm water: (1) Demonstrate the following strokes: bow draw, rudder, and sculling draw. (2) Demonstrate a high brace and low brace.

pamphlet_excerpts: Knee Pressure Boat Tilt: In the peel out, note how both paddlers use their left knees to lean into and tilt the boat into the turn (p. 50).
Offside Peel Out Mechanics: An offside peel out incorporates all the same features of the on side peel out except that the turning strokes are different (p. 50).
Opposite Kayak Blade Turn: For kayakers, the opposite paddle blade is used for the turning stroke (p. 50).
Solo Canoe Turning Strokes: After crossing the eddy line, solo canoeists can use a variety of turning strokes, including a forward sweep or crossbow draw (p. 50).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Engage Opposite Kayak Blade: For kayakers, the opposite paddle blade is used for the turning stroke (p. 50).
Step 2 - Apply Cross-Bow Draw: After crossing the eddy line, solo canoeists can use a variety of turning strokes, including a forward sweep or crossbow draw (p. 50).
Step 3 - Coordinate Tandem Turning Strokes: Tandem canoeists use a combination of a cross-bowdraw in the bow while the stern paddler does a low bracing reverse sweep or simply powers (p. 50).
Step 4 - Keep Paddle Shaft Vertical: The paddle shaft should be vertical and move in a path 2 to 3 feet long next to the side of the boat (p. 50).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How do tandem canoeists coordinate their strokes when executing an offside peel out across an eddy line?
quiz_item.question: How do tandem canoeists coordinate their strokes when executing an offside peel out across an eddy line?
options: A. Both paddlers switch sides simultaneously and perform reverse J-strokes.
B. The bow paddler stops paddling completely while the stern paddler rudders hard against the current.
C. Both paddlers lean toward the upstream gunwale and drag their paddles behind the stern.
D. The bow paddler uses a cross-bow draw while the stern paddler performs a low bracing reverse sweep or powers forward.
choices: A. Both paddlers switch sides simultaneously and perform reverse J-strokes.
B. The bow paddler stops paddling completely while the stern paddler rudders hard against the current.
C. Both paddlers lean toward the upstream gunwale and drag their paddles behind the stern.

quiz_item.correct_answer: D. The bow paddler uses a cross-bow draw while the stern paddler performs a low bracing reverse sweep or powers forward.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): In an offside peel out, tandem canoeists tilt the boat into the turn with their knees while the bow paddler uses a cross-bow draw and the stern paddler executes a low bracing reverse sweep or powers forward (p. 50).

Do ALL of the following strokes and techniques on calm water: (1) Demonstrate the following strokes: cross forward, bow draw, cross bow draw, stern draw, pry, stern pry, sculling draw, and forward with stern pry. pamphlet_excerpts: Six Rapid Difficulty Classes: Here are the six classifications used for the International Scale of River Difficulty (p. 34).
Class I Moving Water: Fast-moving water with riffles and small waves (p. 34).
Class II Clear Channels: Straightforward rapids with wide, clear channels (p. 34).
Maneuvering Around Medium Waves: Some maneuvering may be required, but rocks and medium-size waves are easily avoided by trained paddlers (p. 34).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Identify Wide Clear Channels: Straightforward rapids with wide, clear channels (p. 34).
Step 2 - Maneuver Around River Rocks: Some maneuvering may be required, but rocks and medium-size waves are easily avoided by trained paddlers (p. 34).
Step 3 - Recognize Class III Waves: Rapids with moderate, irregular waves that may swamp an open canoe (p. 34).
Step 4 - Prepare for Group Assistance: Some risk to swimmers; group assistance may be necessary (p. 34).

quiz_item.question: According to the International Scale of River Difficulty, which characteristics define a Class II rapid?
options: A. Flat, slow-moving water with no riffles, rocks, or obstructions.
B. Straightforward rapids with wide, clear channels where medium-size waves and rocks are easily avoided by trained paddlers.
C. Long, violent rapids with constricted passages that require expert scouting and carry high risk to swimmers.
D. Moderate, irregular waves that routinely swamp open canoes and require tight, complex maneuvers in fast current.
choices: A. Flat, slow-moving water with no riffles, rocks, or obstructions.
B. Straightforward rapids with wide, clear channels where medium-size waves and rocks are easily avoided by trained paddlers.
C. Long, violent rapids with constricted passages that require expert scouting and carry high risk to swimmers.
D. Moderate, irregular waves that routinely swamp open canoes and require tight, complex maneuvers in fast current.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Straightforward rapids with wide, clear channels where medium-size waves and rocks are easily avoided by trained paddlers.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Class II (Novice) rapids feature straightforward channels that are evident without scouting, requiring some maneuvering around rocks and medium waves that trained paddlers can easily avoid (p. 34).

pamphlet_excerpts: Downstream Left-Right Orientation: River right an driver left always refer to the right side or the left side of the river as if you were facing downstream (p. 33).
Ongoing Team Run Briefings: Teammates should discuss their run on an ongoing basis and make adjustments to any plan as needed (p. 33).
Rapids Drowning Out Speech: Even as mall riffle can muffle words, and roaring rapids often drown out speech altogether (p. 33).
Whistle and Paddle Signals: For emergencies or times when talk is difficult, river runners make use of whistles and paddle signals to communicate (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Anticipate Loud River Noise: Even as mall riffle can muffle words, and roaring rapids often drown out speech altogether (p. 33).
Step 2 - Use Visual Paddle Signals: For emergencies or times when talk is difficult, river runners make use of whistles and paddle signals to communicate (p. 33).
Step 3 - Review Signals Before Launching: Review river signals before the beginning of every trip (p. 33).
Step 4 - Return the OK Signal: To respond that you are OK to someone signaling you, return the same signal (p. 33).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why must whitewater canoes and kayaks be outfitted with extra flotation bags or foam blocks before running rapids?
quiz_item.question: Why must whitewater canoes and kayaks be outfitted with extra flotation bags or foam blocks before running rapids?
options: A. To increase the weight of the boat so strong winds cannot blow it sideways.
B. To displace water so the craft rides high and is much easier to rescue if it flips.
C. To stiffen the keel line so the boat tracks straighter across calm pools.
D. To replace the need for paddlers to wear personal flotation devices in Class I water.
choices: A. To increase the weight of the boat so strong winds cannot blow it sideways.
B. To displace water so the craft rides high and is much easier to rescue if it flips.
C. To stiffen the keel line so the boat tracks straighter across calm pools.
D. To replace the need for paddlers to wear personal flotation devices in Class I water.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. To displace water so the craft rides high and is much easier to rescue if it flips.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Extra flotation installed in a whitewater boat keeps a swamped or capsized hull riding high in the water, preventing heavy waterlogged pinning and simplifying rescues (p. 39).

pamphlet_excerpts: Pre-Launch Gear Inspection: Before you head out on the river, always double-check that you have both personal and group essentials necessary for a safe whitewater outing (p. 12).
Waterproofing Dry Essentials: Items that need to stay dry include food, spare clothing, first-aidkits, maps, sleeping bags, tents, and other camping equipment (p. 12).
Securing Gear Inside Gunwales: Use cam straps, bungee cords, and pieces of rope to secure items and equipment so they will not fall out past the gunwales if you capsize (p. 12).
Eliminating Rope Entrapment Hazards: Itis vital that your lashing does not pose an entrapment hazard (p. 12).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Lash Dry Bags Securely: Use cam straps, bungee cords, and pieces of rope to secure items and equipment so they will not fall out past the gunwales if you capsize (p. 12).
Step 2 - Tuck Loose Strap Ends: Itis vital that your lashing does not pose an entrapment hazard (p. 12).
Step 3 - Maintain Close Buddy Contact: Buddies either ride in the same boat or stay near each other in single-person craft (p. 12).
Step 4 - Verify Group Skill Proficiency: SKILL PROFICIENCY Everyone in an activity afloat must have sufficient knowledge and skill to participate safely (p. 12).

quiz_item.question: What is the most critical safety rule when using cam straps or cords to secure dry bags and equipment inside a whitewater boat?
options: A. Leave 10 feet of slack in every rope so bags can float alongside the hull after a capsize.
B. Tie every piece of gear directly to the paddler's lifejacket buckle.
C. Secure items tightly so nothing falls past the gunwales or creates a loose loop that could cause an entrapment hazard.
D. Place heavy coolers on top of the thwarts to raise the boat's center of gravity.
choices: A. Leave 10 feet of slack in every rope so bags can float alongside the hull after a capsize.
B. Tie every piece of gear directly to the paddler's lifejacket buckle.
C. Secure items tightly so nothing falls past the gunwales or creates a loose loop that could cause an entrapment hazard.
D. Place heavy coolers on top of the thwarts to raise the boat's center of gravity.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Secure items tightly so nothing falls past the gunwales or creates a loose loop that could cause an entrapment hazard.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): All equipment must be lashed snugly inside the hull using cam straps or cords so items cannot fall past the gunwales or create loose loops that could entangle a swimmer (p. 12).

requirements.lead_text: Wearing a proper lifejacket and being appropriately dressed for the weather and water conditions, perform the following skills in moving water in a properly equipped whitewater craft of your choice (tandem canoe, solo canoe, or solo kayak). requirements.req_text: Wearing a proper life jacket and being appropriately dressed for the weather and water conditions, perform the following skills in moving water in a properly equipped whitewater craft of your choice (tandem canoe, solo canoe, or solo kayak). If a tandem canoe is used, the skills must be demonstrated from both the bow and stern positions. (a) Launch and land. (b) Paddle forward in a straight line at least 10 boat lengths. (c) Backpaddle in a straight line at least five boat lengths. (d) Ferry upstream from both sides of the river. (e) Ferry downstream from both sides of the river. (f) Eddy turn from both sides of an eddy. (g) Peel out from both sides of an eddy.

common_misconception_pair.misconception: To ferry across a very fast current, you should turn your boat at a 90-degree angle perpendicular to the river flow.
common_misconception_pair.fact: Turning broadside to a strong current pushes the boat rapidly downstream and risks flipping on the upstream edge, whereas a slight angle to the current lets the water glide the hull sideways (p. 46).

pamphlet_excerpts: Sideways Current Crossing: Upstream (forward) ferries and downstream (back) ferries move you sideways across the current (p. 46).
Upstream Ferry Mechanics: In an upstream ferry, you face upstream and paddle forward with your bow at an angle to the current (p. 46).
Tracking Toward Bow Angle: You move across the current in the direction your bowis pointing (p. 46).
Downstream Ferry Mechanics: To perform a downstream ferry, you face downstream and back paddle with your stern pointed upstream at an angle to the current (p. 46).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Set Narrow Ferry Angle: You move across the current in the direction your bowis pointing (p. 46).
Step 2 - Angle Stern Toward Bank: To perform a downstream ferry, you face downstream and back paddle with your stern pointed upstream at an angle to the current (p. 46).
Step 3 - Backpaddle Steadily Across Current: You move across the current in the direction your stern is facing (p. 46).
Step 4 - Align Bow Facing Upstream: To perform a successful upstream ferry, begin by turning your boat until it faces upstream (p. 46).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What happens if you set too wide an angle to the current when attempting an upstream ferry across fast water?
quiz_item.question: What happens if you set too wide an angle to the current when attempting an upstream ferry across fast water?
options: A. The boat will shoot upstream faster than the surrounding river flow.
B. The current will catch the upstream side of the bow, spinning the boat broadside or pushing it downstream.
C. The stern will automatically lock into the nearest eddy without paddling.
D. The hull will rise onto a plane and skip over submerged rocks.
choices: A. The boat will shoot upstream faster than the surrounding river flow.
B. The current will catch the upstream side of the bow, spinning the boat broadside or pushing it downstream.
C. The stern will automatically lock into the nearest eddy without paddling.
D. The hull will rise onto a plane and skip over submerged rocks.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. The current will catch the upstream side of the bow, spinning the boat broadside or pushing it downstream.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In fast current, a narrow ferry angle is required because if your bow is angled too wide against strong flow, the water overwhelms your strokes and spins the bow downstream (p. 46).

requirements.description: Wearing a proper life jacket and being appropriately dressed for the weather and water conditions, perform the following skills in moving water in a properly equipped whitewater craft of your choice (tandem canoe, solo canoe, or solo kayak). If a tandem canoe is used, the skills must be demonstrated from both the bow and stern positions. (a) Launch and land. (b) Paddle forward in a straight line at least 10 boat lengths. (c) Backpaddle in a straight line at least five boat lengths. (d) Ferry upstream from both sides of the river. (e) Ferry downstream from both sides of the river. (f) Eddy turn from both sides of an eddy. (g) Peel out from both sides of an eddy.

pamphlet_excerpts: Floating Throw Bag Design: Using a Throw Rope to Rescue Others As you will recall, a throw rope is a floating rope that is stored in a throw bag (p. 71).
Smooth Rope Deployment: The rope will pay out neatly when the bagis tossed (p. 71).
Accessible Non-Entrapping Storage: A throw bag or a neatly coiled throw rope should always be secured in your craft so that it will be handy in a rescue situation but is not an entrapment (p. 71).
Keeping Extra Rope Contained: Allow the remainder of the rope to stay in the bag (p. 71).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Mount Throw Bag Securely: A throw bag or a neatly coiled throw rope should always be secured in your craft so that it will be handy in a rescue situation but is not an entrapment (p. 71).
Step 2 - Hold Loose Rope End: Allow the remainder of the rope to stay in the bag (p. 71).
Step 3 - Open Bag Mouth Halfway: Be sure that the mouth of the bag is only halfway open (p. 71).
Step 4 - Alert Swimmer Before Throwing: Get the attention of the person in the water by yelling, "Rope!" or giving a single blast of your whistle (p. 71).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the proper technique for a swimmer in whitewater to hold a throw rope while being pendulumed to shore?
quiz_item.question: What is the proper technique for a swimmer in whitewater to hold a throw rope while being pendulumed to shore?
options: A. Tie a bowline loop around the waist and swim headfirst toward the rescuer.
B. Wrap the rope three times around the dominant wrist and float face down.
C. Hold the rope with both hands at chest level, feed it over the shoulder opposite the shore to which you are being pulled, and float on your back with feet downstream.
D. Clip the end of the throw rope directly to the front zipper of the lifejacket.
choices: A. Tie a bowline loop around the waist and swim headfirst toward the rescuer.
B. Wrap the rope three times around the dominant wrist and float face down.
C. Hold the rope with both hands at chest level, feed it over the shoulder opposite the shore to which you are being pulled, and float on your back with feet downstream.
D. Clip the end of the throw rope directly to the front zipper of the lifejacket.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Hold the rope with both hands at chest level, feed it over the shoulder opposite the shore to which you are being pulled, and float on your back with feet downstream.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A swimmer receiving a throw rope should never wrap or tie the line around their body, and instead should float on their back holding the rope over the shoulder opposite the rescuer so the current swings them to shore without pulling their face underwater (p. 72).

requirements.lead_text: Participate in one or more whitewater trips using either a canoe or kayak on a Class I and/or Class II river. The trip(s) must involve at least six hours of paddling time. For each trip:
requirements.req_text: Participate in one or more whitewater trips using either a canoe or kayak on a Class I and/or Class II river. The trip(s) must involve at least six hours of paddling time. For each trip: (a) Help to prepare a written plan, specifying the route (put-ins and takeouts), schedule, equipment, safety precautions, and emergency procedures. (b) Determine local rules and obtain permission from landowners and land managers in advance. (c) Explain what steps have been taken to comply with Scouting America Safety Afloat and the American Whitewater safety guidelines. (d) Show how to protect personal and group equipment from water and how to load and secure the containers in boats to be used in the trip. Execute the plans with other paddlers. (e) Explain to your counselor how well your plans worked for each trip taken.
